title: Ministry and Marriage: How to Be a Healthy Team
summary: Marriages with one or both spouses employed in ministry face unique pressures, challenges, and opportunities.
summary_zh: 配偶一方或双方受雇于事工的婚姻面临着独特的压力、挑战和机遇。
title_zh: 事工与婚姻：如何成为一个健康的团队
content: Marriages with one or both spouses employed in ministry face unique pressures, challenges, and opportunities. Over the years, we change, our ministries change, and the pressures on us change. How can we navigate these changes in a way that draws us closer to each other instead of driving us apart? In this discussion, recorded at TGC25, Michael and Lucy Aitcheson talk with Jim and Angela Davis about their experiences of seeking to keep their marriage healthy while ministering faithfully. title: ‘Mosquito Bowl’: Football Stars on the Front Lines
summary: Peter Berg’s ‘The Mosquito Bowl’ is essentially ‘Friday Night Lights’ meets ‘Hacksaw Ridge.’
summary_zh: Peter Berg的“The Mosquito Bowl”本质上是“周五夜灯”与“Hacksaw Ridge”相遇。
title_zh: “蚊子碗” ：前线的足球明星
content: Peter Berg’s The Mosquito Bowl is essentially Friday Night Lights meets Hacksaw Ridge . It’s a movie with the same creative vibe as Friday Night Lights (gritty handheld camera, muted color palette, Explosions in the Sky post-rock soundtrack) but applied to a brutally violent true story of WWII’s Battle of Okinawa, one of the single bloodiest battles of the 20th century. Also like Berg’s Friday Night Lights , The Mosquito Bowl ( out now in theaters ; coming to Netflix November 25) is based on a book by Pulitzer Prize–winning journalist Buzz Bissinger . The 2022 book—subtitled A Game of Life and Death in World War II —only has one chapter (of 41) devoted to the actual 1944 football game dubbed “The Mosquito Bowl.” Most of the book is about the war, and the young men who left wives, kids, and promising NFL careers to fight it. Likewise, Berg’s film adaptation is mostly a somber, unflinching WWII film, with a brief reprieve of joy in the form of a football game on Guadalcanal between the 4th and 29th regiments of the 6th Marine Division. Just as in Friday Night Lights , where the drama of high school football parallels the struggles and triumphs of life off the field, the football game in The Mosquito Bowl parallels the “game of life and death” that surrounds the men at war. Sports are interesting in this way: They provide escape from real life but also training for it, an arena of danger and high stakes but not ultimate stakes. Sports often map onto life—we draw up plans and plays but have to improvise; we get hurt but can heal; we thrive individually through teamwork; sometimes we win and sometimes we lose. Yet sports are unlike real life too. Winning or losing on the field is a matter of trophies and glory, but off the field, it can be a matter of life and death. Young Men Willing to Fight and Die The Mosquito Bowl (rated R for graphic war violence and language), opens with a well-known epigraph from Herbert Hoover : Older men declare war. But it is youth that must fight and die. And it is youth who must inherit the tribulation, the sorrow, and the triumphs that are the aftermath of war. This is a movie about youth—or rather, the passage from youth into adulthood that war accelerates. This is a movie about youth—or rather, the passage from youth into adulthood that war accelerates. The movie opens with muddy college football scenes in the fall of 1941, as the four central characters are introduced: John McLaughry (Nicholas Galitzine), Brown quarterback; Bob Baumann (Bill Skarsgård), University of Wisconsin tackle; Tony Butkovich (Ray Nicholson), Purdue fullback; and Dave Schreiner (Tom Francis), Wisconsin end. They were all-star athletes with promising futures. Many of them were collegiate All-Americans and drafted by NFL teams. Yet December 7, 1941, happened, and their futures were all changed. Once bound together by football skill, friendly rivalry, and fierce competition on the gridiron, these men soon bonded in a different setting: as marines in WWII’s savage Pacific theater. Instead of fighting for yards on the field, they fought for ground in a war of attrition on Okinawa. Instead of a football in hand, they carried guns and bayonets. Instead of tackling their opponents, they wrestled them to the death in hand-to-hand combat. Like many in the Greatest Generation, these men volunteered to enlist and fight. The Mosquito Bowl celebrates their duty and sacrifice. In one scene, Baumann’s younger brother says, “You don’t have to go,” to which Baumann replies, “I do. I’m needed.” It’s hard to imagine star athletes, whether collegiate or professional, volunteering to go to war in 2026. But in 1943, it was normal. Okinawa, Bissinger writes in the book, was “by far the largest collection of athletes ever to die in a single battle.” And in the entirety of WWII, 21 NFL players died in combat, as well as two players from Major League Baseball. Bissinger在书中写道,冲绳是“迄今为止在一次战斗中死亡的运动员人数最多的集合地”。 而在整个二战中,有21名NFL球员在战斗中丧生,还有来自主力联赛棒球的两名球员. 为什么他们这么愿意牺牲自己的生命? 也许那时,男人有更大的鸡尾酒

title: Pastor, Be Opportunistic
summary: Pastor, you cannot afford to coast. You cannot afford autopilot. Be a gospel entrepreneur. Eternity is at stake.
summary_zh: 牧师，您负担不起海岸。您买不起自动驾驶仪。成为一名福音企业家。永恒岌岌可危。
title_zh: 牧师，抓住机会
content: My coffee had gone cold as the church planter mourned that his church felt stagnant. Worse than not growing—a thick malaise had settled over the congregation. The first three years were exciting; the community was intrigued by a new church plant, genuinely curious about what it was all about. But everything had plateaued. Leaders grew complacent. Sundays—even with strong preaching—felt cold and passionless. The church’s reason for existing had shrunk to feeding and caring for the Christians who already called it home. The church planter couldn’t see how it was still transforming the community. An older mentor at the table cleared his throat. “I’m sorry to hear that. Let me ask you—what is one risky, hard thing the Lord is inviting your church to do that you’re hesitant to do?” The planter scratched his head. “I don’t know. I’ve never been asked that before.” The older man shrugged. “Every pastor should be ready to answer that question. If he can’t, he needs to spend some time praying and fasting until he can. Comfort and complacency are incredibly dangerous.” I’ve sat in enough of these conversations to know that wise, healthy risks are vital to the life of the church. Without them, the church atrophies. Its reason for existing collapses into self-care and, after a few years, into self-preservation. Risky and hard things keep gospel blood flowing through the body. Pastor, you cannot afford to coast. You cannot afford autopilot. You owe it to Jesus and to your church to make the most of opportunities in your city—which means that alongside preaching, teaching, praying, and developing leaders, you need to prioritize seeking new avenues for ministry. Be a gospel entrepreneur. Church-planting networks have long understood that entrepreneurial aptitude is essential for planters. But what about established churches—do their pastors need to be entrepreneurial too? What Is a Gospel Entrepreneur? There’s still hesitancy around saying pastors need entrepreneurial aptitude. Maybe it’s because we picture someone who constantly starts new things he can’t sustain—a person with a billion ideas who follows through on none of them. If this is what we mean, then no, we don’t want our pastors to be entrepreneurial. Comfort and complacency are incredibly dangerous. But a gospel entrepreneur is something different. He doesn’t pile up harebrained ideas. He stays awake and sober-minded about the opportunities the Lord is opening in the community. He sees the wooden frames of a new development and prays about how the gospel will reach those families once they move in. He looks at neighborhoods where existing churches can’t possibly reach everyone—and plants a church there. He saves, scrimps, and sacrifices to move a growing church plant into a more strategic location. He keeps his eyes open, his mind sharp, and his hands ready for the moment God opens a door. Biblical Call When this topic comes up, someone usually asks, “Where do you see the need for a pastor to be an entrepreneur in the Bible?” My answer often surprises people: Jesus’s parable of the dishonest manager. In Luke 16:1–9, a rich man discovers his property manager has been wasting his possessions and tells him to settle accounts—he’s about to be fired. The manager realizes losing his job means either digging or begging, so he immediately goes to work cutting deals to gain favor with other wealthy employers. When his employer finds out, he commends the manager for his shrewdness. Ethical or not, it was a genius move. At this point, we should ask, Why is Jesus telling this story? Maybe he’s about to indict people like the manager. But the manager’s dishonesty has nothing to do with Jesus’s point. The twist is that Jesus holds up the dishonest manager as an example of what he wants his disciples to be. “The master commended the dishonest manager for his shrewdness,” Jesus says. “For the sons of this world are more shrewd in dealing with their own generation than the sons of light” (Luke 16:

title: The Dangers of Getting Advice from the Internet
summary: Melissa and Courtney discuss how to cultivate discernment when seeking advice online and recognize the danger of letting AI or influencers replace wise counsel from the body of Christ.
summary_zh: Melissa和Courtney讨论了如何在网上寻求建议时培养洞察力，并认识到让人工智能或影响者取代基督身体的明智建议的危险。
title_zh: 从互联网上获取建议的危险
content: Melissa and Courtney discuss how to cultivate discernment when seeking advice. They talk about how sometimes we think we need information when what we really need is relationship. They discuss what kind of advice they like to get from the internet or ChatGPT, why they don’t recommend it for wisdom issues such as marriage and parenting, and why we shouldn’t let advice from AI or influencers replace wise counsel from the body of Christ. Resource Mentioned: Kitchen-Table Counseling Within Your Local Church Related Resources: Let’s Talk: Finding a Mentor and Being a Mentor Want to Grow in Wisdom? You Need Gospel Friends. Why AI Parenting Advice Falls Short Don’t Treat AI as Your Pastor Discussion Questions: 1. When you face a difficult decision or struggle, where do you typically turn for advice? 2. How do you discern whether online advice is helpful or unwise? 3. What makes advice offered within a personal relationship different from advice taken from an online blog or influencer or generated by AI? 4. How might repeated exposure to ideas about marriage, parenting, or relationships on social media influence our thinking without us being aware of it? 5. What do we lose when we turn to online sources for counsel instead of investing in relationships with people who know and love us? 6. Who in your life knows you well enough to speak honestly into your decisions and loves you enough to do so? How can you cultivate those kinds of relationships? 7. How would you like to grow in your ability to offer wise counsel to others?

title: Beware Making Mental Illness an Identity
summary: ‘All in Your Head’ is a concrete and compelling remapping of mental health culture with impressive explanatory power.
summary_zh: “All in Your Head”是对心理健康文化的具体而引人注目的重新映射，具有令人印象深刻的解释力。
title_zh: 小心让精神疾病成为一种身份
content: In the years since he was involuntarily committed to a mental health institution for bipolar disorder, Frederik deBoer has wrestled with both profound gratitude for a system that saved his life and also palpable frustration that his experience of healing has become so rare. All in Your Head: Illness as Identity, Trauma as Fashion, and the Desire to Be Disordered is the latest broadside from one of the internet’s most heterodox thinkers and writers. As an “old school” Marxist best known for writing The Cult of Smart , deBoer takes aim at how the cultural drift within his own tribe is responsible for making mental health care so elusive for those who need it most: “The tendency to treat mental illness as an exciting adventure, the endless romanticization of lunacy in popular culture, is one of many aggravations I have nursed for years” (8). The root of his aggravation—the treatment of mental illness and disability as an identity to be celebrated rather than a disability that needs treatment —isn’t all in his head. The use of talk therapy rose 47 percent between 2019 and 2024 . A 2025 LifeStance survey found around 29 percent of U.S. adults have self-diagnosed their mental health condition after consuming online content, rising to 50 percent among Gen Z (versus 9 percent of boomers). Of the people who self-diagnose symptoms, almost a quarter (24 percent) “rarely” or “never” feel the need to take the next step to discuss them with a qualified clinician. DeBoer argues that rather than reducing the stigma surrounding mental illness, the inordinate attention given to the mildly and dubiously afflicted is a dangerous distraction crowding out help for the severely ill. Accelerated by social media, this “gentrification of disability” has become a full-blown social contagion, compromising even the experts and institutions responsible for mental health care (153–54). DeBoer is largely right, and the cultural shift he identifies has real-world implications both inside and outside the church. But the same ideological priors that so sharpen deBoer’s critique also suffer from two significant blind spots that, were they addressed, would make All in Your Head the more courageous, more constructive, and, therefore, more widely read manifesto we need. General Bipartisan Ire If you picked up All in Your Head to understand how modern therapy culture spread like wildfire across social media over the last several years, it’s not immediately obvious why deBoer starts his argument with an in-depth analysis of the anti-psychiatry movement’s influence in late 20th century politics and academia. But, if you can forgive me the pun, there’s a method to his madness. After a blistering critique of “rightwing libertarian” policies that neglected mental illness, he cashes in on the subsequent trust he earns with left-leaning readers to launch a series of absolute haymakers toward “a species of thought that sometimes amounts to a kind of leftist pseudo-radicalism or a libertarian fantasy” (198) that drives the “destabilizing . . . move from mental illness as reality to mental illness as symbol” (8). American individualism and anti-institutional bias aren’t new, but the painstakingly specific way deBoer traces their spread through the culture surrounding mental health and therapy is refreshing and instructive. Our “apolitical romanticism of resistance to modern society” fuels two opposite errors: On the right, mental illness is sometimes seen as either imagined or a symptom of weak character. But on the left, the same romanticism often describes mental disability as more en abling than dis abling, as if neurodivergent minorities don’t need society’s help—society needs theirs. Gentrification of Disability DeBoer’s emphatic rejection of this predominantly progressive error— of “making a medical disorder an identity”—is the “overarching principle of [his] book” (165). This is never more clear in what he labels “the gentrification of disability,” where “diagnoses bec
content_zh: 在他非自愿地被送入精神病院治疗两极分化后的几年里,弗雷德里克·德·博尔带着对挽救他生命的系统深表感谢和明显的沮丧,因为他的治愈经验变得如此罕见. 在你的脑海中:作为身份的疾病,作为时尚的创伤,以及希望陷入混乱,是互联网上最异形的思想家和作家之一的最新一面。 作为一位最以写作"聪明的邪教"而出名的"老派"马克思主义者,德博尔以自己的部落内部的文化漂移为目的,让那些最需要的人如此难以接受精神保健:"将精神疾病视为激动人心的冒险的倾向,在流行文化中无休止地浪漫化的放荡,是多年来我所照顾的诸多恶化之一"(8). 他的病情恶化的根源——将精神疾病和残疾视为一种值得庆贺的身份,而不是需要治疗的残疾——并不是他脑子里所有的东西。 2019年至2024年间,谈话疗法的使用率上升了47%. 2025年生活稳定调查发现,约29%的美国成年人在消费了在线内容后自行诊断出自己的心理健康状况,在Gen Z中上升到了50%(相对于9%的繁荣者). 在自我诊断的人群中,近四分之一(24%)的人“勉强”或“从未”感到有必要采取下一步措施,与合格的临床医生讨论这些症状。 DeBoer认为,对受轻度和可疑折磨的人的过度关注,与其减少精神疾病的污名化,不如说是一种危险的分心,挤出对重病患者的帮助。 社交媒体加速了这种 " 残疾意识化 " ,已成为一种全面的社会传染,甚至损害负责精神保健的专家和机构(153-54)。 DeBoer基本上是正确的,他所认定的文化转变在教堂内外都具有现实世界的影响. 但德布尔批评如此尖锐的意识形态前科也遭遇了两个重大盲点,如果这些盲点得到解决,将使你的头脑更加勇敢,更具建设性,因此,我们需要更广泛地阅读宣言。 一般两党爱尔兰人 如果你在脑海中看到现代治疗文化在过去几年里如何像野火一样在社交媒体上传播,那么DeBoer为什么以深入分析20世纪后期反精神病运动在政治和学术界的影响为出发点,这并不明显。 但是,如果你能原谅我的双关语,他疯狂是有办法的。 在对忽视了精神疾病的“右翼自由派”政策猛烈批评后,他依靠后来与左翼读者获得的信任,发动了一系列绝对的干草人,走向“有时相当于一种左翼伪激进主义或自由派幻想的思想”(198年),这种思想驱使“从精神疾病变成现实,转变为精神疾病作为象征”(8)。 美国的个人主义和反机构偏见并非新事物, 但DeBoer通过精神卫生与治疗的文化, 我们“反对现代社会的政治浪漫主义”助长了两个相反的错误: 在右边,精神疾病有时被视为一种想象或一种弱性症状. 但是在左边,同样的浪漫主义常常将精神残疾描述为比分身更困难,仿佛神经分身的少数民族不需要社会的帮助——社会需要他们的帮助。 对DeBoer残疾人的强烈反对,即 " 使医疗障碍成为身份 " 这一主要进步的错误,是 " 书中的首要原则 " (165)。 这在他所称的“残疾的基因化”中再清楚不过了。

title: How a Former Prisoner in Iran Wants You to Pray for Christians in Chains
summary: Pray not only for what God might do for Christian prisoners in Iran but for what God might do through them, for his glory.
summary_zh: 不仅祈求神可以为伊朗的基督徒囚犯做些什么，而且祈求神可以通过他们为祂的荣耀做些什么。
title_zh: 伊朗前囚犯如何希望你为被锁的基督徒祈祷
content: Not long ago, I had a surreal phone call with two young Christian men serving prison sentences in one of Iran’s hardest prisons. They’re there because they refuse to stop preaching about Jesus. When I asked how I could pray for them, their answer wasn’t what you might expect. “Pray that we would not be released until our job here is finished,” they said. They had led numerous fellow prisoners to faith. Now, their chief concern was to remain inside long enough to disciple them. The call took me straight back to the five years I spent in prison for my faith. Now, these dear brothers (let’s call them Vahid and Reza) were behind bars, and I was outside. As we spoke, I pictured the wards and corridors, imagined the sounds and smells, and remembered how hard it was not to know how many years I would be there. But it was also an encouraging call. Vahid and Reza were in high spirits, talking about Bible passages that were sustaining them and how the Lord was at work. They didn’t see themselves in a miserable, dark place. They saw themselves in a different mission field. Their focus was the same as Paul’s in Colossians 4:3: “Pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, to declare the mystery of Christ, on account of which I am in prison.” Paul’s request wasn’t for an open prison door but for an open door for the gospel. Pray for Gospel Fruit Vahid and Reza’s request resonated with me. I remember being unable to pray for my own release. I tried on a few occasions, but I couldn’t open my mouth to ask the Lord to release me. If I’m following Christ, I cannot choose the path. I cannot choose the location. I should follow him wherever he goes. And as I followed him to prison, he brought beautiful fruit. They didn’t see themselves in a miserable, dark place. They saw themselves in a different mission field. I think of one prisoner, a devout Muslim, who was wrongly accused of spying for Iran’s enemies. He was praying he would be released and was frustrated to get no answer. He approached me one day, saying, “Farshid, our God is dead. But I’ve heard yours is alive. Will you pray for me?” Fearing it might be a trap, I took him quietly aside and prayed briefly in the name of Jesus: “Lord, you know this man. Please hear his prayer.” The very next day, the man rushed over excitedly and gave me a huge hug. That morning, he had learned his name had been cleared. He was released two weeks later. Our God is indeed alive. The Lord was also at work softening my parents’ hearts toward Christ during those years. I always say that even if only for the salvation of my parents, my time in prison was worth it. So, when you pray for persecuted believers, pray not only for what God might do for them but—as Vahid and Reza requested—for what God might do through them, for his glory. Pray for gospel fruit. Pray for Comfort and Endurance I don’t want to make prison sound easier than it was. The suffering was real. So pray also for comfort and endurance. They beat me; they broke my toe. But the prolonged separation from my two children was the hardest burden to bear. The day I went to prison, my son was 2 years old and my daughter was 7. Missing their childhoods was an unspeakable loss. Yet I know others who have suffered much more than I did. I think of a brother currently in prison who has been tortured. I think of a sister who was sexually assaulted when she was arrested. Even the apostle Paul was at times “so utterly burdened beyond [his] strength that [he] despaired of life itself.” And his request to the church was simple: “You also must help us by prayer” (2 Cor. 1:8, 11). Brothers and sisters like these need us to pray for them with love. Whatever the situation, we can pray that God would grant the suffering believer comfort, peace, and endurance. title: Best Practices from Evangelistically Effective Churches
summary: While thousands of Americans are dechurching, some churches are baptizing many new members. Here’s how the country’s most evangelistically effective churches are sharing the gospel.
summary_zh: 虽然成千上万的美国人正在脱离教会，但一些教会正在为许多新成员施洗。以下是这个国家最有效传福音的教会分享福音的方式。

content: https://media.thegospelcoalition.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/23102213/effective-evangelism.mp3 In the summer of 2021, pastor Luke Peterson moved to Columbus, Ohio, to look for lost people. To find them, he joined a gym. He started building friendships. And then he began asking those friends if they wanted to come over. “Word started getting around—‘You’re not going to believe this, but Luke’s a pastor,’” he said. ‘It created some intrigue, and people started coming. I used to have a note in my phone of how many people came to our church because I went to CrossFit Grandview. It was up to like 60 or 70 before I stopped counting because it was impossible.” Peterson’s good at evangelism, and his church is too—last year, they welcomed around 500 first-time visitors. When he preaches, he knows about half his audience is probably unchurched. Pastor Luke Peterson (right) chats with Capital Church attendees / Courtesy of Capital Church Facebook This is unusual in a country where 40 million adults have stopped attending church over the last 30 years, and where 76 percent of pastors said “fostering connections with unchurched people” is a need in their church. Much has changed since the Billy Graham rallies of the ’60s, the door-knocking of the ’80s, and seeker-sensitive church billboards of the ’90s. In the past, “you could randomly walk up to the person pumping gas next to you and say, ‘Do you know Jesus?’” said Perimeter Church pastor Jeff Norris. “Could that still work? Sure. But more and more, we tell people to invite neighbors into their home. The reality is that evangelism is much slower, and more relational, than it used to be.” Today, people aren’t as likely to read the Bible, think it’s the Word of God, or go to church . But they’re also less hostile to Christianity than they were five years ago. And while they read the Bible less—especially in Gen Z—the trajectory is moving up . “We’re not past ‘my truth, your truth,’” said Rob Warren, pastor of Doxa Church in Madison, Wisconsin. “But people aren’t as sure that their truth is actually true.” These days, evangelistically effective churches are keeping evangelism front of mind in the way they preach, train, and encourage their congregations. They’re celebrating small wins. And they’re leading with a high view of Scripture, prayer, and God’s sovereignty. “We’ve seen all of our ministries grow—from kids to youth to college ministry to Doxa Church as a whole,” Warren said. “It’s not just one demographic of people who are getting saved. God’s doing something.” Times Have Changed Thirty years ago, evangelical churches leaned on programs like Evangelism Explosion or Continuous Witness Training to deliver evangelistic focus and training, church leader Thom Rainer said . Those structured initiatives fit well in a culture that was more Christian and more institutionalized—it took an average of 20 church members to reach one person for Christ per year. Today, it takes 50, Rainer said . “Evangelism efficacy, evangelism effectiveness, has definitely diminished.” That trend is likely to continue. As social media and AI fill our time and increase our social anxiety, even relational evangelism is growing more difficult. title: We Need to Know Our Reformed Roots
summary: This volume is an invitation to rediscover that heritage and to find fresh encouragement in the faithfulness of God, who has sustained his church through the centuries.
summary_zh: 这本书邀请我们重新发现这一遗产，并在神的信实中找到新的鼓励，神几个世纪以来一直支持他的教会。
title_zh: 我们需要了解我们的改革根源
content: What does it mean to be Reformed? The label is used frequently but not always carefully. For some, it simply refers to a particular view of salvation. For others, it evokes a tradition, a culture, or even an aesthetic. Yet historically, to be Reformed has meant something much richer. While no single sentence can capture the fullness of the Reformed tradition, at minimum it means three things: to be biblical, to be covenantal, and to be confessional. The authority of Scripture governs our theology, covenant theology provides Scripture’s redemptive framework, and the historic confessions summarize and safeguard the church’s doctrinal convictions. Remove any one of those pillars, and something essential to the Reformed tradition is lost. With “Reformed” in its name, it’s hardly surprising that Reformed Theological Seminary has long sought to equip pastors and church members in all three areas. In recent years, members of its faculty have produced substantial volumes on the Old and New Testaments and on covenant theology. Now, with The Westminster Confession of Faith: A Comprehensive Commentary on Its History, Theology, and Application , they turn their attention to the confessional foundation of the Reformed tradition. The result is a volume that seeks not only to explain what the confession teaches but also to demonstrate why confessional theology remains vital for the church today. What Is the Westminster Confession of Faith? The Westminster Confession of Faith takes its name from the Westminster Assembly, a gathering of more than 100 ministers and theologians convened by the English Parliament in 1643 at a time of profound political and ecclesiastical upheaval. The assembly was tasked with recommending reforms to the doctrine, worship, government, and discipline of the Church of England. After more than five years of careful biblical study and theological deliberation, the assembly produced the Westminster Confession of Faith along with the Larger and Shorter Catechisms. Together, these documents have served as the doctrinal foundation of Presbyterian churches throughout the world for nearly four centuries. The assembly’s influence, however, extends far beyond Presbyterianism. The confession has helped shape the broader Reformed tradition, providing the framework for later confessional statements. As a result, its theological influence shaped generations of Congregationalists, Baptists, and other evangelical Christians. The editors of this volume rightly observe, The confession is also ecumenical because it found wide acceptance among Congregationalists and Particular Baptists in the seventeenth century, as two different groups of theologians adapted the confession according to their theological convictions, producing the Savoy Declaration (1658) and the Second London Confession (1689). Thus the Westminster Confession is relevant to Presbyterians, Congregationalists, and Baptists. (xx) Why Another Commentary? The Westminster Confession has never lacked commentators. From the 17th century onward, pastors and theologians have written to explain its theology. Quality works by A. A. Hodge , G. I. Williamson, R. C. Sproul, and more recently Chad Van Dixhoorn have each served the church well in different ways. So why do we need another commentary on the confession, and what makes this one useful? The Westminster Confession has helped shape the broader Reformed tradition, providing the framework for later confessional statements. First, this isn’t the work of a single author but a collaborative effort by scholars whose expertise spans several areas of theology. That breadth allows the volume to approach the confession from different perspectives while maintaining a clear unity of purpose. Each contributor brings particular expertise to the section he addresses, but the volume as a whole is concerned with helping readers understand the confession and its significance for the church. Second, the commentary is consciously pastoral. Rath
content_zh: 改革意味着什么? 标签经常使用,但并不总是谨慎。 对某些人来说,它只是提到救赎的特定观点. 对其他人来说,它引起一种传统、一种文化,甚至一种美学。 然而,从历史上看,改革意味着更加富有的东西。 虽然没有一句话能捕捉到被改造后的传统的全部,但至少它意味着三件事:是圣经,是盟约,是忏悔. 圣经的权威支配着我们的神学,盟约神学提供了圣经的红发框架,历史的忏悔总结并捍卫了教会的教义信念。 移除其中任何一根支柱,失去对改革后的传统至关重要的东西。 改革神学院长期试图在所有三个领域为牧师和教会成员提供教具, 近年来,该校院士编写了大量关于"旧约"和"新约"和"盟约神学"等著作. 现在,随着《威斯敏斯特信仰的忏悔:对其历史、神学和适用的综合评论》,他们把注意力转向改革后传统的忏悔基础。 结果的一卷不仅试图解释忏悔的教义,还试图表明为什么忏悔神学在今天仍然对教会至关重要. 韦斯敏斯特对信仰的忏悔是什么? 威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔会取而代之的是威斯敏斯特大会(Westminster Assembly),这是1643年英国议会在政治与教会剧变深刻的时期召开的由100多位部长和神学家组成的集会. 大会的任务是建议对英格兰教会的学说,崇拜,政府和纪律进行改革. 经过五年多的认真的圣经研究和神学审议后,大会产生了"威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔"(Westminster Confession of Faith)和"更大规模和更短的卡特克主义". 近四个世纪以来,这些文件共同成为全世界长老会教会的理论基础。 然而,议会的影响远远超出长老会。 忏悔有助于形成更广泛的改革后传统,为后来的忏悔声明提供了框架。 因此,它的神学影响塑造了几代基督教会,浸信会等福音派基督徒. 这本书的编辑们正确地指出,《忏悔书》也具有普世性,因为它在17世纪被基督教会和特定浸信会广泛接受,因为两个不同的神学家群体根据他们的神学信念修改了供词,产生了"萨伏依宣言"(1658年)和"第二次伦敦忏悔书"(1689年). 因此,威斯敏斯特忏悔与长老会、基督教会和浸信会有关。 (二十) 为什么另作一评注? 威斯敏斯特的"忏悔"从未缺少评论家. 从17世纪起,牧师和神学家都撰文解释其神学. A. A. Hodge、G. I. Williamson、R. C. Sproul和最近的Chad Van Dixhoorn以不同方式为教堂服务。 因此,我们为什么需要关于供词的另一条评论,是什么使得这一条有用呢? 威斯敏斯特忏悔有助于形成更广泛的改革后传统,为后来的忏悔声明提供了框架. 首先,这不是一位作者的工作,而是学者的合作努力,他们的专业知识跨越了神学的几个领域。 这种宽度允许量从不同的角度对待供词,同时保持明确的目的一致。 每个贡献者都会为他所讲的一节带来特殊的专门知识,但该卷整体关注的是帮助读者理解忏悔及其对教会的意义. 第二,评注是自觉的放肆。 拉斯语Name

title: If the Church Did Its Job, Would the Parachurch Exist?
summary: Do pregnancy centers, food pantries, or campus ministries exist because the church is failing to do her work?
summary_zh: 是否存在怀孕中心、食品储藏室或校园事工，因为教会未能完成她的工作？
title_zh: 如果教会做了它的工作，教堂会存在吗？
content: I’ve heard it said more than once: “If the church did its job, the parachurch wouldn’t have to exist.” For instance, I was consulting with a local pastor who wanted to see the church serve people in poverty in his community. It was important to him that the church do it, not a nonprofit. Since he understood that God’s kingdom is bigger than his congregation, he wanted to engage multiple churches in the project. I suggested he consider forming a council of pastors and collectively hiring a staff member to manage the operations of the combined program. He thought that could work well for his context. I’m not sure he was aware of the irony. I certainly was: We’d just reinvented a variant of the 501(c)(3) nonprofit that he so keenly wanted to avoid in the first place. While the allergy to faith-based nonprofits was especially strong in his case, many people accept the premise at a basic level. In my experience, this sentiment is just as likely to come from someone who works in nonchurch ministry as from a pastor. If we understand the church is the core institution created by Christ to advance the kingdom of heaven, has it failed so badly that we need an army of auxiliaries to prop it up? Clarifying Terms and Roles I answer that the parachurch doesn’t exist because the church has failed. It exists because God’s commands naturally generate institutions beyond family, church, and state. Proving that starts with clarifying terms. The parachurch exists because God’s commands naturally generate institutions beyond family, church, and state. “Church” has more than one use in Scripture. In some contexts, it describes the people of God universally (Matt. 16:15–18; Eph. 1:22–23; Col. 1:18). In others, it’s a local congregational institution with the parameters God has placed around its operation (1 Thess. 1:1; 1 Tim. 3:1–5; Philem. 1:2; James 5:14). “Parachurch” typically refers to faith-based nonprofits who serve people in need or provide evangelistic and discipleship resources. Certainly, as part of the universal church, all God’s people hold equal status in advancing God’s mission, whether they labor as nurses, students, pastors, or tentmakers (see Acts 18:1–3). Just as surely, all God’s people shouldn’t merely attend but be accountable to a local congregation that enables their spiritual formation. When not assembled, God’s people are charged with many tasks—everything from stewarding creation to seeking justice for the oppressed. We can fulfill these tasks as individuals, but it often makes sense to create or join institutions dedicated to fulfilling them. Which brings us to a crucial point: God ordained some institutions specifically, and some emerged organically from God’s commands. Ordained or Emergent Institutions The family, the local church, and the government are ordained institutions. The Bible gives each ordained institution some guidance but also leaves a lot open to interpretation. While these ordained institutions are necessary for all people, they aren’t sufficient to fulfill God’s myriad commands to their fullest extent. Thus, some institutions emerge from the commands, rather than from a revealed institutional structure: The command to work led to the formation of businesses. The command to pass knowledge to subsequent generations led to the formation of schools. The command to care for the sick caused Christians to form the first hospitals. The command to care for the poor, widows, orphans, and strangers led to the formation of charities . The command to make disciples of all nations led to mission boards, publishing houses, and Bible-translation ministries. This ordained-emergent distinction parallels Abraham Kuyper’s “ sphere sovereignty ” in its recognition of institutions not explicitly outlined in Scripture. Many of these commands can be fulfilled to some lesser degree by the ordained institutions, but there are limitations. A family may work without forming a business, but they’ll never raise a skyscraper. Most be
content_zh: 我听到它不止一次地说 : “ 如果教会完成了它的工作, 例如,我在咨询一位当地牧师,他希望看到教堂为他所在社区的穷人服务。 对他来说重要的是,教会必须这样做,而不是非营利组织。 由于他知道上帝的王国比他的会众还大,他想让多个教会参与这个项目. 我建议他考虑成立一个牧师理事会,并集体雇用一名工作人员来管理合并方案的运作。 他认为这对他的背景来说是可行的。 我不确定他是否意识到讽刺。 我当然是:我们刚刚重新发明了501(c)(3)非营利的变体,他一开始非常想避免它。 虽然在他的案件中对基于信仰的非营利组织特别过敏,但许多人在基本层面上接受了这一前提。 根据我的经验,这种情绪可能来自在非教会部工作的人和牧师。 如果我们理解教会是基督为推进"天国"而建立的核心机构,那么它是否如此地失败了,以至于我们需要一支辅军来支撑它? 我回答说教区并不存在, 它的存在是因为上帝的命令自然产生超越家庭、教会和国家的体制。 证明从澄清条款开始。 教区之所以存在,是因为上帝的命令自然会产生超越家庭、教会和国家的体制。 “教会”在《圣经》中有不止一种用途。 在某些情况下,它普遍描述了上帝的人民(Matt. 16:15–18;Eph. 1:22–23;Col. 1:18)。 在其他情况下,它是一个具有上帝设定参数的地方教会机构,围绕它的运作(1 Thess. 1:1; 1 Tim. 3: 1–5; Philem. 1:2; James 5:14). “教会”一般是指为有需要的人服务或提供福音和门徒资源的基于信仰的非营利组织。 当然,作为普世教会的一部分,所有上帝的人民在推进上帝的使命方面都具有同等的地位,无论是作为护士、学生、牧师还是帐篷匠(见第18:1至3号法案)。 诚然,所有上帝的信徒不应该只参加,而应该对能够形成精神的当地教会负责。 在没有集合的时候,真主的宗族将担负许多任务,从管理创造到为被压迫者寻求正义。 我们可以作为个人完成这些任务,但建立或加入专门履行这些任务的机构往往是合理的。 这让我们到了一个关键点:真主专门规定一些制度,有些制度是从真主的命令中有机地出现的。 组织或应急机构 家庭、地方教会和政府是法定机构。 《圣经》为每个指定机构提供了一些指导,但也为解释留下了很大余地。 尽管这些指定机构对所有人来说都是必要的,但它们不足以最充分地执行上帝的众多命令。 因此,有些机构产生于指挥部,而不是一个公开的体制结构: 工作指挥导致了企业的形成. 将知识传给后人的命令导致了学校的形成. 照顾病人的命令使得基督徒组成了第一批医院. 照顾穷人、寡妇、孤儿和陌生人的命令导致了慈善机构的成立。 使各国门徒的指挥导致了传教板,出版社,和圣经翻译部. 这一规定性的区别与亚伯拉罕·库伊珀的 " 领域主权 " 相似,因为它承认了《圣经》中没有明确阐述的机构。 许多这些命令在较低程度上可以由指定机构执行,但有一些限制。 一家人可以工作而不创业, 多数是

title: Ministry Lessons from the Puritans (with Joel Beeke)
summary: Joel Beeke joins Matt Smethurst and Ligon Duncan to explore what the Puritans can teach today’s pastors about prayer, preaching, personal holiness, shepherding souls, handling criticism, and persevering in ministry.

content: What can pastors today learn from the Puritans? Matt Smethurst and Ligon Duncan welcome Joel Beeke to discuss the lasting wisdom of Puritan pastors and theologians. title: On My Shelf: Life and Books with L. Michael Morales
summary: L. Michael Morales talks about what’s on his bedside table, favorite fiction, favorite rereads, and more.
summary_zh: L. Michael Morales谈论他床头柜上的东西、最喜欢的小说、最喜欢的重读等等。
title_zh: 在我的架子上： L. Michael Morales的生活和书籍
content: On My Shelf helps you get to know various writers through a behind-the-scenes glimpse into their lives as readers. I asked L. Michael Morales—professor at Greenville Presbyterian Theological Seminary and author of Exodus Old and New: A Biblical Theology of Redemption —about what’s on his bedside table, his favorite fiction, the books he regularly revisits, and more. What’s on your nightstand right now? Malcolm Guite’s Galahad and the Grail . Myths of origin hold potential for shaping a society’s culture and character. I believe Guite, aside from writing good poetry and a national epic, is endeavoring to reawaken (or refound) England to her rich Christian heritage. This volume is the first of a projected four-volume work that may well represent the new definitive collection of Arthurian legends. Writings of the Ramban , translated and annotated by Charles B. Chavel. Nachmanides is my favorite medieval Jewish exegete and commentator, and these essays illumine his character and offer gleaming gems of insight. His essay on redemption, for example, gives a nuanced understanding of eschatology in the Hebrew Scriptures. He argues convincingly that the exile threatened in Leviticus relates to the Babylonian exile that occurred in Jeremiah’s day, whereas exile in Deuteronomy uses more eschatological language and seems to relate to the exile after the Second Temple’s destruction. Another essay records his Disputation in Barcelona, when Nachmanides was forced by the Spanish government to engage in debate with a Jewish Christian convert. The disputation eventually led to his exile from Spain since, as one of the intellectual giants of his era, he acquitted himself overly well. (Christian readers will, for the most part, be disappointed with the representation of our faith by his opponent, but the disputation is helpful in that it offers insights into the sort of questions about the Messiah we should think about more deeply.) What are your favorite fiction books? Aside from literary classics, I enjoy mystery books, especially medieval mysteries, although it’s hard to find good ones. Ellis Peters’s Brother Cadfael series is good, although aimed for a younger audience (and so a bit tame). She had a beautifully poetic sense of providence and justice, which makes for satisfying conclusions. I also appreciate the espionage genre, such as the early works of John le Carré, like The Spy Who Came in from the Cold , A Small Town in Germany , and Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy . Perhaps less thoughtful but often more fun, Alistair MacLean’s books never fail to offer a little escape into adventure. What biographies or autobiographies have most influenced you and why? Iain H. Murray’s two-volume biography of D. Martyn Lloyd-Jones had a profound impact on me as a young, inexperienced pastor—my copies are filled with underlining and scribbled notes. This account of the Doctor’s life and ministry not only led me onto the paths of the Reformed faith, but demonstrated God’s blessings on a faithful minister’s diligent commitment to the ordinary means of grace, to prayer and preaching. Many of the problems and challenges facing the wider evangelical church when I was pastoring had their roots in the era of Lloyd-Jones’s ministry, so reading his biography offered much-needed biblical wisdom and the discernment of hindsight. Augustine’s Confessions is also a treasured book—it’s so personal and honest, and displays the sure and gracious hand of God in one’s life. Confessions is also about Augustine’s mother, Monica, and how she persevered in prayer on his behalf; and about God’s faithfulness and goodness in answering her prayers so abundantly. Throughout the book, readers also get fascinating glimpses of life in the late fourth and early fifth centuries. What are some books you regularly reread and why? Aside from regular Bible reading, it’s a challenge to reread many books, since my research-reading stacks are always waiting. Classics and modern classics, however
content_zh: 《我的书架》帮助你了解各种作家, 通过幕后人物的一幕来了解他们作为读者的生活。 我问L. Michael Morales — — 格林维尔长老会神学院的教授和《出老而新:救赎的圣经神学》的作者 — — 关于他的床边桌子上的内容、他最喜欢的虚构故事、他经常重读的书籍等等。 现在睡台上有什么? 马尔科姆·盖特的加拉哈德和圣杯。 起源神话具有塑造社会文化和性格的潜力。 我相信Guite除了写好诗作和国史诗外,还努力使英国重新认识(或重新发现)她丰富的基督教遗产。 本卷是一出预测的四卷作品中的第一部,很可能代表了"亚瑟传奇"的新最终集. 由Charles B. Chavel翻译和注释的《拉姆班人》的著作。 纳克曼尼得斯是我最喜欢的中世纪犹太人的特质和评论家,这些散文照亮了他的性格,并提供了光辉的洞察力. 例如,他关于赎罪的论文对希伯来圣经中的空想学有细微的理解. 他令人信服地辩称,在利维提库斯受到的放逐与耶利米时代发生的巴比伦人放逐有关,而Deuteronomy的放逐则使用更多的宗教语言,似乎与第二圣殿被摧毁之后的放逐有关。 另一篇散文记录了他在巴塞罗那的争议,当时纳克曼尼得斯被西班牙政府强迫与一名犹太基督徒皈依者展开辩论. 争议最终导致他被流放出西班牙,因为作为他时代的知识巨头之一,他为自己释出过好. (基督教读者大多会对其对手代表我们的信仰感到失望,但争论很有帮助,因为它能让人们深入了解我们应该更深入地思考的弥赛亚问题。 ) 你最喜欢什么小说? 除了文学经典之外,我还喜欢神秘的书籍,特别是中世纪的神秘,尽管很难找到好的书籍。 Ellis Peters的"Cadfael兄弟"系列虽然针对年轻观众(也有点温柔), 她有着美妙的诗意感 天赐和正义, 这可以得出令人满意的结论。 我也欣赏间谍流派,如约翰·勒·卡雷的早期作品,如"从寒冷中进来的间谍"(The Spy Who Came in from the Cold),"德国的一个小镇"(A Small Town)和"丁克"(Tinker,裁缝,Soldier,Spy)等. Alistair MacLean的书中, 什么传记或自传 影响最大,为什么? Iain H. Murray的两卷自传D. Martyn Lloyd-Jones对我这个年轻、经验不足的牧师产生了深远的影响——我的书中充满了强调和写作的笔记。 这种对医生生活和牧师的描述不仅使我走上了改革后信仰的道路,而且表明上帝保佑一位忠实的大臣勤勉地致力于普通的恩典、祈祷和传道。 在我做牧师时,广大福音派教会所面临的许多问题和挑战都起源于劳埃德-琼斯部的时代,因此阅读他的传记提供了急需的圣经智慧和后视力。 奥古斯丁的忏悔书也是一本珍贵的书 -- -- 它非常个人和诚实,在一个人的生活中展现出上帝的坚定和仁慈之手。 忏悔的内容还包括奥古斯丁的母亲莫妮卡,以及她如何代表他坚持祈祷;以及上帝如此忠实和善良地回答她的祈祷。 在整个书中,读者也获得了第四世纪后期和第五世纪初生活的迷人一瞥. 你经常读什么书? 除了定期阅读圣经之外, 重读许多书籍也是个挑战, 然而,古典和现代古典
author: Ivan Mesa, L. Michael Morales

title: How Can I Find the Motivation to Use My Time Better at Work?
summary: Let’s start by counting the cost.
summary_zh: 让我们从计算成本开始。
title_zh: 如何找到更好地利用工作时间的动力？
content: I work for a property management company that oversees retail space. I haven’t been doing this very long, but I’m finding that I’m not as productive as I’d like to be. Often, entertainment and fear of failure keep me from working. How can I get motivated to use my time better? Given that we’re to submit to our earthly masters with sincere hearts as unto Christ (Eph. 6:5), our productivity at work isn’t ultimately about our advancement or our employer’s success—it’s about our gospel witness. From before the fall, God ordained our work for keeping, cultivating, subduing, and exercising dominion over his creation. We’re still called to that today in any work to which we set our hand—including the property management of retail space. As believers, all work invites us to leverage our God-given talents and strength to bless and bring order to God’s creation in order to glorify him. When alluring distractions or a fear of failure hinder our labor, we can turn to him who calls us for the truth that will rightly spur us on. Distraction of Entertainment When entertainment distracts us from working, we should start by counting the cost. If we’re spending work hours on entertainment and then have to finish our tasks in what should be our free time, what else is this keeping us from stewarding well? It may be infringing on our time for relationships, spiritual disciplines, or true rest. On the other hand, if our working hours are fixed regardless of how on (or off) task we are, such as a job we clock in and out of with responsibilities only while we’re present, why are we willing to steal from our employer by accepting their payment without exchanging it for the labor we promised? Maybe we need to “cut off” what’s tempting us by blocking entertainment apps on our phone and computer during the workday (Matt. 5:30). If we’re spending work hours on entertainment, what else is this keeping us from stewarding well? Once we do, how might we instead faithfully devote that time to our employer’s good, even being willing to go a mile beyond what’s expected of us (v. 41)? Maybe we provide the talking points requested for a presentation—but also organize them into slides to save someone else from having to do so. Maybe we address the three issues our leader ask us to correct—but also address two more we discovered in the process. Perhaps if we worked with this level of diligence and care, like Joseph with Potiphar, we’d be given increased responsibility and influence that could be leveraged for the kingdom. Those who can be trusted with little can also be trusted with much (Gen. 39:1–6; Luke 16:10). Certainly, God would be glorified as we work with all our heart as to the Lord and not to man (Col. 3:23). Fear of Failure When a fear of failure keeps us from working altogether, we can start by digging out the root of that fear. Do you fear that your limitations and propensity to error will keep you from succeeding? Acknowledge that inaction guarantees you won’t succeed, but attempts to succeed in the work God has entrusted to you allow the opportunity for his power to be made perfect in your weakness (2 Cor. 12:9). When you feel discouraged by your insufficiencies, trust God to provide the wisdom and strength necessary for the work to which he’s called you—by prayer (James 1:5), the edification of his Word, and your humble pursuit of correction and growth through helpful resources and the example of others. Do you fear others’ judgment when you fail? Remember that your purpose is ultimately to please God, not man, and that there’s no condemnation for those in Christ (Rom. 8:1; Gal. 1:10). When you make a mistake or fall short of what’s expected of you, admit your error, seek understanding about what to do differently, and move forward with the humility and resolve that may make others respect you even more than they did before. content_zh: 我为一家监管零售空间的物业管理公司工作 但我发现自己没有自己想要的那么有生产力。 通常,娱乐和对失败的恐惧使我无法工作. 我怎么能有积极性 更好地利用我的时间? 我们的工作效率最终不是关于我们的进步或雇主的成功, 而是关于我们的福音见证。 从秋天之前开始,上帝就规定我们的工作是保持、培育、征服和支配他的创造。 包括零售空间的物业管理。 作为信徒,一切工作都邀请我们利用上帝赐予我们的才华和力量来祝福并给上帝的创造带来秩序来赞美他. 当引人注意或担心失败会阻碍我们的工作时,我们可以求助于他,他呼唤我们寻求正确激励我们的事实。 娱乐的分心 当娱乐干扰我们工作时,我们应该从计算成本入手。 如果我们在娱乐上花工时, 然后必须在什么是空闲时间完成我们的任务, 它可能侵犯我们的时间 关系,精神学科,或真正的休息。 另一方面,如果我们的工作时间是固定的,不管我们是如何完成(或关闭)任务的,比如我们只是在在场时就负责地工作,那么我们为什么愿意接受雇主的付款而不以我们承诺的劳动来换取呢? 也许我们需要在工作日(Matt. 如果我们在娱乐上花工时, 一旦我们这样做了,我们如何忠实地把时间用于雇主的利益,甚至愿意超越我们的期望(v.41)? 也许我们提供了演讲所要求的谈话要点,但也把它们组织成幻灯片,以拯救别人不必这样做。 我们或许可以解决我们领导人要求我们纠正的三个问题, 也许如果我们像约瑟夫和波提乏那样勤奋谨慎, 能够被很少信任的人也可以被很多信任(Gen. 39:1-6;Luke 16:10). 当然,当我们全心全意地为主而不是为人工作时,上帝将受到赞美(第3:23上校)。 对失败的恐惧 当对失败的恐惧使我们无法完全工作时,我们可以首先挖掘出这种恐惧的根源。 难道你怕自己的限制和偏执使你无法成功吗? 承认这种无所作为保证了你不会成功,但为了在上帝委托给你的工作上取得成功而作的尝试,允许他的机会在你的弱点中完美地发挥出他的力量(2 Cor. 12:9). 当你们因自己的不足而感到沮丧时,请相信上帝为他所说的你们的工作提供必要的智慧和力量——通过祈祷(詹姆斯1:5),将他的话化,并通过有益的资源和他人的榜样谦卑地追求纠正和成长。 难道你不怕别人的判断吗? 记住你的目的最终是为了取悦上帝,而不是取悦人类,对基督中的人没有谴责(8:1;Gal:1:10). 当你们犯错误或者没有达到预期时,你们承认自己的错误,寻求了解应该如何采取不同的做法,并以谦卑和决心前进,这可能会使别人比以前更加尊重你们。 相信上帝为他所说的你的工作提供必要的智慧和力量。 你怕你的身份吗?
author: Kaitlin Febles

title: Simon Says: Inconspicuous Evidence of Eyewitnesses in Mark
summary: Several features indicate that the eyewitness accounts of Simon stand behind Mark’s Gospel.
summary_zh: 有几个特征表明，西门的目击者叙述支持马可福音。
title_zh: 西蒙说：马可福音中不明显的目击者证据
content: When I watch Jesus films, whether the current series The Chosen , The Passion of the Christ in the early 2000s , or even Godspell from the 1970s, I can’t help but ask, Where did they get those stories? Sometimes I can piece together bits from Matthew, Mark, Luke, or John. Occasionally I detect legendary material from church history or the apocryphal gospels. But at other times, my best guess is “They made it up,” and I ascribe the scene to creative liberty. When we turn to the Gospel of Mark, which most scholars see as the first extant telling of the story of Jesus, we might also wonder, Where did Mark get these stories? Around the 1920s to ’50s, the fashionable scholarly answer was found in a field of study known as form criticism . This enterprise tried to tie different sayings and stories of Jesus back to an occasion within the early church that would have prompted their creation. Though the heyday of form criticism has passed, the legacy of seeing the Gospels as a “mixtape” of various ad hoc literary traditions can still be seen today. In contrast to form criticism and the Jesus-film industry, the canonical Gospels are sourced in eye-witness testimony and were written within living memory of the events they describe. Perhaps no other scholar has written so persuasively on this subject as Richard Bauckham in his magisterial Jesus and the Eyewitnesses . Indications of eye-witness testimony are peppered throughout Mark’s gospel. Here we will consider just a few, each revolving around the name “Simon.” These are more obscure than what normally make their way into works on apologetics, but their subtlety is a strength since they are not the kind of details one fabricates. We will discover that inconspicuous indicators of eyewitnesses reveal what is happening behind the scenes more than front-and-center observations. Evidence of Simon Peter There are signs that Simon Peter has been a significant source for Mark’s Gospel, despite Mark not making a show of it. The church father Papias famously stated that Mark was Peter’s interpreter, who wrote down what he remembered from his preaching. Though many scholars doubt Papias here, Mark goes out of his way to emphasize Simon Peter. Several features indicate that Mark is particularly told from a Petrine perspective. For example, his prominence verges on redundancy when he is introduced in 1:16: “Passing alongside the Sea of Galilee, [Jesus] saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.” This is part of what Bauckham calls a Peter inclusio, so that his testimony brackets the Gospel of Mark (see 16:7). Later in the narrative, those “sick or oppressed by demons” are brought to Jesus in Capernaum (1:32), the summary after the climactic exorcism at the synagogue (vv. 21–28). But sandwiched in the middle is the healing of Simon’s mother-in-law (vv. 29–31). Similarly, Mark writes of when the disciples look for Jesus, “Simon and those who were with him searched for him” (v. 36). Details like these betray a “Simon-centric” source. Bauckham argues that, with few exceptions, “Peter is actually present through a large proportion of the narrative from 1:16 to 14:72.” Several features indicate that Mark is particularly told from a Petrine perspective. An oddity in Mark’s grammatical style reinforces not just Simon Peter’s perspective but that of all the disciples: Mark uniquely favors using plural verbs to introduce singular ones. For example, Mark 11:12 reads, “On the following day, when they came from Bethany, he [Jesus] was hungry” (emphasis added). This provides the perspective of the group, as opposed to Matthew’s retelling: “In the morning, as he was returning to the city, he became hungry” (21:18). This literary device occurs 21 times in Mark’s narrative. Evidence of Many Simons The name “Simon” occurs 11 times in Mark. It most famously refers to Peter (1:16 [twice], 29, 30, 36; 3:16; 14:37), but it also refers to the other apostle, “Simon the Z
content_zh: 当我看耶稣的电影时,无论是现在的系列"选择"(The Chosen, The Passion of the Christ in 20世纪20年代早期),还是甚至从20世纪70年代起的"神话"(Godspell),我都不得不问,他们从哪里得到这些故事的? 有时我可以拼凑出马修,马克,卢克或约翰的位子. 偶尔我也会从教堂历史或启示录中 发现传奇材料 但在其他时候,我的最佳猜测是“他们编造的”,我把场景描述为创造性的自由。 当我们转向"马克福音"时,大多数学者认为它是第一个讲述耶稣故事的现存者,我们也可能会想,"马克从哪里得到这些故事的? 20世纪20至50年代, 时髦的学术答案出现在一个研究领域, 这个事业试图把耶稣的不同说法和故事与早期教会内部本来会促使他们创造的机会联系起来. 尽管形式批评的热潮已经过去,但今天仍然可以看到将福音书视为各种临时文学传统“混合”的遗产。 与形而上学的批评和耶稣-电影行业形成对比的是,"神舟福音"来源于目击证人的证词并被写在了他们描述的事件活生生的记忆中. 可能没有其他学者如此有说服力地写了 理查德·鲍克汉姆 在他的大法官耶稣和目击证人。 在马克的福音中, 在这里,我们将只考虑几个,每个环绕“西蒙”的名称。 这些比平时在古琴系上的工作更为模糊,但是其微妙性是一种力量,因为它们不是一种编织出来的细节。 我们将发现,目击证人的不显眼指标显示在幕后发生的情况比前中观察更明显。 西蒙·彼得的证据 有迹象表明西蒙·彼得一直是"马克福音"的重要出处,尽管马克没有对此表态. 教父帕皮亚斯出名地说,马克是彼得的翻译,他记下了他在布道时所记得的. 虽然许多学者怀疑这里有帕皮阿斯,但马克却不择手段地强调西蒙·彼得. 一些特征表明,马克尤其被从Petrine的角度讲述. 例如,在1:16介绍他时,他的突出之处是冗余:“[耶稣]在加利利海一并看到西蒙的兄弟西蒙和安德鲁将网投入大海,因为他们是渔民。” 这是Bauckham称之为"彼得·因克利奥"的一部分,因此他的证词将马克福音(见16:7)置于其中. 后来在叙事中,那些"被恶魔所生病或被压迫"的人被带到了卡佩尔瑙姆的耶稣面前(1:32),即犹太会堂的高潮驱魔后的摘要(v. 21–28). 但中间的三明治是西蒙婆婆(vv. 29–31)的治愈. 同样地,马克写道,当门徒们寻找耶稣时,“西蒙和与他在一起的人寻找他”(v.36)。 这些细节背叛了“以西蒙为中心”的来源。 Bauckham认为,除了少数例外,“彼得实际上通过1:16至14:72的很大一部分叙述存在。” 一些特征表明,马克尤其被从Petrine的角度讲述. 马克语法风格的奇特之处不仅强化了西蒙·彼得的观点,而且强化了所有门徒的观点: 使用复数动词标记独有的偏好来引入单数。 例如,Mark 11:12写道:“第二天,当他们从Bethany来时,他[耶稣]饿了”(着重号由作者标明)。 这提供了这个团体的视角,而不是马修的重述:"早上,当他回到城市时,他变得饥饿"(21:18). 这个文学装置在马克的叙述中发生21次. 许多西蒙的证据 “西蒙”这个名字在马克有11次出现。 最出名的是彼得(1:16 [两次],29,30,36;3:16;14:37),但也指另一位使徒"Simon the Z".
author: Bruce Henning

title: Broken Bodies Make Beautiful Temples
summary: We must view our foreign-feeling bodies as vessels through which God demonstrates his redeeming strength.
summary_zh: 我们必须把外在的身体看作是神展示祂救赎力量的器皿。
title_zh: 破碎的身体造就美丽的寺庙
content: The Lord’s ways are not our ways (Isa. 55:8–9). Do we take this seriously, or do we revert to “our ways” in desperate seasons when we wander from God to seek meaning? I revisit this battle every time I look in the mirror at a quadriplegic body I desperately hope is not me. “Our ways” tell me that the body is incidental to identity. It’s an enticing lie that exploits disorienting bodily experiences such as disability , sickness, gender dysphoria, or other bodily insecurities hindering people from seeing meaning in bodies that feel foreign. I don’t see the nobility of God’s image or a temple worthy to house the divine when I’m being catheterized, bathed, or rolled in bed to prevent pressure sores. For others, disfiguration, tumors, or injury characterize bodies they can’t wait to “escape” at the second coming. For still others, their bodies contradict strong inward feelings telling them who they “really” are. Whatever the motivation, we tend to downplay bodily meaning when we feel it compromises our dignity. But this is autonomy’s way, not the Lord’s way. Scripture tells us there’s nothing undignified about weak, broken, dependent, or foreign-feeling bodies. The apostle Paul says our bodies (of all conditions) are temples of the Holy Spirit (1 Cor. 6:19). No higher calling exists for the physical than to serve as a temple to house its Creator. Paul’s claim is a hard truth for those with bodily insecurities, because it means we must trade the disdain we feel toward our bodies for contentment—a difficult but worthy exchange. ‘Glory of the Immortal God’ Paul is well acquainted with bodily fragility and limitations, yet he doesn’t hesitate to make the body central to the identity of people he calls “more than conquerors through him who loved us” (Rom. 8:37). For example, Paul observes in Romans 1:18–31 that the quintessential sin resulting from “exchang[ing] the truth about God for a lie” (v. 25) and “exchang[ing] the glory of the immortal God for images resembling mortal man” (v. 23) is bodily sin that distorts God’s “very good” design for the body (Gen. 1:31). Thus, the “glory of the immortal God” of which Paul speaks is, at least in part, our bodies, which God created as his image (vv. 26–27). In Romans 6, Paul includes the body as part of the life Christ calls us to after “we have died with Christ” and subsequently “also live with him” (v. 8). He exhorts us to use our bodies “as instruments for righteousness” (vv. 12–13). Paul makes no exception for those with bodily insecurities. The body God gave you is an instrument for righteousness, no matter how broken or “inauthentic” it may feel. God’s Image, Not Ours Scripture teaches that my bodily self, no matter how foreign it feels, is me . And, like the rest of me, it doesn’t “belong” to me for two reasons. First, we’re not our own because the Lord makes his temples. Under the new covenant, “the Most High does not dwell in houses made by hands” (Acts 7:48), and the “Lord of heaven . . . does not live in temples made by man” (17:24). I did not make myself. The Lord “fearfully and wonderfully made” me; I am his “wonderful” work (Ps. 139:14) and “workmanship” (Eph. 2:10). He “formed my inward parts” and “knitted me together” (Ps. 139:13). Even brokenness, including disability, is the Lord’s wonderful work (Ex. 4:11; John 9:2–4). Second, we’re not our own because the Lord purchased us, body and all. Paul tells us bluntly, “You were bought with a price” (1 Cor. 6:20). A very high price: the death of his Son. My body is his, disability and all. Nothing about me is “mine” to do with as I please. My body is a temple for the Lord , not for me. He designed, constructed, and purposed it. “I” am no longer my own. Rather, my body is “meant . . . for the Lord, and the Lord for [my] body” (1 Cor. 6:13). My body is his, disability and all. Nothing about me is ‘mine’ to do with as I please. God has purposed my broken body and purchased my identity at the great price of his Son’s death to proclaim h
content_zh: 主道不是我们的道(以萨. 55:8-9). 我们是否认真对待这个问题,还是在绝望的季节里,当我们从上帝那里徘徊去寻求意义时,我们又回到“我们的方式”上来? 每次我照镜子时,我都会重温这场战斗,我迫切地希望这不是我。 “我们的方法”告诉我,尸体是身份的附带因素。 利用残疾、疾病、性别障碍或其他不安全感等令人不快的身体体验, 我看不到上帝的尊贵形象, 对其他人来说, 对其他人来说,他们的身体与告诉他们自己“真正”是谁的强烈内在感情相矛盾。 无论动机为何,当我们觉得身体损害我们的尊严时,我们往往会贬低身体意义。 但这是自治的方式,不是主的方式。 圣经告诉我们,对于软弱、破碎、依附或异国情调的躯体,没有什么不光彩的。 使徒保罗说,我们的身体(所有条件)都是圣灵的圣殿(1 Cor. 6:19). 没有比作为寺庙容纳造物主更高的要求了。 保罗的主张对身体不安全感的人来说是很难接受的,因为这意味着我们必须用我们对身体的蔑视来换取满足感——一种艰难而有价值的交换。 保罗非常熟悉身体的脆弱性和局限性,但他毫不犹豫地将身体置于他所称的“比通过爱我们的人来征服者”的人身份的中心地位(第8:37室)。 例如,保罗在罗马语1:18-31中观察到, " 以谎言为由推翻上帝的真理 " (v. 25)和 " 以不朽之神的光荣为像凡人的形象 " (v. 23)所产生的五等罪是身体罪,扭曲了上帝对身体的 " 非常好 " 的设计(Gen. 1:31)。 因此,保罗所说的“不朽之神的荣耀”至少部分是我们的身体,上帝创造了我们的身体作为其形象(v. 26-27)。 在罗马人6中,保罗将尸体列为基督要求我们在“与基督同生共死”之后生活的一部分,随后又“与他同生共活”(v.8)。 他劝我们用我们的身体 " 作为正义的工具 " (v.v.12-13)。 保罗对身体不安全的人也不例外。 上帝赐予你的身体是正义的工具,无论它多么破碎或“不真实”的感觉如何。 上帝的影像,而不是我们的经典,教导我身体的自我,无论感觉多么外在,都是我。 与我其他人一样, 我们不是自己人, 根据新盟约,“最高层不居住在由手造的房屋”(第7:48号法)和“天主......不居住在由人造的寺庙”(17:24)。 我没有做我自己。 主“亲切而出色地”我;我是他“出色”的作品(第139:14页)和“工作技巧”(第2:10页)。 他“组成了我的内在部分”并“把我织在一起”(第139:13页)。 甚至包括残疾在内的骨折也是主的精彩作品(Ex. 4:11;John 9:2–4). 我们不是自己人, 保罗直言不讳地告诉我们,“你被买下的价格”(第6:20节)。 一个非常高的代价:他儿子的死. 我的身体是他的,残疾和所有。 与我无关, 我的身体是上帝的神庙,不是我 他设计、建造和设计它。 “我”不再是我自己。 相反,我的身体是“为主而出,为我而出"(第6:13节)。 我的身体是他的,残疾和所有。 与我无关, 上帝用我破碎的躯体 以他儿子死后的巨大代价买下我的身份
author: James Abernathy

title: What My Grandparents Taught Me About Pastoral Ministry
summary: You’re being prepared for the work the Lord has for you in ways you may not understand until you’re standing in a hospice living room.
summary_zh: 你正准备好接受主为你所做的工作，直到你站在临终关怀的客厅里，你才会明白。
title_zh: 关于牧灵事工，我的祖父母教会了我什么
content: When I was in high school, and early on during the summers in college, I spent my days working at a local pharmacy. I got a one-hour lunch break, and I ended up going almost every day to lunch at my favorite place: Granny and PawPaw’s house. I don’t remember how it started. One day, I drove over on my lunch break, and after that, it became my routine. They wanted to see me, and I wanted to see them. Sitting at their table instead of alone at a restaurant was comfortable and unhurried. At the time, I didn’t think much about it. I was just eating lunch with my grandparents. But looking back, I realize the Lord was doing more than I understood. Having now sat beside countless hospital beds and in living rooms with families walking through suffering, I can see how those lunches prepared me for ministry in ways I didn’t yet understand. My grandparents taught me how to slow down, listen, and simply be present with people. PawPaw When we ate, my grandfather talked mostly about his time serving in the Korean War, his years as an insurance agent for Liberty National, or fishing, which he loved almost as much as anything in the world. Courtesy Jared Cornutt Of the three topics, he talked about Korea the most. The war had ended decades earlier, but it hadn’t really ended for him. It shaped the rest of his life. PawPaw survived the war; he never escaped it. He talked around it in the way men of his generation often did when they carried wounds no one had given them language for. They wanted to see me, and I wanted to see them. At the time, I didn’t think much about it. I was just eating lunch with my grandparents. When I sat across from him at that table, I didn’t know what PTSD was. I just knew Korea was never far from his mind. Now I realize why. My PawPaw came home from the war during an era when PTSD wasn’t understood. Men like him were told to put the war behind them. They were expected to come home, go to work, raise a family, and move on. Many did. But many, like my grandfather, carried the war with them for the rest of their lives. As a boy, I didn’t understand that. I just knew him first as my grandfather, and I knew he loved me. I’m thankful that’s how I got to know him. Granny My grandmother had an tenth-grade education. She grew up on a farm in a poverty she also never fully escaped. She never had much of a formal education, but I can tell you this: She knew the Lord, and the Lord knew her. If you heard her whole story, you might call her life a tragedy. But due to her remarkable faith, she wouldn’t describe it that way. Courtesy Jared Cornutt I can still see her sitting in that rocking chair when I’d come over, reading glasses on and her Bible open in her lap. She was eager to tell me what she’d read that morning. She loved God’s Word because she needed it and depended on it. Every time I left her house, she’d tell me the same thing: “I’m praying for you.” That meant more to me than any gift she could’ve ever given, because I knew she wasn’t just saying it. She really was praying for me . I now know there was much about her life I didn’t understand. But what stayed with me was that my grandmother loved Jesus, loved his Word, and faithfully prayed for her grandson. The Lord didn’t answer every prayer she prayed the way she hoped. But I’ve often wondered how many of God’s kindnesses in my life came through Granny’s faithful prayers. Ministry Now I share all this because I recently sat in another living room. It was different, but it felt oddly familiar. As I left that room, it dawned on me almost immediately that I was equipped to minister there only because of those lunches years before. title: Art Programs in Lebanon Bring Beauty to Midst of Crisis
summary: With Lebanon currently being impacted by war, a refugee crisis, and more, stories of beauty can be hard to come across. For ministries active in Lebanon, meeting the spiritual, physical...
summary_zh: 由于黎巴嫩目前受到战争、难民危机等的影响，美丽的故事可能很难被理解。对于在黎巴嫩活跃的事工，满足精神，物质...
title_zh: 黎巴嫩的艺术项目将美丽带入危机
content: With Lebanon currently being impacted by war, a refugee crisis, and more, stories of beauty can be hard to come across. For ministries active in Lebanon, meeting the spiritual, physical and emotional needs of a country just trying to survive can take its toll. Horizons International’s Pierre Houssney said that despite the trauma the country faces due to the fallenness of man in a sinful world, God has still created a world that contains beauty. “And I think that beauty speaks to people’s hearts about God, especially when it’s not just beauty, you know, for beauty’s sake, but when it’s beauty in the name of Christ,” Houssney said. “In the midst of the trauma, in the midst of the poverty, we’re trying to give opportunities for believers, who have artistic gifts, to have a prophetic voice through their art to the society, so that we can be calling out for Christ in the midst of the crisis.” Some of these opportunities for creating beauty are fine art classes offered by Horizons International. Horizons International has had up to 35 students at one time participating in these classes revolving around painting or drawing. Students in visual arts classes had the opportunity to participate in an exhibition in Beirut called “His Touch.” People from the community were invited to see the work of beginner students as well as 10 different Christian artists. Graphic design classes offer a more practical element, allowing students to learn a skill they could use in their everyday lives. On the worship side of things, music theory and classes in instruments are helping raise up worship leaders for local churches. One unit teaching guitar, piano, and drums to beginners looking to lead worship at their church had 70 people participate. “And so this new generation needs training, and they need, you know, they need mentoring, and they need to have those skills so that they can, they can lead their congregations in worship,” Houssney said. Though some may have more trouble connecting visual arts directly with ministry, Houssney says social media helps make that connection more clear. Beautiful videos that contain scripture messages alongside visual art tend to get a higher viewership. When posts like that get more views, they can potentially bring more people to Christ. “And so it needs to be beautiful. It needs to be excellent, it needs to be well done. And that’s what our Lord deserves,” Houssney said. “That’s not just what social media deserves.” Currently, Horizons International has to spread resources between humanitarian aid like food and medicine and projects that glorify God through the arts. In the midst of the crisis in Lebanon, pray for God to provide the resources for canvases, studio spaces, art instructors and more. Houssney also says what an organization like Horizons International is here for is to see God open more and more hearts to the Gospel. “So I’m not praying that the church would have less hardship. I’m not praying for you know, for less, you know, political chaos. What I’m praying for is that, through it all, people would continue to open their hearts, and that God will be glorified.” Learn more about the work of Horizons International in Lebanon by visiting https://www.horizonsinternational.org/lebanon-crisis .
content_zh: 黎巴嫩目前受到战争、难民危机等影响, 对活跃在黎巴嫩的各部来说,满足一个国家的精神、身体和情感需求,只是为了生存而努力,这可能会造成损失。 Horizons International的Pierre Houssney说,尽管由于人类在罪恶世界中的堕落,国家仍然面临创伤,但上帝仍然创造了一个包含美丽的世界。 “我认为,美丽对人们的心来说是关于上帝的,特别是当它不仅仅是为美丽着想,而是以基督为名的美丽时,”Houssney说。 “在创伤中,在贫困中,我们试图给那些拥有艺术天赋的信徒机会,通过他们的艺术向社会发出先知的声音,以便在危机中呼唤基督。” 其中一些创造美貌的机会是地平线国际提供的精美艺术课. 地平线国际曾经有多达35名学生参加这些围绕绘画或绘画而旋转的课. 视觉艺术课的学生有机会在贝鲁特参加一个名为“他的触摸”的展览。 社区人士被邀请观看初学者和10名不同的基督教艺术家的作品. 图形设计课程提供了更实用的元素,让学生学习在日常生活中可以使用的技能. 在事物的崇拜方面,乐器中的音乐理论和课程正在帮助培养地方教会的崇拜领袖. 一个教吉他,钢琴,和鼓的单位在他们的教堂里为初学者寻找引领崇拜,有70人参加. “因此,这新一代需要培训,他们需要,你知道,他们需要指导,他们需要这些技能,以便他们能够领导他们的教会进行礼拜。” 虽然有些人可能更难直接将视觉艺术与部委联系起来, 包含经文信息与视觉艺术的美丽视频往往获得更高的收视率. 当这样的帖子获得更多的观点时,它们有可能将更多的人带入基督. “因此,它必须是美丽的。 它需要出色,需要做得很好。 这才是我们的主应得的。 这不仅仅是社交媒体应得的。 目前,地平线国际必须在食品和医药等人道主义援助和通过艺术来赞美上帝的项目之间分配资源。 在黎巴嫩危机中,祈求上帝为画布、工作室空间、艺术教员等提供资源。 霍斯尼还说,像地平线国际这样的组织在这里是为了看到上帝对"福音"越来越开放的心. 我并不祈祷教会会减少困难。 我并不是为你们祈祷, 我所祈祷的是,通过这一切,人们将继续敞开心扉,而上帝将受到赞美。” 透过访问https://www.horisonsinternational.org/lebanon-crisis,

title: Abide
summary: This incident took place over 15 years ago, and yet, I remember it clearly. In the buzz of daily life, it is easy to get caught up in the carelessness...
summary_zh: 这件事发生在15年前，但我记得很清楚。在日常生活的嗡嗡声中，很容易陷入粗心大意……
title_zh: v.容忍
content: This incident took place over 15 years ago, and yet, I remember it clearly.  In the buzz of daily life, it is easy to get caught up in the carelessness of the checklists, and forget the intentionality of abiding in Him. I remember how frantic I was once at or late deadline and how frustrated I was at all the problems we were having in getting the program together.  We’d all kinds of equipment failure throughout the day and I was going to have to drive the program across town to get it uploaded to the satellite.  It was already 7 pm and the babysitter was calling me every 10 minutes. Then, I got a call from a lady with a gentle Creole accent. She told me, “I felt led to call you and pray with you.”  I SO didn’t want to talk to this lady, wasn’t interested in being prayed over, and really just wanted to leave to get this program fed and pick my 2-year old up.  I was impatient when I responded to her.  Rather than take insult from what was probably a curt rebuff,  she just said , “Wow. You REALLY need the peace of our heavenly Father on your heart right now.” And…she burst out in song.   Now I’m wondering why I’m on the phone with this crazy lady, and then she prayed through the worship song and then rolled right into praying for me, for my distress, for the things I thought I needed to do…and prayed that I would be still and listen, that my heart would be quiet long enough to remember the awe of God, and that the joy would come back to my heart as we produced MNN… The more she prayed, the more convicted I grew and I realized I was caught up in the ‘do’ and not the ‘be’…and THEN she pulled out the big guns: the story of Mary and Martha. Luke 10:38-42 New International Version (NIV) At the Home of Martha and Mary 38 As Jesus and his disciples were on their way, he came to a village where a woman named Martha opened her home to him. 39 She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to what he said. 40 But Martha was distracted by all the preparations that had to be made. She came to him and asked, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister has left me to do the work by myself? Tell her to help me!” 41 “Martha, Martha,” the Lord answered, “you are worried and upset about many things, 42 but few things are needed—or indeed only one. [ a ] Mary has chosen what is better, and it will not be taken away from her.” She ended our conversation with, “Sometimes, it’s ok to be Mary and sit at the feet of Jesus.  Stuff will still be there to do. It will eventually get done.  But the lasting investment is remembering to sit and BE at the feet of Jesus.” It was a much needed gentle rebuke along with a little encouragement from an unknown sister in Christ that I still remember to this day…thousands of productions later.   What we do is important…but not at the risk of forgetting to abide in Christ.
content_zh: 这一事件发生在15多年前,然而,我清楚地记得。 在日常生活中,很容易陷入清单的粗心大意之中,而忘记遵守他的意向。 我记得我曾经在最后期限或晚到的时候 多么疯狂 以及我对我们把节目整理好时遇到的所有问题 感到多么沮丧 我将不得不把程序推向全城, 已经七点了 保姆每十分钟给我打电话 然后,我接到一个女士的电话 带着温柔的克里奥尔口音。 她对我说:我的确猜想,我曾与你一起祈祷。 我本不想和这位女士交谈, 我对她的反应很不耐烦 她没有从可能是一种曲折的反驳中取出侮辱,而是说,“哇。 你现在真的需要我们天父的和平。” 然后... 她唱出歌来 她透过崇拜之歌祈祷, 然后转而为我祈祷, 为我的痛苦祈祷, 祈祷我需要做的事情. 她越是祈祷, 我越是被定罪, Luke 10:38-42 新国际版 (NIV) 在玛莎和玛丽38的家,由于耶稣和他的门徒们在路上,他来到一个村庄,一个叫玛莎的女人向他打开了她的家. 39 她有一个叫玛丽的姐姐,她坐在主的脚下,听他说的话。 40,但玛莎被所有必须做的准备所分心. 她来到他身边问道,“主啊,你难道不关心我姐姐离开我一个人做这个工作吗? " 41 " Martha, Martha, " 主回答说, " 你对许多事情感到担心和不安,42件,但需要的东西很少,甚至只有一件。 [a] 玛利亚已选择了更好的事物,它不会被夺走。 她结束我们的谈话时, 事情还会在那里做。 它最终会完成。 但持久的投资是记得坐在耶稣的脚下。” 这是非常需要的温柔的回斥 以及基督中一个未知的妹妹的一点鼓励 我至今仍然记得... 我们所做的是重要的... 但不会冒着忘记遵守基督的风险

title: Koinonia
summary: Koinonia (Koy-no-nee’-ah) is a Greek word, occurring 20 times in the Bible, which means “fellowship” or “brotherly love.” It carries with it the meaning of a committed, trustworthy, and dependable...
summary_zh: Koinonia （ Koy-no-nee '-ah ）是一个希腊语单词，在圣经中出现了20次，意思是“团契”或“兄弟之爱”。“它带有忠诚、值得信赖和可靠的意义……
title_zh: Koinonia
content: Koinonia (Koy-no-nee’-ah) is a Greek word, occurring 20 times in the Bible, which means “fellowship” or “brotherly love.” It carries with it the meaning of a committed, trustworthy, and dependable relationship. Such a relationship can be experienced through participation, sharing, giving, and contributing. The first occurrence of koinonia is Acts 2:42 “They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.” But the rest of the passage reads:  “ 43 Everyone was filled with awe at the many wonders and signs performed by the apostles. 44 All the believers were together and had everything in common. 45 They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. 46 Every day they continued to meet together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, 47 praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.” Christian fellowship is a key aspect of the Christian life. Believers in Christ are to come together in love, faith, and encouragement. The essence of koinonia: “one another”. Scripture commands us to be devoted to one another (Romans 12:10), honor one another (Romans 12:10), live in harmony with one another (Romans 12:16; 1 Peter 3:8), accept one another (Romans 15:7), serve one another in love (Galatians 5:13), be kind and compassionate to one another (Ephesians 4:32), admonish one another (Colossians 3:16), encourage one another (1 Thessalonians 5:11; Hebrews 3:13), spur one another on toward love and good deeds (Hebrews 10:24), offer hospitality (1 Peter 4:9), and love one another (1 Peter 1:22; 1 John 3:11; 3:23; 4:7; 4:11-12). Koinonia is translated many different ways in English Bibles: -fellowship (koinonia), to the breaking of bread and the prayers.” -contribution (koinonia) for them and for all others.” Paul writes to the believers in Philippi: “That I may know him and the power of his resurrection, and may share (koinonia) his sufferings, becoming like him in his death” (Phil 3:10). – Christian living– the dynamic whole of it. It describes an interactive relationship between God and believers who are sharing new life through Christ.  It captures the entirety of this relationship. It involves active participation in Christian community: sharing in spiritual blessings and giving material blessings. How does this idea fit into the theology of ‘And’? Acts 1:8—it empowers us with the chisomo—the grace to DO—the all-inclusive– “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.” And they will know you by your love.  (John 13:35)   “By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.”

title: Covenant
summary: Isaiah 54:10 Though the mountains be shaken and the hills be removed, yet my unfailing love for you will not be shaken nor my covenant of peace be removed,” says...
summary_zh: Isaiah 54:10大山虽摇动，小山虽迁移，我对你们永不止息的爱却不摇动，我平安的约也不迁移。”
title_zh: 契  约
content: Isaiah 54:10  Though the mountains be shaken and the hills be removed, yet my unfailing love for you will not be shaken nor my covenant of peace be removed,” says the LORD, who has compassion on you. There is something of music in the very sound of these words. The thought that lies below them, sweeping as it does through the whole creation, and parting all things into the transient and eternal, the mortal and immortal, is still greater than the music of the words. ‘These’ are removed; ‘this’ abides. The thing in God which abides is all-gentle tenderness, that strange love mightier than all the powers of Deity beside, permanent with the permanence of His changeless heart. ‘My loving kindness and the covenant of My peace,’ outlast everything else. The antithesis of what passes and what abides is mind-boggling. ‘all things are in a state of flux’—it’s a basic tenant of physical science…and yet it seems as unchanging as anything we know…it’s the shape of the box…and yet,  if we had nothing abiding beyond this universe, what would be the point? There’s an unspoken  ‘But’  here–  in that vacuum, the Great Spirit moves all the material universe, Himself unmoved, undiminished by creation, or by said vacuum.  The Unknowable whose name means ‘breath’ is YHWH—who comes to us in man-form to help the created move toward and abide in this presence. I’m sort of blown away by how big this passage paints God…and blown away that we are His children…and that we able to abide because of Christ…that our part in glorifying Him and enjoying Him forever comes in walking alongside a global family and telling their stories.  Insignificant, by itself, but being used as a tool to help others abide and recognize the mercy and grace of this big Abba. We can touch the face of God…because He calls us to Himself.
