title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有“万能钥匙”
content: The first of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. A question of major importance is ‘How am I to live as a Christian’? It is one thing to be certain on biblical grounds that I have life from Christ, now I must be clear as to how I am to live the life of Christ. My purpose in setting before you some of the major principles of living the Christian life is three-fold: —I wish to sketch in a biblical theology of the Christian life. My purpose is unashamedly one of indoctrination. I wish by God’s help, by Spirit and word, to indoctrinate you in a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. —I wish to inoculate you and to immunize you against the major false views of the Christian life. Some of us desperately wish we had received such an inoculation early in our Christian experience. We spent many years chasing rabbits that we could never catch. We went after experiences and states of mind and heart in the hope that somehow in so doing we would find what it really meant to live as a Christian. —I wish to purge you of any existing misconceptions which you may presently have. It may not be pleasant but it is in your own best interests. We now examine these major principles of the Christian life. Principle 1: There is No One ‘Master Key’ to Living the Christian Life The kind of teaching I am purposing to focus upon in this principle goes something like this: There is a Christian who for many years has found himself in the doldrums. He has had his sails hoisted but he goes nowhere. It seems that he knows little of the wind of the Spirit filling his sails and carrying him anywhere. Or, to change the analogy, he may have his sails hoisted but they seem for ever to be full of holes, and while all around him have hoisted sails and appear to be making progress he seems to be going nowhere. And then one day at a conference or while reading a book or in his own devotions he comes across a passage of Scripture, say John chapter 15, and there he reads in the words of our Lord Jesus that beautiful analogy of the Christian’s relationship to Christ as the relationship of a branch to a vine. This so ignites his own spiritual life that he is almost overnight lifted to an entirely new plateau of spiritual vitality. Either the holes in his sails get mended or it is as though a mighty zephyr from God himself fills his sails, causing them to billow out to the full. He makes more substantial progress in the Christian life in six months than he has made in the previous six years. This man says that the master key to the Christian life is understanding John 15 and if others will only come to understand the concept of Christ’s relationship to his people as the branch and the vine are related they too will come to an entirely new plateau of spiritual vitality and reality in their Christian walk. Another example could be someone who has been struggling with a certain besetting sin which leaves him continually bowed down and crippled with guilt. Here is a young Christian struggling with a certain area of besetting sin, unknown to others, and he is constantly bogged down. His wheels are up to the hub-caps in mud, and no matter how much he changes the gears and pushes down on the accelerator he is spinning his wheels and all he is doing is using up petrol and making a mess. He is in that position for weeks and months perhaps, and then one day at a conference or reading a book or in his own devotions he comes to Romans, chapter 6, and he reads the glorious truth that in union with Jesus Christ all that he was as old man has been put to death, and in union with Jesus Christ the totality of the old life has been buried in Christ’s tomb and he is now a new man in Jesus Christ and he sees that he is called upon to reckon it so, and in the light of that, present himself as alive from the dead. content: Edited by John Hendryx in epub , .mobi & .pdf formats Since faith is infinitely beyond all the power of our unregenerated human nature, it is only God who can give the spiritual ears to hear and eyes to see the beauty of Christ in the gospel. God alone disarms the hostility of the sinner turning his heart of stone to a heart of flesh (2 Cor 4:4-6). It is God, the Holy Spirit, alone who gives illumination and understanding of His word that we might believe; It is God who raises us from the death of sin, who circumcises the heart; unplugs our ears; It is God alone who can give us a new sense, a spiritual capacity to behold the beauty and unsurpassed excellency of Jesus Christ. The apostle John recorded Jesus saying to Nicodemus that we naturally love darkness, hate the light and WILL NOT come into the light (John 3:19, 20). And since our hardened resistance to God is thus seated in our affections, only God, by His grace, can lovingly change, overcome and pacify our rebellious disposition. The natural man, apart from the quickening work of the Holy Spirit, will not come to Christ on his own since he is at enmity with God and cannot understand spiritual things (1 Cor 2:14). Shining a light into a blind man's eyes will not enable him to see, because eyesight first requires a set of healthy eyes.

content: by Louis Berkhof In ePub , .mobi and .pdf formats You may also download the separate Introductory Volume to Systematic Theology here. Professor Berkhof, who was the President of Calvin Seminary and professor of Systematic Theology at the same in the first half of the twentieth century, has given us an excellent compendium of Reformed theological thought in this hefty volume. The subject is treated in the classical style, moving through the Doctrines of God, Man in Relation to God, the Person and Work of Christ, the Application of the Work of Redemption, the Church and the Means of Grace, and the Last Things. For decades, Louis Berkhof’s Systematic Theology has remained one of the most important and widely-used systematic theologies. It provides the clearest and most succinct articulation of Reformed theology. From its first publication in 1932, Berkhof’s work was revised, reprinted, and translated into Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, and Portuguese, and it had become a standard theological text by 1950. It has gained near-universal use in seminaries and Bible colleges across the world, and is widely cited and used by pastors, theologians, and students of nearly all denominational affiliations.

content: by Thomas Manton in ePub , .mobi & .pdf formats SUCH is the divine matter and admirable order of the Lord’s Prayer, as became the eternal wisdom of God, that composed and dictated it to his disciples. In it are opened the fountains of all our regular petitions, and the arguments contained to encourage our hopes for obtaining them. In our addresses to men, our study is to conciliate their favourable audience; but God is most graciously inclined and ready to grant our requests, therefore we are directed to call upon him by the title of ‘Our Father in heaven,’ to assure us of his love and power, and thereby to excite our reverent attention, to raise our affections, to confirm our confidence in prayer. The supreme end of our desires is the glory of God, in conjunction with our own happiness: this is expressed in the two first petitions, that ‘his name may be hallowed,’ and ‘his kingdom come,’ that we may partake of its felicity. In order to this, our desires are directed for the means that are proper and effectual to accomplish it. And those are of two kinds — the good things that conduct us, and the removal of those evils that obstruct our happiness.

I told you then that this passage contains two things—first the character of true Christians, and secondly their privileges—first what they are to their Savior, and secondly what their Savior is to them. Let me, then, remind you what the text says of their character. "My sheep hear My voice, and I know them, and they follow Me." (John 10:27) 1. God's children, His real believing people, are compared to sheep , because they are gentle, quiet, harmless and inoffensive; because they are useful and do good to all around them; because they love to be together, and dislike separation; and lastly because they are very helpless and wandering and liable to stray. 2. Jesus calls them " My sheep ," as if they were His peculiar property. "Mine," He would have us know, by election, "Mine" by purchase, and "Mine" by adoption. 3. Christ's sheep hear His voice, they listen humbly to His teaching, they take His word for their rule and guide. 4. Christ's sheep follow Him, they walk in the narrow path He has marked out, they do not refuse because it is sometimes steep and narrow--but wherever the line of duty lies they go forward without doubting.

content: by Archibald Alexander In ePub , .mobi and .pdf formats On the basis of fifty years as a pastor, preacher and professor at Princeton Theological Seminary, Archibald Alexander (1772-1851) deals with the subjective work of the Holy Spirit in the heart in all its phases, from the new birth until final preparation for heaven. There are two kinds of religious knowledge which, though intimately connected as cause and effect, may nevertheless be distinguished. These are the knowledge of the truth as it is revealed in the Holy Scriptures; and the impression which that truth makes on the human mind when rightly apprehended. The first may be compared to the inscription or image on a seal, the other to the impression made by the seal on the wax. When that impression is clearly and distinctly made, we can understand, by contemplating it, the true inscription on the seal more satisfactorily, than by a direct view of the seal itself. Thus it is found that nothing tends more to confirm and elucidate the truths contained in the Word, than an inward experience of their efficacy on the heart. It cannot, therefore, be uninteresting to the Christian to have these effects, as they consist in the various views and affections of the mind, traced out and exhibited in their connection with the truth, and in their relation to each other.

But, alas! after our utmost and most diligent inquiries, we must say, How little a portion is it of him that we can understand! His glory is incomprehensible, and his praises are unutterable. Some things an illuminated mind may conceive of it; but what we can express in comparison of what it is in itself, is even less than nothing. But as for those who have forsaken the only true guide herein, endeavouring to be wise above what is written, and to raise their contemplations by fancy and imagination above Scripture revelation (as many have done), they have darkened counsel without knowledge, uttering things which they understand not, which have no substance or spiritual food of faith in them.

content: "Although They Knew God ... They Suppressed the Truth..." The opportunities are wide open for Christians to speak with secular people these days, especially if you live in a metropolitan area. The average hipster you may meet in the medium to big sized city is a secularist who may listen to NPR, has a liberal, ecological, and/or anti-capitalist political ideology ... wears vintage clothing from a thrift store and consumes ethically. He or she often either rides a bike, uses public transportation or even may be driving a hybrid or bio-diesel vehicle. This person is deeply concerned with the ethical treatment of animals, is strongly against slavery, torture, racism and political oppression against women. In other words, he takes morality very seriously. Another characteristic of this individual is that he/she thinks Christianity is irrelevant at best. Since we deeply care about the eternal destinies of such individuals how should we go about reaching such a person with the gospel? Where would you start? Once of the more effective ways, I have found, is to remember that that your secular friend already knows God exists. He/she knows God exists and lives as if He does. In Romans chapter 1 Paul clearly teaches this about all people when he says, "For although they knew God" (verse 21) "...by their unrighteousness suppress the truth" (verse 18). But how can we demonstrate to your friends that they already believe in God, when intellectually they deny His existence? While there are many ways this could be done, I would like to suggest one way that I have found to be quite persuasive: The knowledge of God through their own morality.
content_zh: "虽然他们认识上帝... 这些天基督徒与世俗人士交谈的机会是广阔的,特别是如果你生活在一个都市地区. 在中等至大城市中,你可能遇到的平凡的嬉皮士是一个世俗主义者,他可能听从NPR,具有自由主义,生态主义和/或反资本主义的政治意识形态.穿着节俭店出产的古装并合乎道德地消费. 他或她往往要么骑自行车,使用公共交通,要么甚至可能驾驶混合或生物柴油车辆. 此人对动物的道德待遇深感关切,强烈反对奴役、酷刑、种族主义和对妇女的政治压迫。 换句话说,他非常重视道德。 这个人的另一个特征是,heshe认为基督教最多是无关紧要的. 既然我们深深地关心这些人的永恒命运,那么我们如何用福音去帮助这样一个人呢? 你从哪里开始? 我发现,最有效的方法之一 就是记住,你的世俗朋友已经知道上帝的存在。 他/她知道上帝的存在 并活得像他一样 在罗马人第一章中,保罗明确教导了这一点,他说:"虽然他们认识上帝"(第21节)"......以不义压制真理"(第18节). 但我们怎能向你的朋友证明,他们已经信仰了真主,而他们在理智上否认他的存在呢? 虽然有许多方法可以做到这一点,但我想建议一种方法,我认为它很有说服力: 以自德而知神.

content: Good morning. I am making my way home from Colorado today after a productive series of meetings and video shoots. I’ll look forward to a more normal week next week! In the meantime, be sure to check in tomorrow for Weekend A La Carte and on Sunday for a favorite feature, Works & Wonders. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include lots of interesting books like an exposition of the London Baptist Confession, some brief biographies of Christians you should know, and Thaddeus Williams’s book on reverence. Some of my books are 50% off at ChurchSource in their print editions: Visual Theology , A Visual Theology Guide to the Bible , and Pilgrim Prayers . Recommended Reading Time Flies—and Death Comes Speedily. The older you get, the more you come to understand that time flies and death comes speedily. “As teenagers, my friends and I were awash with youthful pride, poking fun at weighty things we knew little about—completely ignorant that our life here below is ‘a mist that appears for a little time and then vanishes.’ The dew was still afresh upon our heads; the road of life unfurling in a great spool before our feet, disappearing into the far-off horizon. We could quote you verses here and there from the Scriptures, all the while being completely unversed in this point: “It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting, for this is the end of all mankind, and the living will lay it to heart.” In our minds, we could afford to mock death because we were, at the time, so far removed from it.” Was Piper Unprepared? A little while ago, John Piper indicated that he may have been unprepared for pastoral ministry when he began it. In this episode of Ask Pastor John , he is asked to explain what he meant by that. Take Your Faith Deeper with Ligonier’s Grow App. During a time of spiritual decline, God used the Protestant Reformation to bring renewal to His church through the recovery of the biblical gospel. This Reformation Day, explore the truths that fueled renewed devotion to God and His Word in the Grow app from Ligonier. Discover hundreds of Reformation-themed articles, video teaching series, and conference messages to help strengthen your faith and deepen your walk with Christ. Download the Grow app today. (Sponsored) The Engineering Behind Every Heartbeat. This is a celebration of the engineering of the human heart. “The human heart does not beat like a perfect clock. The time between beats changes as the body breathes, moves, rests, and reacts to the world around it. New research shows that these changes are part of a feedback system linking the heart, brain, and nerves. The heart keeps a steady rhythm while remaining flexible when needed, much like a well-built control system.” When You Trick-or-Treat, Nod to Martin Luther. Daniel Hyde writes in a local paper to explain to its readers the Protestant contribution to Halloween. “So, by all means, dress up and hand out the candy. When the doorbell rings, remember: The principle that no authority may command conscience protects the civil liberty of the religious and nonreligious alike.” God’s Left Hand. Bryce Waller: “The most difficult part about politics is what happens after the elections. In Romans 13:1, God calls us to be subject to these governing authorities—to obey the laws they pass, to show them honor and respect, to give them our hard-earned money by paying taxes. Voting is one thing, but submitting my life to a politician, showing respect to that guy , paying taxes to those people —even the people I didn’t choose? That’s not so easy.” These are good things to work out before an election since it will shape your response, whether you are happy with the results or dismayed. 17 Exhortations For Christian Citizens. Aaron Renn explains how “asymmetric blame, hectoring lectures, and selectively revived norms are driving young men to the influencers the mainstream condemns.” How Mental Illness Became an Identity. Myles Werntz has an interesting review of a new book by Fredrik deBoer that explains how mental illness became an identity. “Mental illness in the 21st century is an expanding category—and one increasingly dominated by its most functional and therefore visible members. That displacement—in our collective imagination and public discourse—of the profoundly mentally ill by my college students didn’t happen all at once. And how did it happen? title: Is It a Sin to Use AI Porn?
summary: What happens when the people in porn are not real exist, but are merely generated by AI? Could AI allow us to create ethical pornography that solves one of the foremost concerns that come with real pornography? In other words, is it a sin to look at AI-generated porn? See Also 10 Ugly Numbers Describing Pornography Use in 2017 10 Articles on Pornography 7 Good Reasons To Stop Looking at Porn Right Now
summary_zh: 当色情片中的人并不真实存在，而只是由人工智能产生时，会发生什么？人工智能是否允许我们制作道德色情作品，以解决真实色情作品带来的首要问题之一？换句话说，看人工智能生成的色情片是一种罪恶吗？另请参阅2017年描述色情使用的10个丑陋数字10篇关于色情的文章7个现在停止观看色情的好理由
title_zh: 使用人工智能色情片是罪过吗？
content: Over the past two decades, I have written a great deal about pornography . At many different times and in many different forms, I have urged people to consider a long list of arguments against it. I’m thankful to have interacted with many people who have come to see pornography as evil and who have committed themselves to sexual purity. Some of the strongest and most effective arguments against using pornography are based upon the humanity of the people who are involved in it. So, for example, in “ 7 Good Reasons To Stop Looking at Porn Right Now ,” I wrote that we need to consider the cost to those who make it. “Pornography exacts a high cost of those who create it—the cost to their bodies, to their souls, to their mental well-being, to their dignity, to their future. A vast amount of the pornography you enjoy is created by people against their wills. The simple fact is, by watching porn, you are watching rape and deriving pleasure from it. You become a willing participant in sexual violence and you allow that actor on the screen to suffer for your pleasure.” Even if some pornography is consensual, a great deal of pornography is not, and the viewer cannot know which is which. Similarly, in “ 8 Sins You Commit Whenever You Look at Porn ,” I said that those who watch it are guilty of sexual assault. “A person who drives a getaway car for a band of bank robbers will rightly be charged with murder for anyone who is killed in committing that crime. The person who voluntarily watches sexual assault for purposes of titillation is rightly guilty of that sexual assault. And a nauseating quantity of pornography is violent in nature, displaying men taking advantage of women. Sometimes these women have volunteered for such degradation and sometimes they are forced or raped into it. To watch such horrifying smut is to be a participant in it and to bear the moral blemish of it.” While these are far from the only arguments against pornography, I believe they are especially effective ones. But what happens when the characters involved in pornography are no longer people? What happens when they no longer exist at all, but are merely generated by AI? Could AI allow us to create “ethical pornography” that solves one of the foremost concerns that come with “real” pornography? In other words, is it a sin to look at AI-generated porn ? (For our purposes, we will assume that we are already rejecting deepfake porn—using the likeness of an existing person—as morally repugnant and both immoral and illegal. Instead, we are considering images of people who are generated entirely by AI.) The simple answer is yes: it is as sinful to look at AI-generated porn as it is to look at human-created porn. While some of the arguments may not be as relevant, the majority are unchanged. Before I explain how and why, I want you to listen to a warning: we are all experts at circumventing the spirit of the law by abiding within the strict letter of the law. There is something deep within us that wants to defy the rules that are given to us, and we become skilled at justifying the ways we do this. Often this involves reducing morality to a strict binary, then convincing ourselves that because we have not blatantly broken the law, we have abided by it. This was exactly the sin of the Pharisees of Jesus’s day who would strictly tithe the spices they grew in their gardens, yet fail to live according to the higher principles of justice, mercy, and faithfulness. There is something of the Pharisee in each one of us. With that in mind, here are reasons why it is a sin to use pornography that has been generated by AI. You are still lusting , even if you are lusting after a person who exists only on a screen. To lust is to long for an illicit sexual pleasure, and to long for an illicit sexual pleasure is to find satisfaction in what God has forbidden. It is to make something other than God necessary for your joy—in this case, the sexual release that would come with looking at an
content_zh: 在过去20年里,我写了很多关于色情的内容。 在许多不同的时刻,我以许多不同的形式敦促人们考虑一长串反对它的论点。 我很感激与许多人互动, 一些强烈而最有效的反对使用色情作品的论据是基于参与其中的人的人道. 因此,例如,在“停止看色情电影的7个好理由”中,我写道,我们需要考虑制作者的成本。 " 色情制品的制作者付出了高昂的代价 -- -- 他们的身体、灵魂、精神健康、尊严、未来的代价。 你所欣赏的大量色情作品都是由人们违背自己的意愿所创造的. 简单的事实是,通过看色情片, 你正在看强奸,并从中获得乐趣。 你成为性暴力的自愿参与者,你允许屏幕上那个演员为取悦而受苦。” 即使有些色情作品是合意的,但大量的色情作品却不是,观众也无法知道哪个是. 同样,在“每当你看到色情制品时,你就会犯下八起罪行”中,我说,观看色情制品的人犯有性侵犯罪。 “为一帮银行劫匪驾驶逃跑的汽车的人,将因犯下这种罪行而被杀害的人受到谋杀的指控。 自愿观看性攻击以达到抚慰目的的人理应犯有性攻击罪。 而令人恶心的色情作品数量在性质上是暴力的,展现出男性利用女性. 有时,这些妇女自愿从事这种有辱人格的工作,有时她们被迫或被强奸。 目睹这种令人发指的一团糟,就是参与其中,并承担其中的道德污点。” 虽然这些与反对色情制品的唯一论点相去甚远, 但是当参与色情的人物不再是人时会怎样呢? 当它们不再存在,而只是由AI产生时会发生什么? 大赦国际能否允许我们制造出“道德色情制品”,解决与“真正的”色情制品有关的最主要关切之一? 换句话说,看AI生成的色情片是不是罪过? (为了我们的目的,我们将假定,我们已经在拒绝利用像现有个人那样的深层假色情,认为这种色情在道德上是令人厌恶的,既不道德又非法。) 相反,我们正在考虑完全由大赦国际创造的人的形象。 ) 简单的回答是:看AI生成的色情片和看人造色情片一样罪恶. 虽然有些论点可能并不那么相关,但大多数论点没有改变。 在我解释方式和原因之前,我要你们聆听一个警告:我们都是通过遵守严格的法律条文来规避法律精神的专家。 我们内心深处有些东西想藐视赋予我们的规则,我们变得有技巧为我们这样做的方式辩护。 这往往涉及将道德降低为严格的二进制,然后说服自己,因为我们没有公然违法,我们遵守了法律。 这恰恰是耶稣时代的法利赛人的罪过,他们严格地说要将自己在花园所种的调味品的两倍之多,但却未能按照正义、慈悲和忠诚的更高原则活下来。 我们每个人都有法利赛人 考虑到这一点,以下是使用大赦国际制作的色情制品的罪责。 你仍然在贪欲, 即使你在贪欲 一个人只存在于屏幕上。 性欲是渴望非法的性快感,而渴望非法的性快感是寻求上帝所禁止的满足. 是为了让上帝之外的东西成为你欢乐的必备之物——在这种情况下,是性释放,而这种性释放会伴随着对一个...

content: Good morning. May the Lord be with you and bless you today, my friends. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include lots of good books from New Growth Press and other publishers. Among them you’ll find several good options from Jared Wilson. Recommended Reading Goodbye, ‘Sam’s Club’ Megachurch. Hello, Stained Glass. Christianity Today reports on what I consider a welcome trend: church buildings that look like churches instead of warehouses. It begins this way: “Trinity Presbyterian finally has a church building of its own. That building has arches. And carved hammerbeams that tell the story of the Bible.” 3 Reasons Why Christians Should Lay “R.I.P.” to Rest. Nick Batzig thinks it would be best for Christians to lay R.I.P. to rest. “I’ve noticed something of a concerning trend over the past several years. It is the way in which believers speak about culture-impacting individuals at their deaths. Instead of simply expressing appreciation for their life and achievements, it has become commonplace for Christians to use the shorthand ‘R.I.P.’ (rest in peace) on social media when speaking of individuals in whose lives there was no evidence of saving grace at their death. At the risk of sounding ill-tempered, I wish to set out several reasons why I am troubled by this occurrence.” Go Deeper with Ligonier’s Grow App. Looking to put down roots in God’s Word? The Grow app from Ligonier Ministries gives you clear Bible teaching and guides your daily study for a deeper walk with Christ. Ministry Partners can also access the verse-by-verse notes from the Reformation Study Bible directly in the app and get reliable answers to their theological questions with the Ask Ligonier intelligent assistant. Not a Ligonier Ministry Partner yet? Try these features for 30 days when you download Grow and sign in. (Sponsored) Beauty Demands to Be Noticed. Michael Jensen is right: beauty demands to be noticed. He tells about people who understand the connection between beauty and transcendence and says, “Clearly, the reductive and polemical explanation of the atheists isn’t proving to be compelling. People can’t square their deeply felt experience of the world with that. To the people I’ve been speaking with, at least, the world simply cannot be reduced to its material components, nor can its coherence be explained by resorting to chance.” Aslan Sane: The Bowiefication of Narnia. I’ve got a pair of articles to share that comment on the forthcoming Narnia movies, each taking a different perspective. In the first, the writer remembers the old Narnia series from her childhood and bridges from there to what we know of the new one. She’s not impressed with it. Aslan and the Christians Who Can’t Be Enchanted. In the second, the author rebukes people like me (and the previous author) who have expressed concerns. He reminds us that it’s a movie for kids and that we don’t really know much about it yet. (I’d say he writes with some degree of exaggeration when he accuses me of losing my mind, but I’m glad to consider what he says nonetheless.) The Day of Pioneer Missions Is Not Over. Writing for Desiring God, my friend Tim Keesee wants us to know that the day of pioneer missions is not over. “Pioneer missionaries are still needed today because there are vast territories and high-rise megacities where the gospel message has yet to reach.” Videos Worth Watching Here are several brief videos that are worth your time. 5 Signs Your Church Might Be Too Seeker Sensitive. Adriel Sanchez explains seeker sensitivity and offers signs your church might lean too much in that direction and become seeker driven. How to Leave a Church Well. Hershael York speaks specifically to pastors to explain how and when to leave a church well. The Enduring Word. This short film from Crossway celebrates God’s providence through the history of Bible translation. Flashback What’s The Point Of Family Devotions? content: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books, so each week I let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. This week brings a substantial new commentary on the Westminster Confession of Faith from a whole team of Reformed scholars, an updated edition of a well-known apologetics book, a couple of books for kids, and a new edition of the ESV. In each case, I’ve included the publisher’s description. (This is a new feature I trialed last week. The response was positive, so I’m going to keep it going. I have tried to improve the format and layout to make it easier to read.) Books for Everyone Crossway The Westminster Confession of Faith A Comprehensive Commentary on Its History, Theology, and Application Edited by J. V. Fesko, John R. Muether, and D. Blair Smith Endorsed by: Joel R. Beeke, Michael Horton, Keith A. Mathison, Robert Letham, and Jonathan L. Master Publisher’s description What is Reformed theology? In 1646, a group of theologians composed what is arguably the most comprehensive statement of faith, the Westminster Confession. Their efforts to preserve Protestant theology against opposing beliefs endured. Today, amid growing interest in Reformed Christianity, the Westminster Confession remains an indispensable guide for living out doctrine, worship, and church governance sola Scriptura, “by Scripture alone.” This essential collection of essays presents an accessible guide to the Westminster Confession of Faith for 21st-century readers. Each chapter is devoted to a section of the historic document, carefully studying its context, its significance to the faith, and its application, as well as any controversies. Clear, thorough explanations of principles, including the Trinity, creation, providence, baptism, last judgment, and more, make this the definitive guide on Reformed Christian doctrine. The essays are written by faculty from Reformed Theological Seminary in their areas of expertise, ensuring a trustworthy and high-quality text for church leaders, teachers and students of theology, and laypeople. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . Crossway I Don’t Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist Updated Edition Norman L. Geisler and Frank Turek Endorsed by: Gavin Ortlund, Sean McDowell, Gregory Koukl, Alisa Childers, and Josh Howerton Publisher’s description To some, the concept of having faith in a higher power or a set of religious beliefs is nonsensical. Indeed, many view religion in general, and Christianity in particular, as unfounded and unreasonable. Frank Turek and Norman Geisler argue, however, that Christianity is not only more reasonable than all other belief systems but is indeed more rational than unbelief itself. With conviction and clear thinking, Turek and Geisler guide readers through some of the traditional, tested arguments for the existence of a creator God. They move into an examination of the source of morality and the reliability of the New Testament accounts concerning Jesus. The final section of the book deals with a detailed investigation of the claims of Christ. This updated volume with fresh arguments will be an interesting read for those skeptical about Christianity, as well as a helpful resource for Christians seeking to articulate a more sophisticated defense of their faith. Buy it at Amazon . Baker Books Giver of All Good God as the Beginning and End of Ethics Chase R. Kuhn Publisher’s description Where do our ethics come from? Are they based on unchanging realities or subject to revision as human culture develops and changes? What distinguishes Christian ethics from other moral claims? And how can Christians engage these questions with clarity and confidence—without either abandoning their convictions or abandoning the conversation? In Giver of All Good , Chase R. Kuhn argues that the answer begins not with ourselves—our feelings, our culture, our moral intuitions—but with God. What we believe about God shapes how we live. Our theology guides
content_zh: 星期二是大多数出版商发行新书的一天,所以每周我都会告诉你,我最密切地关注的出版商刚刚给我们带来了什么。 本周来自整群改革派学者对"威斯敏斯特信仰的忏悔"(Westminster Confession of Faith)提出了实质性的新评论,并更新了一出名作"通俗小说"(Apologetics Book),一出给孩子们的几本书和一出"ESV"的新版本. 每一次,我都包括出版商的描述。 (这是上星期我试演的新节目) 回应是积极的, 我努力改进格式和布局,使其更容易阅读。 ) 由J. V. Fesko、John R. Muether和D. Blair Smith编辑, 乔尔·R·比克、Michael Horton、Keith A. Mathison、Robert Letham和Jonathan L. Master Publishers对改革神学的描述。 1646年,一群神学家组成了可以说是最全面的信仰声明"威斯敏斯特忏悔". 他们努力保护新教神学,反对对立的信仰。 如今,在对改革后的基督教越来越感兴趣的情况下,威斯敏斯特忏悔仍然是“仅靠圣经”活出学说、崇拜和教会治理的不可或缺的指南。 这份重要的散文集为21世纪的读者提供了威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔的可获取指南. 每一章都专门讨论历史文件的一节,仔细研究其背景、其对信仰的意义、其应用以及任何争议。 对原则,包括"三一","创造","天赐","受洗","最后的判断"等进行明确,彻底的解释,使这成为"改革后基督教学说"的决定性指南. 论文由改革神学院的教师在其专业领域撰写,确保教会领导人、神学教师和学生以及外行者能够获得可靠和高质量的文本。 在亚马逊或威斯敏斯特书店买的 Crossway I don't have enough Faith to be an Atheist 更新版 Norman L. Geisler and Frank Turek 由加文·奥尔特伦德,肖恩·麦克道威尔,格雷戈里·库克尔,艾莉莎·柴尔德斯和乔什·豪尔顿出版商的描述认可 对一些人来说,对更高权力或一套宗教信仰有信仰的概念是没有意识的. 事实上,许多人认为,一般宗教,特别是基督教,是毫无根据和不合理的。 然而,弗兰克·图雷克和诺曼·盖斯勒(Norman Geisler)认为,基督教不仅比所有其他信仰体系更合理,而且确实比不信本身更合理. 以信念和清晰的思考,图雷克和盖斯勒指导读者通过一些传统的,经过考验的关于创造出神存在的论点. 他们开始研究道德渊源和"新约"中有关耶稣的叙述的可靠性. 该书的最后一节详细论述对基督的主张的调查. 这本附有新论点的增订本,对于那些对基督教持怀疑态度的人来说,将是一个有趣的读物,也是基督教徒寻求更尖端地捍卫其信仰的有用资源。 在亚马逊买的 Baker Books of All Good God的出品人作为伦理学的开始和结束 Chase R. Kuhn出版社的描述 我们的道德从何而来? 它们是建立在不断变化的现实基础上,还是随着人类文化的发展和变化而需要加以修改? 基督教道德与其他道德主张有什么区别? 基督徒如何以明确和自信的方式处理这些问题,而不放弃他们的信念或放弃对话? Chase R. Kuhn指出,答案不是从我们自己开始的——我们的感情、我们的文化和我们的道德直觉——而是从上帝开始的。 我们对上帝的信仰 塑造了我们的生活 我们的神学指南

content: Good morning from somewhere in rural Colorado. I’m here for the next few days for meetings and training, as well as a bit of hiking and photography and, best of all, some quiet times of writing. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include O. Palmer Robertson’s two-part Christ of the Consummation , which was commended by, among others, D.A. Carson, Sinclair Ferguson, and Joel Beeke. You’ll also find lots of great deals from Zondervan from books that are related to Protestant theology. Recommended Reading Can a Christian Be Demon-Possessed? I know there are many people who are concerned that, even though they are Christians, they may still be possessed by demons. Anthony Faggiano explains why that is not a legitimate fear. “Desire entices us; yielding gives birth to sin; sin grows toward death. Satan can tempt us, but we remain responsible for our desires and decisions. We cannot blame an indwelling demon for what Scripture traces to our sinful hearts. Yet God hasn’t left believers powerless. Through his Holy Spirit, we can begin to put sin to death and walk in obedience.” 7 Keys for Thriving in Lifelong Ministry. I enjoyed reading Joel Beeke’s keys for thriving in pastoral ministry. “Looking back over my ministry over the long term is much more encouraging than looking at it in the short term. A long-term perspective helps me see those who have been saved by the Spirit through my sermons, those marriages that have been strengthened, and even the fruitfulness of elders and deacons who were unsaved when I arrived at my church 40 years ago but have since come to know the Lord personally, vibrantly, and experientially.” Why Does Everyone Else’s Life Seem Better Than Mine? There are some good insights in Zachary Conover’s article on comparison and envy. “Comparison has a way of making us dissatisfied with things we once received with gratitude. We can be thankful for our homes, our families, our work, and the opportunities God has given us. But then we see someone else’s life. We scroll through reel after reel, and suddenly our own begins to feel inadequate. Their opportunities seem greater. Their accomplishments seem more significant. Their circumstances seem more desirable. Am I the only one who doesn’t have it all together? Why don’t I have what they have? And without realizing it, we begin to measure the goodness of God toward us against what He has given to someone else.” Put the Destination in the Frame. John Seel has a guest piece on Aaron Renn’s Substack that offers some helpful points on the way we talk about young men. “We are talking about men incorrectly. We frame discussions of men in terms of problems – the ‘crisis of boys and men’ or ‘failure to launch’ – rather than the destination we want men to arrive at. If we want a different outcome, we need to change the frame of our discussions about men to center on the new reality we want to create. We need a frame that naturally leads us to answer the key question: What kind of men do we want our boys to become?” Welcome to the Valley of Pain. This article from The Atlantic points out, correctly, that the “safe internet” is shrinking and that we need to be more vigilant than ever. “For the next year or two, if not longer, the internet is going to feel a bit touch and go, and more dangerous than we’ve come to expect. ‘It’s going to feel like the sky is falling’ for a while, Prince said. There’s a decades-long backlog of bugs in software written without much review or scrutiny—which was more or less fine so long as there was a very small number of skilled hackers. Over the past two decades, companies, governments, and individuals have been lulled into a false sense of security: Most people don’t think twice about punching credit-card numbers into the website of a local restaurant or gift shop, or forking over a home address and phone number in just about any customer survey. But the internet was always a dangerous place. We’re just waking up from a trance.” Adoption Is Not a T

content: I recently spent a couple of weeks preparing a great deal of fresh material for a weekend-long marriage seminar. Along the way, I often found myself convicted by the content I was preparing. As I readied myself to teach others, I had to consider the ways in which I needed to be a student before I should be a teacher. One area this proved true was intimacy in marriage—but a kind of intimacy I think many of us seldom consider. There is no doubt that marriage is meant to involve a husband and wife baring their bodies before one another, so that marriage is the context in which a man and woman can experience what it is to be naked and unashamed—to be fully bared, yet fully accepted. And because marriage is meant to be the deepest kind of unity two human beings can experience, it makes sense that there is a physical component to it through which two bodies are literally joined together. This is usually what we mean when we discuss intimacy in marriage. It is my understanding that this kind of intimacy, while real, is also in a way representative or symbolic. It is a demonstration of a unity between two people that is not merely body-deep , but fully soul-deep. Physical intimacy is both significant and essential to marriage, but it is not meant to be the sum total of the intimacy shared between a husband and wife. Yet as Aileen and I have interacted with other couples, we have observed that many husbands and wives find it easier to bare their bodies than their souls. Even as they routinely give themselves to one another physically, they can withhold a great deal relationally and emotionally. Even as they give themselves in free and joyful lovemaking, they can stop short of a greater baring, which is the baring of their souls and the revealing of the deep recesses of their hearts. As Aileen and I discussed this together, we had to conclude that this is something we are prone to as well. It’s not that we hold back shocking secrets or scandalous sins that would cause the other to recoil in dismay or disgust. It’s that we are both reserved people who find it hard to let another person in. We are both wounded people who have been hurt by those who have misused information we have revealed to them. And then I suppose we are both prideful or distrustful people who hold back the pieces of ourselves that we think might cause the other person to lower their respect for us. But by holding back, we are failing to live with full transparency and, therefore, failing to live with full intimacy. The baring of our bodies exceeds the baring of our souls. There is an irony to this, because I am convinced there is a deep longing within each of us to be known. We want someone else to know us as we truly are and to still love us and give us their approval. But even while we want it on one level, we resist it on another, because we wonder what that other person will think of us if they know our deep thoughts, our secret longings, and our hidden fears. We wonder if they will still respect us if they know what causes us to feel shame or express remorse. Perhaps we doubt they’ll still love us if they know who we are far beneath the surface. Still, there is this longing to be known, to be as bare emotionally as we can be physically—and still to be loved and accepted. It is this longing that we never address when we hold back from revealing who and what we truly are, when we refuse to foster a deep soul intimacy—an intimacy that is then represented by, rather than superseded by, sexual intimacy. So how can we foster this kind of baring? By letting our spouse really know us, which may mean creating times and contexts for lengthy, deep, and uninterrupted conversation. This will involve asking good questions and then listening attentively so we can come to a correct rather than trite or hasty understanding of what is being communicated. To really know and be known is the work of a lifetime. It is work, but work worth committing to. By assuring one another that no
content_zh: 我最近花了几周时间 准备了大量的新材料 为周末的婚姻研讨会。 一路走来,我常常发现自己被我准备的内容定罪. 当我准备去教别人时,我不得不在做教师之前考虑我需要成为学生的方式。 婚姻中的亲密关系是事实, 毫无疑问,婚姻意味着丈夫和妻子在彼此面前禁止其身体,因此,婚姻是男女能够体验裸体和无羞无耻——被完全禁止,但却被完全接受的背景。 因为婚姻是两个人类能够经历的最深层次的团结,所以它有一个物理成分,通过它,两个身体可以真正结合在一起。 这通常是我们讨论婚姻亲密关系时的意思. 我的理解是,这种亲密关系虽然是真实的,但在某种程度上也是有代表性的或象征性的。 它表明两个人之间的团结 不仅仅是身体深处,而且是灵魂深处 肉体亲密关系对婚姻既重要又重要,但并非夫妻共有亲密关系的总和。 然而,随着艾琳和我与其他夫妇的互动,我们观察到,许多丈夫和妻子发现露出自己的身体比灵魂更容易. 即使在他们习惯上互相施舍的时候,他们也可以在感情上和感情上保持相当的克制。 即使在他们自由而欢快地做爱时,他们也可以停止更大的禁酒,这就是他们的灵魂被束缚,以及他们内心深处的沉睡。 正如我和艾琳一起讨论的那样,我们不得不得出结论,这也是我们容易看到的。 并不是我们隐瞒令人震惊的秘密或可耻的罪恶, 我们都是有保留的人, 我们都是被滥用我们所透露的信息的人所伤害的受伤者。 然后我想,我们都是骄傲或不信任的人,他们屏蔽着我们自己的碎片,我们认为这可能会使他人降低对我们的尊重. 但是,通过阻挠,我们没有完全透明地生活,因此,没有完全亲密地生活。 身体的阻断 超过了灵魂的阻断 这一点具有讽刺意味,因为我相信,我们每个人都有很深的渴望要知道。 我们希望其他人了解我们的真实身份,仍然爱我们,并给予我们批准。 但是,即使我们希望在一个层次上,我们抵制另一个层次,因为我们想知道,如果其他人知道我们的深思熟虑,我们的秘密渴望,以及我们隐藏的恐惧,我们会怎么想。 我们想知道,如果他们知道是什么使我们感到羞愧或表示悔恨,他们是否仍然尊重我们。 也许我们怀疑如果他们知道我们是谁, 然而,人们仍渴望知道这一点,希望我们能像身体上那样裸露出情感——仍然希望得到爱和接受。 正是这种渴望,当我们不愿透露我们真正是谁和什么时,当我们拒绝培养一种深厚的灵魂亲密关系时,我们从未谈到这种渴望——这种亲密关系由性亲密关系而不是取而代之。 那么,我们如何促进这种酒吧? 通过让我们的配偶真正了解我们,这可能意味着为冗长、深入和不间断的对话创造时间和背景。 这将涉及提出好的问题,然后认真倾听,以便我们能够对所传达的内容有一个正确而不是老练或仓促的理解。 真正知道和被了解是一生的工作。 这是工作,但值得致力于工作。 互相保证不会

content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Sales & Deals If all goes well, today’s Kindle deals should include several important books that deal with a Christian understanding of science. Westminster Books is offering a deal this week on the two-part John Calvin’s Illustrated Institutes , which drives the price as low as 50% off. Recommended Reading This Is Roman Catholicism. Here’s a tremendous new project from the Reformanda Initiative—a free documentary series that “offers a firsthand look at often-overlooked yet integral aspects of Roman Catholic theology and practice, challenging idealized perceptions of Rome and encouraging informed, biblical discernment—particularly among those drawn to it. This docuseries is made primarily for Protestant Christians who want to understand what Rome teaches and practices. Featuring: Leonardo De Chirico, Mark Dever, Kevin DeYoung, Albert Mohler, Lauren Montenegro, and Michael Reeves.” Three Ways to Walk With Those Who Grieve. Kirsten Black outlines three ways that any of us can walk faithfully and compassionately with those who are in a time of deep grief. “Often, we do not know how to step into spaces of loss. There is a beautiful and godly desire to bring comfort, yet when facing the reality of walking with the grieving, we are also confronted with the limits of the comfort we can actually offer. This holy work often brings with it an acute awareness of how easy it is to say the wrong thing and unintentionally add more pain to the one who is already suffering.” Explore the Reformation in Ligonier’s Grow App . The Protestant Reformation was not a minor theological dispute—it was a recovery of the biblical gospel. With Reformation Day coming this Saturday, you can explore a variety of free Reformation-themed teaching series with R.C. Sproul in the Grow app from Ligonier Ministries. Download the app and study the five solas , the life of Martin Luther, and much more. (Sponsored) 5 Ways Men Can Serve the Church & 5 Ways Women Can Serve the Church. A pair of articles from Ligonier Ministries offers distinct and meaningful ways that both men and women can serve within the local church. Christian Universalism Is Alive (Just Go to a Funeral). Yes, I have observed as well that funerals are the events where we are most likely to see evidence of Christian universalism. “I’ve been to many funerals and memorial services in my life, and through the years, I’ve encountered religious people who give off the impression that they believe everyone goes to heaven. Culture gives the same impression. Words reveal worldviews. The deceased person may not have received Christ by faith, may not have gone to church, may have even lived an unrepentant and selfish life, and some people still seem to assume they went to a ‘better place’ or went to heaven. Might Christian Universalism be more prevalent than we think?” Stinginess and the Generosity of God. Randy Alcorn contrasts the stinginess of human beings—and even Christian human beings—with the generosity of God. “A life characterized by greed and stinginess is neither Spirit-filled nor Christlike — nor is it happy. If we know Jesus, we will become more and more like our generous God.” Unclear Evangelism Leads to Unclear (And False) Conversions. Writing for 9Marks, John Lee explains how unclear evangelism can lead to false conversions. “When we are unclear about the urgency of conversion, the cost of conversion, or the accountability that should accompany conversion, we risk leaving people deceived about their eternal state. Ultimately, our job is simply to proclaim the gospel clearly, trust God to open people’s hearts to the truth, and provide ongoing discipleship to those who respond in repentance and faith.” Reader Recommendations Once a week, I like to ask what you enjoy and recommend. What books, products, videos, sites, or other experiences do you recommend to others who read this blog/newsletter? Let me know, and I’ll share a collection on Saturday. (If you’re
content_zh: 早上好,你好吗? 格蕾丝和平安 销售和交易 如果一切顺利,今天的Kindle交易应该包括几本重要书籍,涉及基督教对科学的理解。 威斯敏斯特图书公司本周在约翰·加尔文两地的Illustrated Institutes提供一笔交易, 推荐阅读 这是罗马天主教。 以下是Reformanda倡议的一个巨大的新项目,这是一部免费的纪录片系列,“第一手看一看罗马天主教神学和实践中经常被高瞻远瞩但不可分割的方面,挑战对罗马理想化的看法,并鼓励知情的、圣经上的分辨——特别是在那些被吸引的人中。 这种道克系列主要为新教基督徒所制作,他们想了解罗马的教义和实践. 表演:莱昂纳多·德·奇里科、马克·德维尔、凯文·德杨、阿尔伯特·莫勒、劳伦·黑山和迈克尔·里夫斯。” 柯尔斯滕·布莱克概述了我们中任何人都能与那些处于极度悲痛的时代的人们忠实而富有同情心地行走的三种方式. “当然,我们不知道如何进入损失空间。 有一种美丽而神通地渴望带来舒适,然而当面对与悲伤相伴而行的现实时,我们也面临着我们实际所能提供的舒适的限度. 这种神圣的工作往往使人们敏锐地意识到说错话是多么容易,无意中给已经遭受痛苦的人增加了更多的痛苦。” 探索Ligonier Grow App的改造。 新教改革并不是一个小的神学纠纷——这是圣经福音的收复. 随着本周六的改造日的到来,你可以在利戈尼耶各部的"成长"应用中,与R.C.Sproul一起探索各种自由改造主题的教学系列. 下载应用程序并研究五索拉斯, 马丁路德的生活,还有更多。 (赞助) 5 道:男人可以为教会服务 5道:女人可以为教会服务. 利戈尼耶各部的一对文章提供了独特而有意义的方法,男女都可以在地方教会中服务。 基督教世界主义是活的(去葬礼吧). 是的,我也注意到,葬礼是我们最有可能看到基督教普遍主义证据的事件。 「我一生中参加过许多葬礼和追悼会, 文化也给人同样的印象。 语出出世相. 死者可能没有信仰接受基督,可能没有去教堂,甚至过着不悔改和自私的生活,有些人似乎仍然认为他们去了"更好的地方"或去天堂. 基督教世界主义会比我们想象的更盛行吗? 坚忍与神通相. Randy Alcorn将人类的吝啬——甚至基督教人类——与上帝的慷慨相提并论。 “一种以贪婪和吝啬为特点的生活既不是充满精神,也不是基督般的,也不是幸福的。 如果我们了解耶稣,我们将越来越像我们慷慨的上帝。” unclear Evangelism 引出unclear(和假)转换. 写作为9马克斯,约翰·李(John Lee)解释不清楚的福音会如何导致虚假的转换. “当我们不清楚转换的迫切性、转换的成本或与转换相关的问责制时,我们有可能让人们对其永恒状态受到欺骗。 归根结底,我们的工作只是明确宣示福音,相信上帝为人们打开真理的心扉,为那些以忏悔和信仰回应的人不断提供弟子之道". 读者建议 每周一次 我想问问你喜欢什么 推荐什么 你推荐哪些书籍、产品、视频、网站或其他经验给阅读博客/通讯的其他人? 让我知道, (如果你是的话)

summary_zh: 本周的工作与奇迹：上帝的智慧和力量瞄准了我们的好处，环游地球7.5小时的旅程，顶级野生动物照片，鸟类广播和新歌。另请参阅作品与奇观（ 10月11日）作品与奇观（ 9月27日）作品与奇观（ 8月30日）
title_zh: 作品和奇迹： 10月25日
content: In my weekly Works & Wonders column, I combine a brief devotional with other interesting and uplifting bits and pieces I gleaned throughout the week. I hope you enjoy this week’s collection! It includes: What a God We Serve! (A Devotional) Ambient Earth Wildlife Photographer of the Year What Animals Can You Outrun? Who Would Have Dreamed 🎵 Bird Radio Who Is Like the Lord? 🎵 1. What a God We Serve! God has wisdom to know what is best and wisdom to know how to accomplish it by the best possible means. He also has power to execute it all. But we may wonder, as it pertains to us, what is his will? What does his wisdom determine is best? What is he accomplishing through the execution of his power? The book of Romans contains words of tremendous comfort: “And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose” (Romans 8:28). God’s will is our good, which means that God’s wisdom and power are directed at accomplishing what is ultimately for our good, and accomplishing it all in the best ways. All the things we experience, all the things we undergo, all the things we endure, all the things we celebrate and lament, the things that make us laugh and cry—all of them are born of God’s love, directed at our good, and executed in a way that is nothing short of perfect. What a God we serve! And what a God we worship today. 2. Ambient Earth Ambient Earth is a great project! A guy named Seán Doran took 49,000 of Butch Wilmore’s photos taken aboard the International Space Station, then repaired, remastered, and retimed them to create an incredible 7.5-hour, 4K journey around the earth. He also added Chris Hadfield’s recording of the sounds of the ISS, which honestly gets a bit annoying, so you may want to mute it and then put on some nice instrumental music in its place. This is a great video to just leave playing on a TV in a public place. (While we’re on the subject of Butch Wilmore, he’s a believer and recently wrote Stuck in Space , which you may enjoy.) 3. Wildlife Photographer of the Year I always enjoy a good photography contest and, for whatever reason, this is the time of the year when many of them announce their winners. That’s the case with the Wildlife Photographer of the Year contest, which had 65,000 entries from 121 countries and territories. That link leads to The Atlantic ‘s gallery of highlights, though if you prefer to see the official site, you can find it here . As you’d expect, many of the photos are nothing short of stunning. 4. What Animals Can You Outrun? I suppose we all wonder at one time or another whether we would be able to outrun certain animals. The BBC did some research to find out which animals we’d possibly be able to outrun and the ones we definitely wouldn’t. Overall, the news isn’t particularly good. It’s a good thing God made us smart, since he didn’t make us particularly fast. See: The animals you can’t outrun – and the ones you can . 5. Who Would Have Dreamed Over a decade ago, Sovereign Grace Music released a Christmas album titled Prepare Him Room . I guess they have dusted off that album and decided to give it new life by recording a live version of it. I’m glad they’ve done so, because it has some really good songs on it. My favorite, and one we sing seasonally at Grace Fellowship Church, is also the first track they’ve re-released: “ Who Would Have Dreamed .” 6. Bird Radio Bird Radio is a neat concept—you simply tune in to hear the calls of different birds from all around the world. God displays his creativity in many different ways and the sheer variety of bird calls is a pretty impressive one. (Also on the subject of birds, did you know the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service maintains a feather atlas so you can learn about the ones you happen to find?) 7. Bonus: Who Is Like the Lord? content: Good morning. This Weekend edition of A La Carte has some long-form content, some think pieces, some lists of the most popular articles from the week gone by, and a whole collection of recommendations from readers like you. Enjoy! Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include books on sexuality, forgiveness, Habakkuk, Revelation, and more. Recommended Reading Not everyone is familiar with the term concupiscence , but most of us are familiar with some of the debates surrounding it. For example, are our unholy desires sinful, or is it only sinful to act out on those desires? This question often arises when we discuss same-sex attraction. Writing for Logos, Mark Jones explores the concept of concupiscence from a Reformed perspective. In brief, concupiscence (concupiscentia) originates from the Latin verb concupisco, which means ‘to ardently desire.’ There are proper, non-sinful forms of desire, which we would call ‘non-sinful concupiscence.’ For example, Jesus said to his disciples, ‘I have earnestly desired [ἐπεθύμησα] to eat this Passover with you before I suffer’ (Luke 22:15). But because we live in a fallen world, concupiscence typically has in view sinful desire, and usually in reference to sinful sexual desires. Because sin is the privation (lack) of righteousness and proneness to evil, concupiscence involves not just the acts but the desire of the person. Sinful concupiscence can be understood from God’s moral law: ‘You shall not covet’ (Exod 20:17). Concupiscence: Are Our Unholy Desires Sinful? The Guardian tells a strange and twisting tale of a death, a scandal, and a desire for revenge, which it summarizes like this: “After his mother died, Otto became convinced he’d been wronged by the forensic investigators – and that one of them was a fraud. The truth was even stranger.” Here’s how the article begins: On a balmy, quiet evening in June 2020, Otto’s elderly mother, Doria, was fading in her Munich apartment. As she lay with her eyes closed, her pale face, framed by her white hair, was calm. Otto, masked, gloved and draped in a sterile apron, dozed in a chair beside her. Otto, who sometimes goes by the name Rainer, and whose last name is only known as “Z” because of Germany’s strict privacy laws, was a doctor who had cared for his mother for years, ever since she had suffered a stroke and moved in with him. He described the course of that night to me. He woke to the sound of her short breath and tried to sit her upright. Her eyes were shut, and her lips pursed. She stopped breathing. Otto reached for his phone to call for help, but then Doria opened her eyes and stared into his. She smiled, drew one last deep breath, shut her eyes again, and lay still. A Death, a Plagiarism Scandal and a Quest for Revenge: The Bizarre Tale of Otto Z. Jonathon Van Maren sees Beatrix Potter as an example of true conservatism, and explains why that’s the case in a really interesting article about the life of someone whose work we are probably all familiar with. There is a type of academic who can only get noticed by attacking the legacies of greater men and women, and a prime example was cited by Matthew Dennison in The Spectator in his essay “Don’t Cancel Beatrix Potter.” The beloved children’s author has become the target of “specialist in postcolonial literature” Dr. Emily Zobel Marshall, who hilariously claims that Potter failed “to acknowledge her indebtedness to an oral storytelling tradition of enslaved Africans working on American plantations” and that this contributes to “a damaging and recurring appropriation of Black cultural forms that continues today.” This is frivolous stuff, and Marshall’s claims are a parasitic attempt to gain fifteen minutes of fame by slandering a woman who cannot defend herself. Dennison handily rebuts Marshall, and I’m glad he did—but I can’t help but think that fortunately, some writers are uncancellable. Potter’s books have sold 250 million copies. content_zh: 早上好,你好吗? 这本周末版的A La Carte 有一些长式内容,一些思想作品,一些周来最受欢迎的文章列表,还有你这样的读者提出的一整套建议. 慢慢来! 今天的销售和交易包括性、宽恕、哈巴克克、启示录等书籍。 建议阅读 并非每个人都熟悉“巧妙”一词, 例如,我们的恶性欲望是有罪的,还是只对这些欲望采取行动是有罪的? 这个问题经常在我们讨论同性吸引力时出现. 为Logos写作,马克·琼斯从改革的视角探索了巧妙的概念. 简而言之,康克塞克语(concupiscentia)起源于拉丁语动词concupisco,意为"强烈的欲望". 我们称之为“无耻的谦虚”。 例如,耶稣对他的门徒说:我的确希望在我受苦之前与你们一起吃这个逾越节。 但是,因为我们生活在一个堕落的世界中,巧妙通常会考虑到罪恶的欲望,通常会提到罪恶的性欲望。 因为罪恶是正义被剥夺(黑暗),容易被邪恶所侵扰,所以巧妙的行为不仅涉及行为,而且涉及人的欲望. 从上帝的道德法则可以理解罪恶的欺骗: " 你不应该贪婪 " (20:17). 混淆:我们的不祥愿望是否有罪? 《卫报》讲述了一个奇怪而曲折的死亡、丑闻和复仇欲望的故事,它这样总结道 : “ 在他母亲死后,奥托开始相信自己被法医调查人员冤枉了 — — 其中一人是骗子。 真相甚至是陌生的。” 以下是文章的开头: 2020年6月,奥托的年长母亲多莉亚正在慕尼黑的公寓中消亡。 当她闭上眼睛躺下时,被她白发所陷的她苍白的脸色是平静的. Otto被蒙上面具 被手套并被涂上不育的围裙 睡在她旁边的椅子上 奥托有时取名"雷纳"(Rainer),由于德国严格的隐私法,他的姓只被称作"Z",自她中风后一直和他一起住入,他是一个照顾他母亲多年的医生. 他向我描述了那晚的经过。 他醒来时听到她短促的呼吸声,想让她坐直. 她的眼睛被闭上了 嘴唇被包住了 她停止了呼吸。 奥托打电话求救,但后来多莉娅睁开眼睛并盯着他. 她微笑了,画了最后一口深呼吸,又闭上了眼睛,躺了下来。 A Death, a Plagiarism Sandal and a Quest for Evention: The Bizarre Tale of Otto Z. Jonathon Van Maren将Beatrix Potter视为真正保守主义的典范, 并解释为什么在一篇非常有趣的文章中会出现这种情况, 有一类学者只能通过攻击大男人和大女人的后遗症来引起人们的注意,马修·丹尼斯森在"观察者"一文中引用了"别取消碧翠克丝·波特"中的主要例子. " 后殖民时期文学专家 " 已成为受爱戴的儿童作家的目标。 Emily Zobel Marshall博士幽默地声称波特没有“承认她欠一个口头讲故事的传统,即在美国种植园工作的被奴役的非洲人的债”,这助长了“对黑人文化形式的破坏和反复侵吞,这种掠夺今天仍在继续 ” 。 Marshall的主张是企图通过诽谤一个不能自卫的妇女来赢得十五分钟的名声。 我很高兴他这样做了, 但我不禁觉得幸运的是, 一些作家是无法取消的。 波特的书已经售出2.5亿册. 她的遗产很好 她的角色会继续

content: This week’s Free Stuff Friday is sponsored by Ligonier Ministries , who also sponsored the blog this week. Sometimes one word is all that stands between the truth and a lie, between life and death. In the Reformation, that word was sola , “alone.” At a time when leaders in the church claimed to speak for God, the Protestant Reformers reminded God’s people that Scripture alone is our infallible authority. While many people sought to work their way to heaven, the Reformers boldly proclaimed the only true gospel: salvation is by God’s grace alone, through faith alone, in Christ alone, to the glory of God alone. Today, Ligonier Ministries is offering The Heart of the Reformation , a 90-day devotional exploring the five solas , as a free ebook for Challies readers. Download your copy to discover how these core biblical truths display the reliability of God’s Word and the depths of His mercy, helping you grow in faith day by day. In addition, ten Free Friday winners will receive a paperback edition of The Heart of the Reformation . Learn more about The Heart of the Reformation here. title: Fear Itself
summary: Widow's Bay  and the Trolley Problem of Life   The post  Fear Itself  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
summary_zh: 寡妇湾和生活的手推车问题帖子Fear Itself首先出现在Mockingbird上。
title_zh: 恐惧自身
content: W hat is your biggest fear? Spiders? That’s a classic. Deranged clowns? Sure! Maybe you prefer the more existential variety? How about never fully realizing your potential or dying alone? All of the above? Similar to the What superpower would you choose? question, it is hard for me to select only one. I am a fearful person. I have a way of collecting fears as I go about my life. Alpha-gal, something I did not know existed until two days ago, is the flavor of the week. But my fear of dying alone is more like a longtime, trusted companion. The world is a scary place. At any moment, our identities could be hacked. Our phones could ring with dreadful news. Our brains could suffer an aneurysm. Swimming in a bottomless sea of insecurity, we are meagerly equipped with our basic survival instincts: fight, flight, freeze, and appease. These impulses may help keep us safe from spiders and clowns (answer for both: flight!), but what do we make of the dangers that are harder to pin down? What if the dangers are not only without but within? Leave it to this year’s hit TV series to explore these questions. If you’re looking for a spooky show to get into this weekend, it’s Widow’s Bay. The Emmy-sweeping, genre-bending, horror-comedic series is a triumph for a number of reasons. For starters, it muddles the black-and-white worlds Hollywood has created (e.g., horror movies without humor, comedies without any depth), reminding us that life can be both scary and funny. The show has all the irresistible horror tropes (the harbinger who warns everyone of impending doom, the suspenseful music, the jump scares) but, along with its crowd-pleasing antics, it dives deeper than surface-level fears. Its anthropology is refreshingly low. This is not a match between good people and evil monsters. Yes, sometimes the enemy is a chainsaw-wielding fiend. Much scarier, however, is when the enemy is yourself. Take Tom Loftis, for instance, the ambitious new mayor who wants to transform the cursed island town of Widow’s Bay into the next Martha’s Vineyard. He is, from every angle, a secular man. For Tom, God is no more real than ghosts. The only higher power that exists is the one you achieve by climbing the ladder. He resents how the locals tolerate the town’s haunted reputation. For too long, people have been resigned to the rumors that the hotel is haunted, the church is cursed, and the bay isn’t safe for a swim. For Tom, the only thing to fear is fear itself. Like any mayor with a messiah complex, he sets out to do something about it. As Loftis sees things, the real problem with the place is not that it is demonically possessed. The real problem is bad branding . In his eyes, Widow’s Bay is simply misunderstood. When visiting Widow’s Bay to write a piece for the New York Times travel section, a reporter asks Loftis about a framed article in the historical society titled “Cannibalism in God’s House.” Loftis tries to water it down. “These stories get so exaggerated over time,” he says. “Was there a deadly storm in 1786? Yes. Did a group of people get trapped inside a church? Apparently so. Did they immediately turn to cannibalism? No, that took four days !” See? That’s not so bad, right? Loftis’ PR campaign is like slapping new siding on a haunted mansion. He is convinced that the plight of Widow’s Bay can be solved by installing a proper cappuccino machine in the local coffee shop. Cappuccino machines are great at making a proper latte but pretty useless when up against the occult. Before long, Loftis’ denial of the curse over the island town is just as dangerous as the curse itself. The first step to keeping the forces at bay is to admit they exist. There is a scene in which Loftis speaks to another character about the Trolley Problem, an ethical thought experiment in which there is a runaway trolley barreling down the tracks toward a crowd of people. In this hypothetical setup, there is a lever that would switch the trolley to a different track with only one
content_zh: 帽子是你最大的恐惧? 蜘蛛吗? 这是经典。 疯狂的小丑? 当然! 也许你更喜欢生存的品种? 永远不能充分发挥你的潜力 或孤独地死去怎么样? 所有这一切? 类似于你选择的超级大国? 问,我很难只选一个 我是一个害怕的人。 我有办法收集恐惧 当我去我的生活。 Alpha -gal,我两天前才知道的东西 是这个星期的口味 但我害怕孤独地死去 更像是长期 值得信赖的同伴 世界是个可怕的地方。 我们的身份随时可能被黑入 我们的电话可能会传出可怕的消息 我们的大脑可能会有动脉瘤 在一个不安全的无底海中游来游去,我们装备了我们的基本生存本能:战斗、出逃、冻结和安抚。 这些冲动也许可以帮助我们远离蜘蛛和小丑(回答:飞行!),但我们如何应对那些更难消除的危险? 如果危险不仅是没有危险,而且是内部危险呢? 让今年的电视连续剧来探讨这些问题。 如果你想要一个恐怖的节目进入这个周末, "艾美扫地"(英語:Emmy-sweating, genre-bending),"恐怖喜剧"(英語:Description-comed)系列,由于多种原因,是一场胜利. 首先,它搅乱了好莱坞所创造的黑白世界(例如没有幽默感的恐怖电影,没有任何深度的喜剧),提醒我们生活既会恐怖又会搞笑. 该节目拥有所有不可抗拒的恐怖颤抖(预告会警告所有人即将来临的末日,悬疑的音乐,跳跃的惊吓等),但连同其人群取悦的焦虑,其潜入比地表恐惧更深. 它的人类学水平低得惊人 这不是好人和邪恶怪物的对决 是的,有时敌人是一个 链锯的恶魔。 然而,更可怕的是当敌人是你自己的时候。 以汤姆·洛夫蒂斯(Tom Loftis)为例, 他,从每个角度来说,都是世俗的人. 对汤姆来说,上帝不比鬼更真实. 唯一高的电能是通过攀登梯子实现的. 当地民众如何容忍镇上闹事的名声? 久而久之,人们对旅馆闹鬼、教堂被诅咒、海湾游泳不安全等谣言辞职。 对汤姆来说,唯一害怕的是恐惧本身. 像任何拥有救世主建筑群的市长一样,他开始对此有所行动. 正如洛夫提斯所见 这个地方真正的问题不是 它被恶魔附身 真正的问题是品牌不好 在他眼中,寡妇湾只是被误解了。 当一位记者访问寡妇湾为纽约时报旅行部写出一篇作品时,他问洛夫蒂斯关于历史社会中一篇被设定为“神殿中的食人狂”的文章。 洛夫提斯试图给它浇水 他说,“这些故事随着时间的推移变得如此夸张。” “1786年是否有致命的风暴? 对 一群人被困在教堂里了吗? 显然如此。 他们有没有立即转向吃人? 不,那需要四天时间!” 这还不算太糟吧? Loftis的公关活动就像在闹鬼的豪宅上再拍一拍。 他相信寡妇湾的困境可以通过在当地咖啡店安装适当的卡布奇诺机器来解决。 卡布奇诺机器很擅长做一个正宗的拿铁 但和神秘主义作对时却很没用 不久之后,洛夫蒂斯否认对岛屿城镇的诅咒,与诅咒本身同样危险。 阻止势力存在的第一步是承认它们的存在. 有个场景让洛夫蒂斯向另一个角色讲述了"特罗莱问题"(Trolley Problem),这是一场道德思想实验,其中有一个跑跑的推车管向一行人冲去. 在这个假想的设定中,有一个杠杆,可以把推车换到只有一跑道的另一跑道.
author: Sam Bush

title: A Crazy Train Crying in the Wilderness
summary: Ozzy Osbourne's Plea to Be Heard   The post  A Crazy Train Crying in the Wilderness  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
summary_zh: Ozzy Osbourne的《Pleas to Be Heard》《A Crazy Train Crying in the Wilderness》一文首次出现在《知更鸟》上。
title_zh: 疯狂的火车在荒野中哭泣
content: No matter who won or lost the last big game you attended, chances are, Ozzy Osbourne was there in electronic chains, locked inside a brain-rattling sound system, unnoticed, unnamed, misunderstood, a voice crying in the wilderness of crowded rows of fans desperate for a win, cheering for their heroes while jeering at their opponents, paying too much for unnecessary carbs and calories, possibly on the sabbath day. When Ozzy cried, “All aboard!” you stood with hundreds or thousands of tangential warriors singing along with the fatalistic chorus, air guitaring with the riffs, nodding with the rhythm, but you weren’t there for music. You were there to shout, thump your chest, flex, thrust hands with fingers contorted into symbols of specific allegiance, or claim you’re #1, convinced that the song, the battle cry, and the power behind it all were on your side. The words didn’t matter. Your heroes were fighting for you, to give you hope. You’d fight for them if you could, if you had to, against whoever stands in your way, to win at all costs. But what if that’s not what Ozzy wanted? How do we know what he wanted? He screams, “You’ve got to listen to my words!” Below is a paraphrase of the “Crazy Train” lyrics: “It’s crazy, but it’s always been like this — we’re all living as enemies. But maybe it’s not too late to learn how to love and forget how to hate. We’ve all got mental wounds that aren’t healing. I’m losing it. I’ve listened to everyone — fools, preachers, anarchists. Nothing helps. There’s always a system run by someone who’s a product of the system and has been conditioned to run the system, which is sold to us by rich people who get richer by keeping the system alive. And we buy it, screaming in pain from our open mental wounds. It’s messed up. I’m messed up. We’re all messed up. We inherit each other’s trouble. We’re heirs of unresolved conflict. I keep saying it, but no one listens. You’ve got to listen to my words. I can’t figure out how to feel. The mental wounds don’t heal. I don’t know who to blame, but I know it’s not fair.” I wrote the above paraphrase to read to my senior literature class last Monday morning. Nearly half of the students in the class are varsity football starters chasing championships and full-rides. I prefaced the reading with a white lie, “I got this message from someone you all know over the weekend. I won’t tell you who it is, but I want you to help me think through how to respond.” The starting quarterback, worried, tried to interrupt me. I didn’t look up, held my hand out to pause questions, and continued reading. When I finished, there was a chorus of concern from several voices: That’s a cry for help! Is it from a boy or a girl? You said we know them? Who is it? Did they email you? What did you say? They need help. Who are you going to talk to? Still in character, I said, “I can’t tell you a name, but I’ll play this song.” A few seconds into “Crazy Train,” the students realized what was going on, looked relieved, but then became uncomfortable when I turned down the volume and read out the actual lyrics. In confused silence, their faces said, We weren’t listening . I felt bad. I smiled and apologized for manipulating their emotions, and the air lightened. Someone started singing the chorus, and we moved on. But I’m not sure we should have. “Crazy Train” is the most popular song from the most recognizable sex, drugs, and rock-n-roll villain to ever bite the head off a bat, but it’s also a cry for help from a struggling human admitting personal weakness and claiming no superiority. While suggesting that love is better than hate, he’s doing more than just asking us to love. He’s asking us to LEARN HOW TO. French philosopher and mystic, Simone Weil, who died during World War II in solidarity with residents of German-occupied France, didn’t write how-to books, but she couldn’t stop talking about attention. Her bumper sticker quote, “Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity,” is clippe

title: East Coker and the Cure for Human Inability
summary: "... to be restored, our sickness must grow worse."   The post  East Coker and the Cure for Human Inability  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
summary_zh: “......要恢复，我们的疾病必须变得更糟。“《East Coker and the Cure for Human Inability》一文首次出现在《知更鸟》上。
title_zh: East Coker和治疗人类残疾的方法
content: H ow strange that one can read the same poems countless times and discover new things with each visit, like a traveler coming home for Christmas only to find it slightly altered! It is the same for me revisiting T. S. Eliot’s Four Quartets : the end is different than I imagined in the beginning when I first read these words, imagined these places, and attempted to grasp the author’s meaning. Eliot had the same experience. The meaning of the Four Quartets was one thing when he originally envisioned them, another when he wrote them, and still another when the public began analyzing them. He never believed they would be forever linked with the world’s most destructive war. He had not even known there would be four. In the beginning, there was only “Burnt Norton,” written in 1936 and intended to be a one-off. It was generally well received by critics, and the whole business could have been over then. But three years passed, and Eliot found himself with that most common of authorly ailments: not knowing what to write or fearing that he no longer knew how to write properly. Specifically, he had gone for some time without constructing new poems. The world had changed since “Burnt Norton” was published. A growing menace once possible to ignore had exploded into a firestorm of destructive force sweeping through the nations of Europe, consuming all in its path. The bonds that had knit together what remained of Western Christian civilization were snapping with wild abandon, supplanted by ideologies of extermination. Faced with such a crisis, Eliot searched for the one fixed point amid the whirling chaos. He settled on the village of East Coker in Somerset, England. His ancestor Andrew Eliot had left there in 1669, abandoning the historic family home and immigrating to New England. Nearly three centuries later, Thomas Stearns Eliot had become the first member of the family to move back to the motherland, and the family connection held spiritual significance for him. In 1937, he visited St. Michael and All Angels’ Church in East Coker, where his ashes would one day be placed. I know something of Eliot’s experience. I too am the descendant of Englishmen and women whose bones lie buried in every corner of that land, some in tombs I have visited. I too was the first person in my family to return and live in England, if only for a year. It did feel in a sense like returning to my beginning, which is probably why I connect so strongly with the Four Quartets . The secret Eliot discovered at East Coker is one that has transformed my own life as well: we do not possess the power to redeem ourselves or the world and are utterly dependent on the gift of grace. Of all the Four Quartets , this is the most law and gospel poem. The Four Quartets are commonly associated with the four traditional elements of the physical world: air, earth, water, and fire. But as I have noted, Eliot did not begin with a grand plan, so the elemental symbolism becomes stronger in the later poems. Yes, we see the movement of air in “Burnt Norton” disturbing a bowl of rose leaves and carrying the laughter of children, but you would not conclude “This is an air poem” unless you had the other three Quartets to guide you. Likewise, the earth theme is not obvious after the first section of “East Coker,” but once we get to “The Dry Salvages,” we will be drowned in water imagery, and “Little Gidding” will pelt us with fire from beginning to end. Thus, Eliot begins “East Coker” rooted in the earth, in time and place and home. But immediately, the earth is overturned by the machinations of human societies succeeding and supplanting one another, building up to heaven and returning to dust. In my beginning is my end. In succession Houses rise and fall, crumble, are extended, Are removed, destroyed, restored, or in their place Is an open field, or a factory, or a by-pass. If you have visited the ancient monument of Stonehenge on Salisbury Plain, you know it sits at a motorway intersecti
content_zh: 奇怪的是,人们可以阅读同名诗作无数次,每次拜访都会发现新的事物,就像一个旅行者回家过圣诞节,只为了发现它略有改变! 我同样重温了T. S. Eliot的四重奏:结局和我最初读到这些话、想象这些地方并试图理解作者含义时所想象的不一样。 Eliot也有同样的经历. 四重奏的意义是他最初设想它们的时候是一回事,他写它们的时候是另一回事,当公众开始分析它们的时候仍然是另一回事. 他从未相信它们会永远与世界上最具破坏性的战争联系在一起。 他甚至不知道会有四个。 一开始只有"伯恩特·诺顿"(Burnt Norton,作于1936年)一作一作一作一想. 它普遍受到批评者的好评,整个业务本来可以到那时结束. 但三年过去了,艾略特发现自己与最常见的作者病症相伴:不知道该写什么,或担心自己不再知道如何正确写作. 具体地说,他已经走了一段时间,没有创作出新诗. 自“Burnt Norton”出版以来,世界发生了变化。 日益严重的威胁一旦可能被忽视,就已演变成一股由毁灭性力量横扫欧洲各国并吞噬其道路的火焰。 将西方基督教文明遗留下来的东西联系起来的纽带,被被灭绝思想所取代而疯狂地抛弃了。 面对这样的危机,埃利奥特在旋转的混乱中寻找一个固定点. 他定居于英格兰萨默塞特的东科克村. 他的祖先安德鲁·埃利奥特于1669年离开那里,放弃了有历史意义的家族家园并移民到新英格兰. 近3个世纪后,托马斯·斯蒂恩斯·埃利奥特成为了第一个搬回祖国的家庭成员,家庭联系对他具有了精神意义. 1937年,他参观了东科克的圣迈克尔和All Angels教堂,在那里有一天他的骨灰会被放置. 我知道Eliot的经验。 我也是英国男人和女人的后人 他们的骨头埋在这片土地的每一个角落, 一些在我的访问过的坟墓。 我也是我家里第一个回到英国生活的人 哪怕只有一年 我确实感觉回到我的开始, 这可能是为什么我如此紧密地与四重奏联系起来。 Eliot在东科克发现的秘密 也改变了我自己的生活: 我们没有拯救自己或世界的能力, 完全依赖恩赐。 在所有四重奏中,这是最有法律和福音的诗. 四重奏通常与物理世界的四大传统元素相通:空气,地,水,火. 但正如我所指出,艾略特并没有从一个宏伟的计划入手,因此元素符号主义在后期诗作中变得更加强大. 是的,我们看到“Burnt Norton”中的空气运动扰乱了一碗玫瑰叶并带了孩子们的笑声,但除非有另外三个四方来指导你,否则你不会得出“这是一首空气诗”的结论。 同样地,在第一部分“东科克”之后,地球主题并不明显,但一旦我们到达“干涸的盐水”,我们将被水上图像所淹没,而“小吉丁”将从头到尾向我们开火。 因此,Eliot开始“东科克”扎根于地球、时间、地点和家园。 但是,立即,人类社会的成功和取而代之的诡计推翻了地球,使地球升入天堂并回到了尘土中。 在我开始的时候,就是我的结局。 房屋的起伏、倒塌、被延长、被拆除、被摧毁、被恢复或取代,都是空地、工厂或旁道。 如果你曾参观过萨利斯伯里平原上古老的巨石阵纪念碑 你知道它坐落在一条相交的公路上

title: A Few Thoughts on 300 Episodes of Grace (and Its Absence)
summary: Fun, Forgiveness, and Death   The post  A Few Thoughts on 300 Episodes of Grace (and Its Absence)  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
summary_zh: 乐趣、宽恕和死亡《A Few Thoughts on 300 Episodes of Grace (and Its Absence)》一文首次出现在《知更鸟》上。
title_zh: 300集恩典（及其缺席）的几点思考
content: Listeners will have a better idea of why The Mockingcast works (or doesn’t) and why they keep tuning in, 11 years later. We included a few such stories at the beginning of the 300 th episode , and the tears I shed were real. But I thought take the opportunity to offer a few observations from behind the curtain about what I personally appreciate about our podcast, what I’m most proud of, and what’s been challenging. No doubt my co-hosts would have other aspects they’d highlight. First, the longevity. It’s worth celebrating, even if it’s both a blessing and a curse. The time has allowed us to develop some pretty priceless chemistry. When I’m picking articles for us to talk about, I know that even if the material falls flat, I can rely on our dynamic to take up the slack. I trust my co-hosts, and it’s been very gratifying to watch us gel in a non-contrived way over the years. We’ve been through a lot together, and it shows, I think. Being around so long (in internet years) means we’ve had the benefit of watching things come and go. Sarah mentioned this recently in relation to the moralization of food in our society. It was super acute about eight years ago, then it retreated a bit with the body-positivity moment, now it’s back again under the guise of #maxxing. But that’s just one example. I could mention radical atheism, or gospel-centered this and that, or mindfulness. We’ve seen cultural fixations take hold and then recede, specific anxieties bubble up and dissipate. The longer view allows for a measure of perspective that I believe lends the show added depth. Longevity can also be a curse. The ebb and flow can foster a degree of detachment that masquerades as superiority. For example, it’s hard to take the latest rebranding of medieval monasticism (or justification by works) seriously when you’ve seen it happen four times under four different (best-selling) names already. Discipline becomes application becomes virtue becomes formation and so on. It’s a challenge to keep listening and paying attention, but a challenge that I’m proud of us for at least trying to live up to. Because beneath every one of the trends we’ve observed are real people with real hopes and dreams and disappointments. The second longevity-related challenge is the same one that afflicts anyone in a public role, especially those in ministry or thought life. It’s the danger of impersonating yourself. Whenever I detect in my voice any sense of “the grace guy needs to say a grace thing now” — it makes my skin crawl. Autopilot is the enemy, along with its cousin repetition. I remember a trusted listener once warning me that we were becoming a podcast about social media. Another said we were talking too much about parenting. These grooves are understandable, but to keep things fresh, especially over the long haul, you have to always be finding fresh vistas, not just in the culture but in yourself. It’s not easy. This leads me to the next observation: over ten years, it’s become notably more difficult to find suitable material for The Mockingcast . One of the things that I hold sacred about our show is its role as a refuge from culture wars. I want listeners to be confident that when they press play, we’re not going to trigger them about the same headlines that trigger them the rest of the day. We haven’t done this perfectly, I realize, but it remains a guiding principle. When the occasional how-dare-you emails come in, folks are usually surprised to hear that they come just as frequently from both sides of the aisle. If they didn’t, I’d try to course correct. Finding stuff that threads the needle of interesting and substantial but not pre-narrativized has gotten more challenging over our tenure. It’s like the ledge we walk has gotten narrower. Not nonexistent, mind you, just narrower. I’m so proud we’ve reached this milestone without, at least in my view, falling into an ideological ditch or becoming (too) predictable. content_zh: 听众会更清楚为何《嘲笑者》在11年后(或不是)工作, 在三百集的开头, 我们包含了一些这样的故事, 我个人对播客的欣赏、我最自豪的以及挑战性。 无疑我的联合主办方还会有他们强调的其他方面。 首先,长寿。 这值得庆祝, 时间允许我们开发一些 相当无价的化学。 当我挑选文章让我们讨论时, 我知道,即使材料平平了, 我也可以依靠我们的动力来消遣。 我信任我的同座主持人, 我们一起经历了很多事情, 在网路上呆了这么久, 莎拉最近提到这个问题,谈到我们社会中食品的道德化。 大约八年前,它非常急性, 随身体接触的瞬间, 但这只是一个例子。 我可以提到激进的无神论, 或以福音为中心的这个和那个,或注意。 我们已看到文化定型逐渐稳固, 较长的视野允许某种角度的视角,我认为这可以使节目更深入。 长生亦能作一咒. ebb和流能培养出某种程度的离散,以伪装为优越. 例如,当你在四个不同的(畅销的)名称下看到中世纪修道院(或以作品为理由)的最新重塑很难认真对待。 纪律变成应用,美德变成形成等等。 继续倾听和关注是一项挑战,但我为我们至少努力做到这一点而感到自豪。 因为在我们所看到的每一个趋势之下,都是真正有希望、梦想和失望的人。 与长寿有关的第二个挑战也是影响任何公共角色,特别是部会或思想生活角色的挑战。 这是冒充自己的危险。 每当我从我的声音中察觉到任何“恩人现在需要说一件恩事”的感觉时,这让我的皮肤爬行。 自动驾驶是敌人,还有它的表弟重复. 我记得一位值得信赖的听众曾警告我,我们正成为社交媒体的播客。 另一个人说,我们谈论太多关于养育子女的问题。 这些凹槽是可以理解的, 但为了保持新鲜, 特别是从长远来看, 你必须总是找到新鲜的外观, 不仅仅是在文化中, 还是在你自己。 这不容易。 更难为《嘲笑者》找到合适的材料。 我对我们的表演持神圣态度之一 就是它作为文化战争的避难所的作用 我希望听众们有信心, 当他们按下播放时, 我们不会引发同样的头条新闻, 我们并没有完美完成这项工作, 人们通常会惊讶地听到, 如果不是,我会试着正确行事。 寻找一些能勾结到 有趣和实质性但并非预述的东西, 在我们的任期内变得更具挑战性。 我们走过的窗帘越来越窄了。 不是不存在的,你介意,只是狭小。 我感到非常骄傲的是, 我们达到了这个里程碑, 至少在我看来, 我认为,
