title_zh: 九十五条论点是什么？
content: On October 31, 1517, Martin Luther, now in his mid-thirties, made his way to the Castle Church in Wittenberg and posted his Ninety-Five Theses on the church door. Originally intended as propositions for public debate, the theses were written in Latin—the language of the scholar, not of the street. Luther could have had no idea that they would echo around Europe and become the catalyst for a spiritual revolution. Many of those who saw the papers on the Castle Church door—which seems to have served as a public notice board—would not have been able to read Latin. But soon the theses were translated into German and thereafter spread throughout Europe like wildfire—indeed, like an “act of God.” What were the Ninety-Five Theses? They were statements aimed directly at specific corruptions in the church of Luther’s day, many of them related to issues of pardon, purgatory, and the power of the pope. The first of them was particularly startling: By saying “Repent,” our Lord and Master Jesus Christ willed that the whole of the life of believers should be repentance. (Dominus et magister noster Iesus Christus dicendo “Poenitentiam agite etc.” omnem vitam fidelium poenitentiam esse voluit.) Luther had grasped that the Vulgate translation of “Repent” ( poenitentiam agite ) was open to the misinterpretation “Do penitence (or penance).” And he had also grasped a principle that John Calvin would later expound with great clarity: penitence or repentance is not the action of a moment; it is the turning around of a life—the rejection of sin effected by the gracious work of the Holy Spirit. It cannot therefore be a single act completed in a moment; it is a style of life that lasts until glory. Luther led a full and adventurous life that only an extensive biography can well describe. He was a remarkable man with enormous God-given energy. His speech was direct and plain and not infrequently earthy. He was a teacher of theology, a preacher of the gospel, and an author of some of the most important books in the Reformation period. Notable among his early publications was his On the Babylonian Captivity of the Church , which exposed the church’s failures, while in On the Freedom of a Christian he explained how in Jesus Christ believers are set free both to love God and to serve their neighbor. Thus he wrote in a beautifully crafted sentence that captures the paradox of the gospel-centered life: “A Christian man is the most free lord of all, and subject to none; a Christian man is the most dutiful servant of all, and subject to everyone.” By his preaching, by writing, and especially by his influence in the explanation of salvation by grace through faith in Christ, Luther was used by God to transform the Christian church. The leading Reformers in England and Scotland were influenced by his writings, often smuggled in by merchant sailors. In Scotland in particular, the martyrs of St. Andrews, Patrick Hamilton and George Wishart (whose bodyguard John Knox had been), were disciples of Luther’s teaching. Likewise in England, the heroic William Tyndale left a legacy not only in his English translation of the Bible but in an entire body of literature that echoed the German Reformer’s work. But what did Luther teach? His chief emphases are aptly summarized in the well-known Reformation solas: (1) sola Scriptura : we come to know God through Scripture alone, not through the traditions of the church as such; (2) sola gratia : we come to receive forgiveness by God’s grace alone, not because we are able to earn merit; (3) sola fide: we receive justification by faith alone, and not by faith plus something else; (4) solus Christus : all of God’s riches are given to us in Christ alone; (5) soli Deo gloria: the goal of all of life is the glory of God alone. These principles simply underlined the emphases Luther found in Scripture. But in context, what is most significant about them is not only what they stressed but what they bypassed. content_zh: 1517年10月31日,现在已30多岁的马丁·路德(Martin Luther)前往维滕贝格的城堡教堂并把他的"九十五部曲"张贴到教堂门上. 这些论文最初是打算作为公众辩论的命题,是用拉丁文写的——学者的语言,而不是街上的语言。 路德根本不知道他们会在欧洲周围呼应,成为精神革命的催化剂. 许多人在城堡教堂门上看到报纸, 但很快,这些论文被翻译成德文,然后像野火一样传遍了欧洲,事实上,就像“上帝的行为 ” 。 "九五传"是什么? 这些言论直接针对路德节教堂的具体腐败,其中许多涉及赦免、炼狱和教宗权力等问题。 其中第一个特别令人吃惊:我们的主和耶稣基督大师说“忏悔”,希望信士们的一生都能悔过。 (Dominus et magister noster Iesus Christus dicendo “Poenitentiam angite等”。 Poenitiam intentium sese voluit。) 路德已经明白,“悔改”的Vulgate译文(poenitentiam angite)对“悔改(或忏悔)”的错误解释持开放态度。 他还理解了约翰·卡尔文后来将非常明确地阐明的原则:忏悔或忏悔不是一瞬间的行动;而是生命的转折——圣灵的慷慨工作对罪恶的拒绝。 因此,它不能是一个在一瞬间完成的单一行为;它是一种直到荣耀的生活方式。 路德过着充实而冒险的生活,只有广泛的传记才能很好地描述. 他是一个了不起的人 拥有巨大的上帝赐予的能量。 他的演讲是直截了当的,而且并非经常是土生土长的。 曾任神学教师,"福音"传道人等职,并出自"改革时期一些最重要的著作". 在他早期的著作中,著名的是他的《关于教会的巴比伦式控制》,该书揭露了教会的失败,而在《基督教自由》中,他解释了耶稣基督信徒如何获得自由,既爱上帝,又为邻居服务。 因此,他用一个精心设计的句子写道:“一个基督教徒是所有人中最自由的领主,不受任何人支配;一个基督教徒是所有人中最忠诚的仆人,服从每一个人。” 通过他的传道,写作,特别是他通过对基督的信仰,对恩典解释救赎的影响,路德被上帝用来改造基督教会. 英格兰和苏格兰的主要改革者受到他所著作的影响,经常被商船水手偷运入去. 特别是在苏格兰,圣安德鲁斯,帕特里克·汉密尔顿和乔治·怀克特(他的保镖约翰·诺克斯曾是)的烈士是路德教的门徒. 同样,在英国,英勇的威廉·廷达勒不仅在圣经的英文译本中留下了遗产,而且在与德国改革者著作相呼应的整个文献中也留下了遗产. 但路德教的是什么? 他的主要重心在著名的"改革"(Reformation solas)中得到了恰当的总结:(1) sola Scriptura:我们通过《圣经》,而不是通过教会的传统来了解上帝;(2) sola 惠给:我们通过上帝的恩惠来获得宽恕,而不是因为我们能够获得功绩;(3)  sola 敬畏:我们通过信仰获得理由,而不是信仰获得其他的东西;(4) Solus Christus:神的所有财富都只由基督给予我们;(5) Soli Deo Gloria:所有生命的目标都是上帝的光荣. 这些原则只是强调《圣经》中路德的强调。 但就背景而言,它们最重要的不仅是它们强调的内容,而且是它们所绕过的内容。 无论是路德还是其他的弹匣

title_zh: 退休人员为教会服务的5种方式
content: “Retirement at last! Now I can sleep as late as I want to. Now I get to do nothing all day.” Such is a popular description of how retirement looks to many people. I know some who would even add, “Now I get to play golf every day.” Obviously, this does not reflect the Christian perspective of someone who understands that his chief end is “to glorify God and enjoy Him forever” (see Westminster Shorter Catechism 1; 1 Cor. 10:31; Rom. 11:36). This is not to say that sleeping later and playing golf are anti-Christian. However, there are some significant ways that retirees can still serve the church. 1. Be a volunteer. Retirees have valuable practical and professional experience that can be used in service to others. For example, some of you may have skill sets and expertise that enable you to erect a building or a cabin at a camp from the ground up in very little time. One organization I’m familiar with travels to camps and other locations, bringing their own living accommodations, tools, and know-how to be a blessing to other ministries. Some may volunteer in maintenance of a church’s lawns and gardens to keep them looking tidy. Volunteers can save churches and various ministries a great deal of money and provide much encouragement to them. The church where I attend has many volunteers (both retired and pre-retired) who help at the annual church youth camps. They serve in the kitchen and dining hall, as cabin staff and counselors, as camp nurses and in technical positions, and pay their own way to camp. While not everyone can serve in such physical ways, everyone can volunteer in some way according to their abilities and gifts: “As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another . . . in order that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ” (1 Peter 4:10–11). 2. Show the younger generations a model of an older person who still walks with the Lord. The youth in our churches need models of older believers who are faithful in their daily walk with the Lord. What might this example look like? We can show that we have not waned in faithfulness in our older years, that we are active and unashamed to belong to God’s people, and that we continue to radiate joy in our relationship with the Lord. We can model what it looks like to have no hesitation to speak about Christ in the doctor’s office, store, or when traveling, and that we are not reluctant to share Scripture with other people. Paul wrote to the saints in Philippi: “Brothers, join in imitating me, and keep your eyes on those who walk according to the example you have in us” (Phil. 3:17). Note these words from the psalmist: O God, from my youth you have taught me, and I still proclaim your wondrous deeds. So even to old age and gray hairs, O God, do not forsake me, until I proclaim your might to another generation. (Ps. 71:17–18) 3. Regularly attend worship services and wholeheartedly participate. Not only should retirees maintain a faithful walk with the Lord, but they ought to remain consistent in their attendance at the regular worship services of the church. It is a testament to the Lord’s faithfulness when they are seen in the pews, not just taking up space or putting in their time, but wholeheartedly and enthusiastically singing, listening, and note-taking. This is important because it seems that many young people today view church as optional rather than a joyful habit. Granted, this should begin with the influence of godly parents, but it is reinforced and aided when the testimony of the older generation displays undiminished love for corporate worship, viewing it not as drudgery but delight. Hebrews 10:23–25 instructs us in this way: Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for he who promised is faithful. And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day drawing near. 4. Teach or assist thos
content_zh: “终于退休了! 瞷и何眔边 现在我整天什么都不做。” 这是许多人对退休的看法的流行描述。 我知道有些人甚至会说,“现在我每天都要打高尔夫。” 显然,这并没有反映基督教的观点,即有人理解,他的主要目的就是“颂扬上帝,永远享受他”(见Westminster Shorter Catechism 1; 1 Cor. 10:31; Rom. 11:36)。 这不是说睡觉后打高尔夫是反基督教的。 然而,退休人员仍然可以有一些重要的方式为教会服务. 1. 志愿工作。 退休人员具有宝贵的实践和专业经验,可用于为他人服务. 例如,你们中有些人可能拥有技能和专门知识,能够在极短的时间内从地上建起一座建筑物或一个小木屋。 我熟悉一个组织前往营地及其他地点, 有些人会自愿维护教堂的草坪和花园, 志愿者可以挽救教会和各部一大笔钱,并为它们提供很大的鼓励. 我所在的教堂有许多志愿者(既有退休的,也有退休前的),他们在每年的教堂青年营中提供帮助. 他们在厨房和餐厅服务,担任木屋工作人员和咨询员,担任营地护士和技术职务,并支付自己去营地的方式。 虽然并非每个人都能以这样的身体方式服务,但每个人都能根据自己的能力和天赋以某种方式自愿: " 由于每个人都收到礼物,利用礼物互相服务,以使上帝在一切事情上都能被耶稣基督所赞美" (1 Peter 4:10-11). 2. 向年轻一代展示仍然与主同道的老年人的模范. 我们教会中的青年需要老信徒的模范,他们在每天与上帝一起行走时是忠实的。 这个例子会是什么样子? 我们可以表明,我们年事已高,在忠诚中并不衰弱,我们积极而且毫不羞愧地属于上帝的子民,而且我们继续在与上帝的关系中放出欢乐。 我们可以在医生的办公室、商店或旅行时, 以毫不犹豫的方式谈论基督, 保罗在Philippi给圣徒们写了一封信:“兄弟们,一起模仿我,并注意那些按照你们在我们身上的榜样行走的人”(Phil. 3:17)。 请注意,这些话来自诗人:上帝啊,你从我的青春中教我的,我仍然宣布你的奇事。 所以,上帝啊,即使老去和灰发,也不要抛弃我,直到我向另一代人宣告你的力量。 3. 定期参加礼拜仪式并全心全意地参加。 退休人员不仅应当与主保持忠实的行走,而且他们应当始终如一地参加教会的定期礼拜服务. 这证明了上帝的忠诚,当人们看到他们出现在树上时,他们不仅占据了空间或投入了时间,而且全心全意地歌唱、聆听和记事。 这一点很重要,因为今天许多年轻人似乎将教堂视为可选的习惯,而不是令人高兴的习惯. 当然,这应该从上帝父母的影响入手,但是当年长者的证词显示对企业崇拜的爱不减时,它得到了加强和帮助,认为它不是劳累,而是快乐。 希伯来人10:23-25这样教导我们:让我们不动摇地坚持我们的希望的忏悔,因为承诺的人是忠实的。 让我们考虑一下如何相互激起爱和善行,而不是像有些人的习惯那样忽视相会,而是相互鼓励,正如你们看到的日子临近的时候一样。 4. 教育或援助托斯人

title_zh: 这五个唯独对今天的教会仍然重要吗？
content: The five solas (Latin for “alone”) of the Reformation—Scripture alone, grace alone, faith alone, Christ alone, to the glory of God alone—are indispensable for the church in any era. They will always be relevant because they summarize the biblical gospel, which is the church’s lifeblood in every age. They are particularly significant today because even professing evangelicals, to say nothing of the culture around us, are being tempted to abandon the gospel. Therefore, the church must recognize the dire need of not only defending the five solas but also celebrating them. The five solas are important for us today for at least three reasons. 1. The five solas set apart the true gospel from every other religion, worldview, or philosophy. Every day, the world calls out its siren song of spiritual compromise. Satan loves to negotiate the nonnegotiables of biblical truth. He whispers the lie that we don’t need to have strong convictions about the Bible as our only standard of truth or hold firm to the teaching that only those who trust Christ alone for salvation are right with God. The temptation to downplay doctrine is unceasing. A winsome but unyielding grasp of the five solas can help us resist these attractive lies. 2. The five solas provide us with unspeakable comfort in a chaotic world. The pace of modern life is unsustainable. It colors our understanding of “the normal Christian life.” We tend to equate busyness in ministry with productiveness for Jesus. But the two must not be confused. Knowing that we are saved by God’s grace alone through faith alone gives us rest from an exhausting world. We leave behind a performance mindset in our relationship with God and embrace a life of trusting, resting grace. Safe in the arms of our Savior, we are set free to let go of trying to earn what God freely gives us—Christ Himself. 3. The five solas remind us that our salvation is secure. Only when we are assured of the love of God will we live out the commands of God. The five solas enable us to say with David, “Oh how I love your law! It is my meditation all the day” (Ps. 119:97). Following Jesus, obeying Him by the Spirit, and killing sin become our joy. So many Christians drift, unconsciously most of the time, to the belief that God loves them when they obey. But the true gospel of the five solas pulls us back to the bedrock scriptural truth that God loves us and therefore we obey. The difference is subtle, but it makes all the difference in our daily lives. Your Father loves you! He is pleased with you in Christ. When those realities come home, John’s words become our delightful creed: “For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments. And his commandments are not burdensome” (1 John 5:3). In sum, nothing is more urgent for the church than protecting, propagating, and passing on the true gospel encapsulated by the five solas . It is our only hope, our greatest comfort, and our supreme joy. Most of all, these biblical teachings will always be important because they bring us to Christ, who is our life. 1 Footnotes Editor's Note: This article was originally published January 19, 2022. ↩
content_zh: 改革的五所索拉斯(拉丁语为“单独”)——光是文字、光是恩典、光是信仰、光是基督、光是上帝的光荣——在任何时代,对教会都是不可或缺的。 因为他们总结了圣经福音, 它们今天特别重要,因为甚至宣称福音派教徒 -- -- 更不用说我们周围的文化 -- -- 被诱惑放弃福音。 因此,教会必须认识到,不仅迫切需要捍卫五个独奏会,而且迫切需要庆祝它们。 五个索拉斯今天对我们很重要,至少有三个原因。 1. 这五所索拉斯将真正的福音与所有其他宗教、世界观或哲学分开。 世界每天都在呼唤着它的精神妥协之歌。 撒旦喜欢商议圣经中不可谈判的真理. 他低语地说,我们不需要对《圣经》作为我们唯一的真理标准抱有坚定的信念,也不要坚持这样的教导,即只有那些只相信基督的人才能与上帝同在。 轻描淡写理论的诱惑是不停的。 能够帮助我们抵制这些有吸引力的谎言。 2. 在一个混乱的世界中,这五相声给我们带来了难以形容的安慰。 现代生活的步伐是不可持续的。 它体现了我们对“正常的基督教生活”的理解。 我们往往把部长的繁忙与耶稣的生产力等同起来。 但两者不可混淆. 仅凭信仰,我们就能从一个疲惫的世界中安息。 在与上帝的关系中,我们留下了一种表现的心态,并拥抱一种信任和安息的恩典的生活。 在我们的救世主的怀抱中,我们被放任去试图获得上帝给我们的自由——基督。 3. 五相声提醒我们,我们的救赎是安全的。 只有当我们得到上帝的爱的保证时,我们才会遵守上帝的命令。 这五相相声使我们能够和大卫说:“我多么爱你的律法! 我一整天都在冥想”(临119:97)。 顺从耶稣,顺从他的精神,杀戮罪孽成为了我们的喜悦. 如此多的基督徒在无意识中大部分时间漂移到相信上帝在他们服从时爱他们. 但是,五相声的真正福音让我们回到上帝爱我们,因此我们服从的基础性文字真理. 区别是微妙的,但它使我们日常生活中的一切不同。 你父亲爱你! 他在基督里对你感到高兴 当这些现实回到故乡时,约翰的话成了我们令人愉快的信念:“这是上帝的爱,我们遵守他的戒律。 他的戒律不是累赘的"(1 John 5:3). 总而言之,对教会来说,最紧迫的莫过于保护、宣传、传递由五所索拉斯所封印的真正福音。 这是我们唯一的希望,我们最大的慰藉,和我们最大的快乐。 最重要的是,这些圣经教义将永远是重要的,因为它们把我们带到基督那里,而基督是我们的生命. 1 脚注编辑注:本文章最初于2022年1月19日发表. .

title_zh: 黑暗之后，光明
content: In the old city of Geneva, Switzerland, there is a large park on the grounds of the University of Geneva that commemorates the Reformation. That park is adorned with a huge wall, called the International Monument to the Reformation or simply the Reformation Wall. In statues and bas-reliefs, the wall depicts figures from the Reformation including John Calvin, John Knox, William Farel, and Theodore Beza. Surrounding these and other statues, the motto of the Reformation is inscribed on each side: post tenebras lux —after darkness, light. This phrase refers not only to the unveiling and liberation of the Scriptures—which were made available to the common people during the Reformation—but also to the loss and recovery of the most important biblical doctrine there is: the doctrine of justification by faith alone. This was the primary and central issue of the Protestant Reformation. During the dispute between the Protestants and the Roman Catholics, both sides saw that justification was so important that no compromise was possible. Both sides were convinced that what was at stake in the doctrine of justification was the very essence of the biblical gospel. When the gospel is at stake, everything is at stake, because the gospel tells us how we can be right with God. In Galatians 1:6–9, Paul writes about the importance of getting the gospel right: I am astonished that you are so quickly deserting him who called you in the grace of Christ and are turning to a different gospel—not that there is another one, but there are some who trouble you and want to distort the gospel of Christ. But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach to you a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be accursed. As we have said before, so now I say again: If anyone is preaching to you a gospel contrary to the one you received, let him be accursed. This Apostle was a man who was constantly extolling the virtues of patience, gentleness, meekness, charity, and tolerance; who, conversely, constantly rebuked the sins of contentiousness, divisiveness, quarrelsome spirits, belligerence, and so on. This man said that we ought to strive as much as we possibly can to live at peace with all men; he was known as the Apostle of peace and unity. Yet suddenly he came to a point over a doctrine where he said, “There can be no toleration here. To tolerate the distortion of the gospel into another gospel is to tolerate the intolerable.” The first thing that Paul did was express his amazement—not that the people had left the gospel that he had preached to them, but that they had done it so quickly. He was hardly gone from their midst before they wanted to listen to the teachings of the Judaizers, who insisted that one cannot be saved by faith in Christ alone but must also have good works and obedience to the law in order to be saved. This “other gospel” was no gospel at all—there is only one gospel, the gospel of God, revealed in and through Christ and proclaimed and expounded by the Apostles. The stakes are so high when it comes to this point that Paul pronounced a curse on anyone who teaches otherwise. The Greek work translated “accursed” is anathema —damned. The Apostle understood that the issue of justification was no mere academic issue, but one that touches every person’s life ultimately. It can be summed up in one question: How are we saved? It is a life-and-death matter, an eternal life matter. The New Testament makes it clear that each of us will be called into account before God, and that God is righteous while we’re not. The doctrine of justification addresses the solution to that problem, declaring how we, as unjust people, can be reconciled to a just and holy God. So if there’s anything in the essence of the Christian faith, of the good news of the gospel, it’s this doctrine. Martin Luther, building on Paul’s assessment, called the doctrine of justification the article on which the church stands or falls. Luther understood that theology is syste
content_zh: 在瑞士日内瓦老城区,日内瓦大学地上有一座大型公园来纪念"改革". 那个公园的装饰有一堵巨大的墙,被称作"改革国际纪念碑"或"改革墙". 在雕像和堡垒救济中,墙上描绘了来自改革派的人物,包括约翰·卡尔文,约翰·诺克斯,威廉·法雷尔和西奥多·贝扎. 围绕这些和其他雕像,"改革"的座右铭被刻在了每一边:后倒行奢侈——在黑暗后,光辉. 这一短语不仅指《圣经》的揭幕和解放(在改革期间提供给普通人民),而且还指最重要的圣经学说 -- -- 仅以信仰为理由的学说 -- -- 的丧失和复苏。 这是新教改革的首要和核心问题。 在新教徒和罗马天主教徒之间的纠纷中,双方认为这种辩解非常重要,不可能妥协. 双方都相信,辩护理论的关键在于圣经福音的精髓。 当福音受到威胁时,一切都处于危险之中,因为福音告诉我们,我们如何能够与上帝对齐。 在加拉提亚1:6-9中,保罗写道正确福音的重要性:我感到惊讶的是,你如此快地抛弃了以基督之恩召唤你并转向另一个福音的人,而不是另一个福音,但有些人烦恼你并想歪曲基督的福音。 即使我们或从天上降下的天神,为你们传福音,与我们所传教你们的福音相悖,教他受诅咒。 正如我们以前说过的,现在我再说一遍: 如果有人向你们宣扬与你们所接受的福音相悖的福音,你们就应当诅咒他。 这名使徒是一个不断赞颂耐心、温和、温柔、慈善和宽容等美德的人;相反,他不断斥责争议、分裂、争吵、好战等罪恶。 这位先生说,我们应该尽我们所能地同所有人和平相处;他被称为和平与团结的使者。 然而,他突然想到一个理论,他说,“在这里是不能容忍的。 容忍将福音歪曲为又一福音就是容忍不能容忍的福音。” 保罗做的第一件事是表达他的惊叹——不是说人民已经离开了他向他们所宣扬的福音,而是他们如此快地做到了. 在他们想听犹太教的教义之前,他几乎没有离开他们中间,犹太教坚持一个人不能只靠信仰基督而得到救赎,为了得到救赎,他还必须有善行并服从法律. 这种 " 其他福音 " 根本不是福音 -- -- 只有一种福音,即上帝的福音,在基督中和通过基督揭示,并由使徒们宣布和阐述。 此时此刻,利害攸关,以致于保罗对教别的人发出诅咒. 希腊翻译的作品“被诅咒了”是令人厌恶的。 使徒们明白,理由问题不仅仅是学术问题,而是一个最终触及每个人生活的问题。 它可以概括为一个问题:我们如何得到拯救? 这是生死攸关的 永生攸关的 《新约》明确指出,在上帝面前,我们每一个人都将受到重视,上帝是善良的,而我们不是正义的。 辩解的理论涉及这个问题的解决,宣布我们作为不公正的人民如何能够与一个公正和神圣的上帝相协调。 因此,如果有基督教信仰的本质,福音的好消息,那就是这个学说。 马丁·路德(Martin Luther)根据保罗的评估,称教会所立足或倒下的文章为辩解理论. 路德知道神学是循环的

title: Who Was Theodore Beza?
summary: Theodore Beza is an unfamiliar figure today in the evangelical world. He has been much maligned by many historians and theologians who created the image of an austere man who turned Calvin’s theology into an arid scholastic system. His life spanned almost the whole sixteenth century, and he died in 1605 at the age of eighty-s
summary_zh: 西奥多·贝扎（ Theodore Beza ）今天在福音派世界中是一个陌生的人物。他受到许多历史学家和神学家的诽谤，他们创造了一个严肃的人的形象，他将加尔文的神学变成了一个干旱的学术体系。这张照片实际上与事实相去甚远。那么西奥多·贝扎到底是谁？他于1519年出生于法国韦泽莱，是一个富裕的法国小贵族家庭。他的一生几乎跨越了整个十六世纪，他于1605年去世，享年八十多岁。
title_zh: 西奥多·贝扎是谁？
content: Theodore Beza is an unfamiliar figure today in the evangelical world. He has been much maligned by many historians and theologians who created the image of an austere man who turned Calvin’s theology into an arid scholastic system. This image is actually very far from the truth. So who was Theodore Beza really? He was born in Vézelay, France, in 1519 in an affluent family of the minor French nobility. His life spanned almost the whole sixteenth century, and he died in 1605 at the age of eighty-six. By God’s providence, there were two clear turning points in his life. The first occurred at the age of nine when he was placed as a lodger with a Lutheran scholar, Melchior Wolmar, who became his preceptor. He spent seven years with Wolmar, who taught him law, Latin, and Greek. Interestingly, one of Wolmar’s other students during that time was none other than Calvin, who was just ten years older than Beza. Wolmar gave Beza a first-rate education, and, like Calvin, Beza was likely more fluent in Latin than in French. More importantly, Wolmar was instrumental in his journey toward the new Reformed faith. It was through Wolmar that, sometime around 1535, Beza read a book by the Swiss Reformer Heinrich Bullinger and was converted. Years later, Beza wrote to Bullinger: “You made known to me true piety, and its purest source: The Word of God.” 1 However, Beza had a lot to lose if he disclosed his newfound faith. He received substantial ecclesiastical incomes through one of his uncles, who was an abbot, and this allowed him to enjoy a life of pleasure in Paris, dedicating himself to poetry and humanistic studies. For several years, he kept his faith secret, and he secretly married Claudine Denosse, the daughter of a Parisian Protestant merchant. Beza promised he would marry her publicly whenever they could find a truly Reformed church. The second turning point of his life came in 1548 when he contracted the plague and came close to death. He took it as a clear warning from God and came out openly about his faith. Shortly after, he fled to Geneva. Theodore and Claudine were publicly married by Calvin himself, and they remained devoted to each other and to the cause of Christ until Claudine’s death in 1588. After teaching Greek in Lausanne for a few years, Beza settled in Geneva permanently in 1558, mainly because of his admiration for Calvin. He lived there until his death, faithfully serving alongside Calvin and assuming his mantle as leader of the French Reformed church after Calvin’s death in 1564. Beza’s legacy is immense and multifaceted, and it is difficult to summarize it in a few words. He was first and foremost a man of letters. One of his first tasks in Geneva was to complete the translation of the Psalms from Hebrew into French for the Huguenot psalter, a translation left unfinished by another Reformed poet at his death. Beza also published a critical edition of the Greek New Testament that was influential on the Textus Receptus, from which the King James Bible was translated. In fact, the 1565 edition was dedicated to Queen Elizabeth I. In many ways, this was Beza’s lifetime project. He tirelessly corrected and improved the text and published several editions, with the last major revision appearing in 1598. In 1559, he published a “Confession of the Christian Faith,” addressed to his father, to explain why he had embraced the Reformed faith. Although it was penned in a few days, it was hugely popular, as it was published at least thirty-five times during his lifetime and translated into Latin, English, German, and Dutch. He consolidated Calvin’s legacy in Geneva by preaching regularly and teaching theology for forty years. We know from several sources that his teaching was greatly appreciated. For example, an alumnus wrote in 1578: We listened to you with so much admiration and pleasure. Apart from your own personality traits, you combined Melanchthon’s penetrating insights, Calvin’s solid and direct common sense, and Vermigli’s
content_zh: 西奥多·贝扎是今天福音世界中不熟悉的人物. 他深受许多历史学家和神学家的污蔑,他们创造了一个把加尔文神学变成干旱学术体系的紧缩人的形象。 这个形象实际上与事实相去甚远. 谁是西奥多·贝萨? 他于1519年生于法国韦泽莱的一个小法国贵族富裕家庭. 他的生平几乎跨越了整个16世纪,他于1605年以86岁之多去世. 上帝保佑,他的人生有两个明显的转折点。 第一个发生在9岁时,他被安置在路德会学者梅尔奇奥尔·沃尔马尔(Melchior Wolmar)的住处,他成为他的受体. 他与沃尔玛共事了七年,沃尔玛教他法律,拉丁语,希腊语. 有趣的是,当时沃尔玛的其他学生中只有一个是加尔文,他刚刚比贝扎大了十多岁. 沃尔玛给予贝扎一流的教育,而同加尔文一样,贝扎在拉丁语中可能比法语更流利. 更重要的是,沃尔玛在走向新的改革后信仰的旅程中起到了推动作用. 正是通过沃尔玛,在1535年左右的某个时候,贝扎阅读了由瑞士改革者海因里希·布林格所著的一出书并被皈依. 多年后,贝扎写信给布林格:"你让我知道真正的虔诚,以及它最纯洁的来源:上帝之道". 1 然而,贝扎如果透露出他新发现的信仰,就会损失很多. 他通过他的一位叔父获得了大量的教会收入,他是一位方丈,这使得他能够在巴黎享受快乐的生活,专心于诗歌和人文研究. 几年来,他保守了信仰的秘密,他秘密地嫁给了一位巴黎新教商人的女儿克洛丁·德诺塞. 贝扎答应他只要找到真正改革的教堂 就会公开娶她 他生命的第二个转折点是1548年他感染了瘟疫并接近死亡. 他认为这是从真主发出的明确的警告,并且公开地阐明他的信仰。 不久,他逃到日内瓦. 西奥多和克洛丁由加尔文本人公开出嫁,两人始终致力于彼此和基督的事业,直到克洛丁于1588年去世. 在洛桑教希腊语几年后,贝扎于1558年在日内瓦永久定居,这主要是因为他对加尔文的钦佩. 他在那里一直活到去世,忠实地与加尔文并肩服役,并在加尔文于1564年去世后担任法国改革会会长. 贝萨的遗产是巨大的和多方面的,很难用几句话概括一下。 他最先是写信的人 他在日内瓦的最初任务之一是完成将"诗经"从希伯来语翻译成法语,为"胡盖诺特诗人"(Huguenot psalter)所翻译,这是另一位改革诗人死后留下的未完成的译作. 贝扎还出版了"希腊新约"的批判版,该版对"特特鲁斯受体"有影响,从中翻译出"国王詹姆斯圣经". 事实上,1565年版是献给伊丽莎白一世女王. 在很多方面,这是贝扎的一生项目. 他不懈地纠正并改进了文本,并出版了多本版本,最后一出重大修订于1598年. 1559年,他发表了一份致其父亲的“基督教信仰的承认”,以解释他为什么接受改革后的信仰。 虽然短短几天就被收录了,但极受欢迎,因为在他的生平中至少出版了35次并被翻译成了拉丁语,英语,德语和荷兰语. 他通过定期传教和教授神学四十年,巩固了加尔文在日内瓦的遗产. 我们从几个来源知道,他的教学受到极大的赞赏。 例如,一位校友在1578年写道:我们非常钦佩和愉快地聆听了你们的发言. 除了你自己的个性特征,你结合了梅兰希通的洞察力,加尔文的坚实而直接的常识,和弗米利的常识.

title_zh: 新教改革的原因是什么？
content: What was the matter with the Protestant Reformation? It might seem like a strange question. Some might say that there was nothing the matter with the Reformation, that it was the acme of spiritual recovery of biblical Christianity in church history and therefore was a sort of golden age of biblical faith. Others might say that the matter with the Reformation was that there was one at all, since it produced the largest schism in church history. That’s not what I mean, however, when I ask about what was the matter with the Protestant Reformation. I’m not using the word matter in the normal way, which typically indicates that something is wrong. When we ask, “What’s the matter with you?” we are assuming that something is wrong or that we’re looking for fault. What I mean, by contrast, is this: What was the essence, the substance, or what is called in philosophy the material cause of the Protestant Reformation? Another way to ask it would be this: What was the chief issue that provoked such massive consequences as this split that occurred in the sixteenth century? When historians consider the causes of the Protestant Reformation, they often use distinctions originally set forth by the philosopher Aristotle, and they distinguish between the formal cause and the material cause . The formal cause, the intellectual background to the issue, was a dispute over the seat of final authority that binds the Christian conscience. We’ll look at that under the heading of sola Scriptura . The material cause , however, the substantive issue that was the core point of dispute, was the doctrine of justification. The Protestant view of this matter is expressed in the shorthand of the Latin phrase sola fide . This is the first of the Latin slogans of the Reformation known as the five solas . They are sola fide , justification is by faith alone; sola gratia , salvation is by grace alone; solus Christus , salvation is through Christ alone; sola Scriptura , the sole authority that binds the conscience of the Christian is the Bible alone; and then, finally, soli Deo gloria , to God alone belongs the glory. Sola fide is shorthand for the central issue of the Reformation, the material cause, which was the question of justification. The Protestant Reformers set forth a doctrine that our justification is by faith and by faith alone without any mixture of good works or merit on our part. To understand sola fide in its historical context, we have to understand something about the theological dispute based on the Roman Catholic understanding of justification. At the heart of this dispute was not a tangential debate over how many angels can dance on the head of a pin or a needless controversy over pedantic points of theology that only academics care about. Rather, this issue touched the very heart of the Christian faith because the question of justification is designed to answer this deeper question: How can an unjust person possibly survive the judgment of a just and holy God? In our day, the doctrine of justification has been degraded in terms of its perceived importance. Historically, the differences among churches over how we obtain a right standing before God were considered significant; those differences have now been minimized as having no great weight. We’re living in a time of relativism, which says that there is no objective truth, and pluralism, which declares that there are many different approaches to truth and views of truth. Therefore, people assert, doctrinal issues should never divide us because what really counts are personal relationships, not doctrine. That notion is propounded even though the New Testament is replete with Apostolic concern about correct doctrine. Sadly, that’s not where the church is in this day and age, and sometimes we have to ask, Why? Some people are in church Sunday after Sunday, are continually exposed to the preaching of the gospel, and are members of the church but have never really committed their lives to Christ. S
content_zh: 新教改革有什么问题? 这似乎是一个奇怪的问题。 有人可能会说"改革"没有问题,它是圣经基督教在教会历史上的精神恢复的一环,因此是某种圣经信仰的黄金时代. 其他人可能会说,改革派的问题是,它完全是一个问题,因为它产生了教会历史上最大的分裂。 我问新教改革有什么问题, 我并不以正常方式使用这个词, 当我们问:“你怎么了? ”我们假设有些事情是错的,或者我们在找错。 我的意思是,反之,这是: 什么是实质,实质,或者哲学中所谓的"新教改革的物质事业"? 另一种方式是问: 十六世纪这种分裂造成如此巨大后果的主要问题是什么? 当历史学家考虑新教改革的原因时,他们经常使用哲学家亚里士多德最初提出的区别,并且区分了形式原因和物质原因. 正式的原因,即问题的知识背景,是对约束基督教良知的最终权威所在地的争议. 我们将在索拉·斯克里普图拉(Sola Scriptura)的标题下审视这一点。 然而,实质原因,即作为争议核心问题的实质性问题,是理由理论。 新教徒对此事的看法用拉丁语中的"sola refine"的简写来表达. 这是改革派的拉丁口号中的第一个, 他们都是虔诚的,只有信仰才是正当的;索拉恩典,只有恩典才有救赎;索卢斯·克赖斯,只有基督才有救赎;索拉·斯克利普图拉,将基督教良知捆绑的唯一权威就是《圣经》;最后,索利·德奥·克罗里亚,光靠上帝才是荣耀。 Sola true是改革这一中心问题的简称,即物质原因,即理由问题。 新教改革者提出了一种理论,即我们的理由仅靠信仰和信仰,而没有任何好的工作和功绩。 为了在历史背景中理解 sola true,我们必须根据罗马天主教对理由的理解来理解神学争议. 这场争论的核心不是一场关于有多少天使可以在一针头上跳舞的微小争论,也不是一场关于只有学者关心的神学的教条点的不必要的争论. 相反,这个问题触动了基督教信仰的核心,因为辩解问题旨在回答这个更深层的问题: 一个不公正的人怎么能活过一个公正和神圣的上帝的判断呢? 在我们这个时代,正当理论在被认为的重要性方面已经退化。 历史上,各教会在如何在上帝面前获得权利问题上的分歧被认为是重大的;这些分歧现在已最小化,因为没有很大的分量。 我们生活在相对主义的时代, 说没有客观的真理, 因此,人们断言,理论问题绝不应该分裂我们,因为真正重要的是个人关系,而不是理论。 尽管《新约》充满了使徒对正确学说的关切,但这一概念还是被提出来。 可悲的是, 教堂现在不是这个时代, 有时我们不得不问, 为什么? 有些人周日后在教堂礼拜,不断被传出福音的传道,并且是教堂的成员,但从未真正为基督献出生命. 页:1

title: IMB seeks teachers, healthcare workers, business professionals to serve as missionaries
summary: When most Southern Baptists think of missionaries, they often picture church planters and evangelists. But leaders with the International Mission Board say some of the greatest needs today are for professionals whose work happens behind the scenes. IMB leaders report that critical roles such as teachers, healthcare workers, counselors, accountants, logistics specialists and member care personnel are helping advance the Great Commission in ways many churches never see. summary_zh: 当大多数"南方浸信会"想到传教士时,他们常常会描绘出教会的植树人和福音派. 但国际使命委员会的领导人说,今天最需要的是那些在幕后工作的专业人员。 咨监委领导人报告说,教师、保健工作者、顾问、会计师、后勤专家和成员护理人员等关键角色正在帮助推进大委员会,许多教会从未看到过。 多琳·贝克,IMB导演
title_zh: IMB寻求教师、医护人员、商业专业人士担任传教士
content: IMB missionary Dr. Heidi Haun, left, checks on patients at Baptist Medical Centre in Nalerigu, Ghana. There are needed roles for IMB missionaries in healthcare, ministering to the needs of local populations and utilizing this time to minister to spiritual needs. IMB Photo When most Southern Baptists think of missionaries, they often picture church planters and evangelists. But leaders with the International Mission Board say some of the greatest needs today are for professionals whose work happens behind the scenes. IMB leaders report that critical roles such as teachers, healthcare workers, counselors, accountants, logistics specialists and member care personnel are helping advance the Great Commission in ways many churches never see. Doreen Baker, IMB director of TCK (third culture kid or missionary kid) education, sees a constant need for education professionals. Teachers are needed in international schools, which cover a variety of global educational entities, and in other settings to provide for missionary kids and their educational needs. “Teachers are significant in that not only are they providing instruction for students, but they are an integral part of the core missionary task ,” Baker said. “We also have great needs for consultants to support our families on the field with their children’s education in many ways.” Baker previously served 25 years teaching in Asia and experienced how education creates access to missions where traditional pathways may be limited. IMB missionary Ellie Bohrer teaches a 12th grade World Views class at Black Forest Academy in Germany. The IMB is seeking other educators, like Bohrer, who are willing to use their skills on the mission field. IMB Photo Scott Ray, IMB senior director of global deployment, noted that many missionary positions go unfilled simply because they fall outside traditional perceptions of missionary service. He said professional skills can provide both practical ministry support and access to countries where traditional missionary visas are difficult to obtain. Opportunities exist for finance professionals, veterinarians, medical workers, Send Relief personnel and others. Healthcare remains one of the most strategic areas in demand. Tom Hicks, IMB director of global health strategies, said many medical professionals have the wrong perception about mission work. “We do have an issue where people will select out because they don’t think that what they do is useful on the mission field,” he said. In reality, Hicks said many areas across the globe are increasingly seeking family medicine physicians, internists, pediatricians, pediatric nurse practitioners, OB providers, physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech pathologists and lactation consultants. The need is especially significant in sub-Saharan Africa, where young populations create a growing demand for pediatric care. Healthcare professionals also provide a unique advantage in countries that restrict missionary activity. “Missionaries with a vocational value, like healthcare missionaries, have opportunities to go places that others can’t go,” Hicks said. Another often-overlooked ministry is member care, which focuses on the spiritual, emotional, mental and relational health of IMB missionaries. Chris Martin is the IMB director of global member care. “Member care missionaries stand alongside those missionaries that are thought of traditionally as church planters or evangelists and support them,” Martin said. Many who serve in these roles come from counseling backgrounds and help missionaries navigate stress, conflict, grief and other challenges that can affect long-term ministry effectiveness. Martin compares their role to Aaron and Hur in Exodus 19, holding up Moses’ arms during battle, strengthening those serving on the front lines. IMB missionary Glen Garner uses his business skills and experience as the logistics director for missionaries serving globally. He lives in Lima, Peru, with his wife, Shannon
content_zh: IMB传教士海迪·哈恩博士出走,在加纳纳莱里古的浸信会医疗中心检查病人. 咨监委的传教士在保健、满足当地居民需要和利用这一时间满足精神需要方面需要发挥作用。 IMB Photo 当大多数"南方浸信会"想到传教士时,他们经常会描绘出教会的植树人和福音会信徒. 但国际使命委员会的领导人说,今天最需要的是那些在幕后工作的专业人员。 咨监委领导人报告说,教师、保健工作者、顾问、会计师、后勤专家和成员护理人员等关键角色正在帮助推进大委员会,许多教会从未看到过。 多琳·贝克(英语:Doreen Baker,IMB Director of TCK (TCK)教育(英语:TCK (third Culture kid or missionary kid)))的导演,不断看到教育专业人士的需求. 国际学校需要教师,这些学校包括各种全球教育实体,其他环境则需要教师,以满足传教儿童及其教育需要。 教师不仅为学生授课, 也是核心传教任务的组成部分。 " 我们还非常需要顾问,以多种方式支持我们在外地的家庭,教育他们的孩子。 " 贝克以前在亚洲执教了25年,并体验了教育如何创造进入传统途径可能有限的特派团的机会。 IMB传教士艾莉·波克勒在德国黑森林学院教授一门12年级"世界观"课程. IMB正在寻找其他教育者,比如波尔,他们愿意在任务领域运用自己的技能. IMB Photo Scott Ray是IMB全球部署的高级主任,他指出,许多传教士职位由于不属于传教士服务的传统观念而无人填补. 他说,专业技能既能提供实用的部委支助,也能进入传统传教签证难以获得的国家。 金融专业人员、兽医、医务工作者、派遣救济人员和其他人都有机会。 保健仍然是需求最有战略意义的领域之一。 全球卫生战略的IMB主任汤姆·希克斯(Tom Hicks)说,许多医疗专业人员对任务工作的看法是错误的. 他表示:「我们确实有个问题, 人们会选择出局, 事实上,Hicks说,全球许多地区正在越来越多地寻找家庭医学医生、实习医生、儿科医生、儿科护士、产科医生、物理治疗师、职业治疗师、语言病理学家和哺乳期咨询师。 这种需求在撒哈拉以南非洲尤为重要,那里的青年人口对儿科护理的需求日益增加。 在限制传教活动的国家,保健专业人员也提供了独特的优势。 「有职业价值的使团, 另一个经常被忽略的部是成员护理,重点是IMB传教士的精神、情感、心理和关系健康。 克里斯·马丁是IMB全球会员关怀的总监. Martin说,“会员关心传教士与那些传统上被认为是教会植树人或福音传教士的传教士站在一起并支持他们。” 担任这些角色的许多人来自咨询背景,帮助传教士应对压力、冲突、悲痛和其他挑战,这些挑战可能影响部委的长期效力。 马丁将他们的角色比作出埃及19号的Aaron和Hur,在战斗中举起摩西的手臂,强化了在前线服役的人. IMB传教士格伦·加纳(英语:Glen Garner)利用其作为在全球服务的传教士的后勤主任的业务技能和经验. 他和妻子香农住在秘鲁利马

title_zh: IMB传教士通过新信徒和当地教会看到神在工作
content: In South Asia, Maryam and a local pastor baptize Tara, a new believer. IMB missionaries work alongside local believers and churches to fulfill the Great Commission. IMB Photo Twenty minutes had passed already. The sun was going down, and they were looking everywhere, but they only saw men in the park. Sophia, an International Mission Board missionary, joined another IMB missionary and Maryam, a South Asian Christian. They went to the park to share the gospel, but approaching a man in their Muslim-majority city was out of the question. They kept walking and watching. Even if they went home without a single conversation, Sophia knew Maryam would want to try again. This woman who had grown up with a distrust of Muslims, now searched a park for a Muslim woman to tell about Jesus. When Sophia first invited her along, Maryam never imagined a Muslim could come to know Jesus. But the more they went out sharing the gospel together, the more God softened her heart. “One day, I found she was sharing in the park by herself, without me,” Sophia said with a laugh. These days, she shares regularly — with classmates, with rickshaw drivers, with women in the park, when she can find them. God transformed Maryam’s heart. He could transform this walk through the park, too. “So we stopped,” Sophia said, “and prayed, ‘God, give us just one woman to talk to.’” Then they spotted her — a girl sitting alone on a bench. Meeting the girl on the bench She looked like other conservative Muslim women in the area, covered in black except for her face. They approached casually, not wanting to frighten her. It was Eid al-Adha – “one of the biggest Muslim holidays here,” Sophia said. They greeted her and asked about her holiday plans. Her name was Tara, and she wasn’t intimidated at all. “You may think I’m a Muslim from the way I dress,” she said, “but actually in my heart, I have left Islam.” “I was a little shocked,” Sophia said, hearing such a bold statement from a stranger. Tara told them she was a university student at a conservative Islamic school, but she had grown disillusioned and discontent with the religion. “ I don’t believe in Islam anymore,” Tara said. Without knowledge of God, she had no one to pray to, and it left her lonely. She’d been searching — Buddhism and Hinduism from friends, even a meeting with atheists, who struck her as unhappy, following only themselves. “Do you know any Christians?” Sophia asked. “Would you like to hear what we believe?” “Sure, please share.” They read about Jesus’ birth, and Tara was hungry for more. When she asked about church, Sophia described their congregation of about 40 believers, many from a Muslim background. Though she wasn’t ready to visit the church, Tara continued her interest in learning. Sophia and Maryam met with her every week in coffee shops, tea shops, Sophia’s home, wherever they could talkthat wasn’t too loud or have “too many ears and eyes” observing them. Finding her closest friend They read through the Gospel of John. One November day in a coffee shop, they reached the passage on the Samaritan woman at the well, and Sophia noticed Tara was crying. “Tara, I see you have tears,” Sophia said. “Let’s stop. Let’s talk about it .” That day, Tara prayed to receive Christ. Soon after, she wanted to visit the church, though nervous how believers would receive her in a hijab. “They will love you,” Sophia told her. “Don’t worry.” Tara went and was welcomed. That Christmas, 80 people packed Sophia’s apartment, singing and dancing in circles. Across the room, Sophia saw Tara, wearing red Christmas garland like a scarf and a smile stretched across her face. “Tara grew up very conservative – music was not even allowed in her home. But now she’s dancing, worshiping the Lord with us with music and songs.” In South Asia, Maryam and a local pastor baptize Tara, a new believer. IMB missionaries work alongside local believers and churches to fulfill the Great Commission. IMB Photo That spring, Tara was baptized.

Tara说:「我不再相信伊斯兰教了。 没有上帝的知晓,她没有任何人可以祈祷,这让她孤独. 她从朋友那里寻找佛教和印度教, 甚至和无神论者会面, “你们认识任何基督徒吗?” 索菲亚问。 你们告诉我吧! 他们读到耶稣的出生,Tara更渴望更多。 当她问起教堂时,索菲亚描述了他们大约40名信徒的聚会,其中许多来自穆斯林背景. Tara继续学习。 Sophia和Maryam每周在咖啡店、茶店、Sophia家相会, 找到她最亲近的朋友 他们通过"约翰福音"阅读. 11月一日在一家咖啡店里,他们到达了井上撒玛利亚女人的通道,索菲亚注意到塔拉正在哭泣. “塔拉,我看到你有眼泪,”索菲亚说。 " 让我们停下来吧。 让我们谈谈。 当天,塔拉祈祷接受基督. 不久后,她想参观教堂,虽然担心信徒会如何用头巾接见她. “他们会爱你,”索菲亚告诉她。 “别担心。 Tara去了,受到欢迎。 80人收拾了索菲亚的公寓, 在房间对面,索菲亚看见了塔拉,身穿红色的圣诞外衣,像围巾和微笑被伸到她脸上. " Tara长大后非常保守——她家甚至不允许音乐. 现在她正在跳舞,用音乐和歌曲与我们一起崇拜上帝。 在南亚,玛丽安和一位当地牧师为新信徒塔拉施洗. IMB的传教士与当地的信徒和教会一起工作,完成"大委员会". IMB 相片 当年春天,塔拉被洗礼.

title_zh: 神通过IMB在意大利的传教士保持忠诚
content: The eastern face of St. Peter's Basilica in the Vatican City in Rome, Italy, is famous for its central balcony from which popes give their papal addresses. Most people in Rome have at least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” IMB Photo In the city where Jason and Lizzy Davis serve, some steps have a lot of meaning. And the meaning is different for them than it is for the thousands who travel there to visit that site. “If you come to Rome, you can come to a place called the Holy Steps,” Jason said. “People go there, and they’ll crawl up on their knees and pray the rosary all the way up.” From the top of the steps, a mural depicting Jesus on the Cross looks down on those making the pilgrimage. For Jason and Lizzy, it’s a spiritual experience, a picture of a religion that asks people to earn their way to Jesus. “That’s really the opposite of what the gospel is. The gospel is Jesus saying, ‘No, you can’t do it . . . no matter how good you think you are,’” they said. Most people in Rome have at the very least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism, as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” Jason explained, “It’s where the Pope lives in the Vatican. It’s very much part of the religion and culture. It’s all intertwined here.” An ‘unavoidable’ call Jason and Lizzy are investing their lives as International Mission Board missionaries in Rome, Italy, to share the truth of the gospel. The Davises partner with national believers through a new church plant, and they’re seeking to plant more churches within the city. Lizzy said for her, the call to missions was unavoidable. “I grew up as a third culture kid, or a missionary kid. My parents were on the mission field, as were my grandparents, all with the International Mission Board.” Then her family moved to Virginia for her dad to work for IMB’s home office staff. As a middle schooler and high schooler, every time Lizzy heard about the need for the gospel to go forth, she felt a burden, a “burning” in her heart. She didn’t know what God would do with that, but she had a feeling she would see one day. Now, years later, she and Jason spend their time trying to find as many opportunities as they can to invite people into their home so they can share the hope of Jesus with them. That can mean Bible study or simply sharing a meal. ‘Completely lost’ Jason has been surprised by just how often people are willing to talk about faith. “You can get into spiritual conversations very quickly with people, especially if you’re just open and honest with them.” Lizzy shared that one of the easiest ways to do this is to be willing to let your day be interrupted. “That’s something I’ve seen Jason do firsthand in our neighborhood. He walks down the street, and everybody knows him because he stops and takes the time to ask them questions about their families, gets to know people, gets to know the newspaper stand guy and the guy at the fruit stand and the grocery store ladies.” She emphasized that caring about people is “what Christ would do.” The Davises, whose previous mission service prevents their photos from being published, live in a neighborhood of about 130,000 people. Their church of 15 people is the only evangelical congregation there. Lizzy said the area is “truly a lost, completely lost, dark neighborhood” with people who have never heard the gospel. Thousands more come to their area on a religious quest. The Davis family’s neighborhood is home to the Basilica Papale di San Paolo (the Papal Basilica of Saint Paul), one of the city’s four major basilicas. “So we get a lot of people coming on spiritual journeys, visiting our neighborhood, seeking some sort of spiritual experience. And oftentimes it’s just trying to earn their salvation,” she added. Jason described this environment as “a genuine need for people to actually hear the gospel and know that their sins can be forgiven and they can have an assurance of that.” IMB missionaries Jason and Liz

title_zh: 全球传教士合作伙伴通过IMB团队扩展福音工作
content: Rebeca Couto poses with her IMB teammates. Couto is a global missionary partner serving alongside IMB missionaries in Japan. IMB Photo Rebeca Couto poses with her violin. Couto is a professional violinist who is serving as a global missionary partner with the IMB in Japan. Doors have opened for her to use her skills with evangel ical Japanese musicians who perform. IMB Photo Rebeca Couto moved from one volcanic archipelago to another, leaving Portugal’s Azores islands to anchor her life in Japan. The percentage of evangelical Christians in the Azores and Japan is similar, with both populations under 1%. Couto is a fourth-generation Christian, a rarity on the small islands. She is one of few, if any, believers in the Azores with such a long spiritual lineage. This rich legacy shaped her and prepared her for ministry. “I’ve always understood the Great Commission as a call for all believers and all disciples of Christ to be missionaries, wherever they are, whatever they’re doing, and whatever God has equipped them with,” Couto said. Couto’s great-grandfather became a Christian through the witness of missionaries from the United Kingdom. Later, missionaries from the Foreign Mission Board, now the International Mission Board, started the first Baptist work in the Azores by planting an English-speaking church near an American military base. A Baptist Brazilian couple planted a Portuguese-speaking church, which became the congregation where Couto grew up and was commissioned as a missionary. Ministry has been passed down through the generations of her family. Couto’s father has pastored for 20 years, and both of her parents have been involved in ministry for most of their lives. Couto now serves in Japan as a global missionary partner, a missionary who is financially supported by a sending church or organization in their home country and serves with IMB teams. Close to 400 GMPs currently serve on IMB teams around the world. Language learning Couto is immersed in language study in Yokohama, Japan. She had a head start before she even arrived. After graduating from high school, Couto moved from the Azores to Lisbon to pursue a degree in music. She spent hours on public transportation and wanted a challenge to pass the time. She decided to study Japanese because she thought it sounded beautiful. At the time, she had no intention of becoming a missionary in the traditional sense. However, the more she learned about the language and the culture, her burden for the lost grew. She began researching Christianity in Japan. “I understood how bleak the scenario was, and how much the country needed Jesus. I struggled with that calling because the doors were closed, and it didn’t seem possible to come to Japan for a myriad of reasons,” Couto said. After finishing master’s degrees in music and violin performance, along with a seminary degree, Couto was considering pursuing a Ph.D. or returning to seminary when her seminary professors, IMB missionaries Jonathan and Bethany Sharp, contacted her about serving as a missionary in Japan. They introduced her to the GMP program and invited her to attend a missions immersion school they piloted . Rebeca Couto (far right) poses with her IMB teammates. Couto is a global missionary partner serving alongside IMB missionaries in Japan. IMB Photo Music to their ears As a professional violinist, Couto brought her violin to Japan, unsure of what opportunities existed, but she knew her call to the mission field somehow involved her gifting. “I see myself as having been called to serve through music. I never even conceived doing missions while excluding the violin entirely,” Couto said. She continued, “Music is such a universal way to connect with people, and it’s so intuitive to pair that with the gospel and with God’s message to people’s hearts.” While she knew the Lord would somehow open a door for her to use the violin for kingdom work, she was at peace with the possibility that, for a season, she may not be as

title_zh: IMB传教士使用家庭、咖啡馆、应用程序为西班牙的福音对话敞开大门
content: Men and women gather to discuss spiritual topics with Caleb and Carina Beaty, International Mission Board missionaries who serve in Madrid. IMB Photo Across Spain, people looking for connection and meaningful conversation turn to the internet to find groups where they can meet others. At a café by the river, Caleb and Carina Beaty engage in conversations about finding purpose, beauty and “what’s wrong with the world.” A website called Meetup allows people to search for groups to meet in person. The description of the Beatys’ group indicates that it discusses spiritual topics. People come expecting to talk about faith, so it’s not a surprise when they arrive. Caleb said he always has a list of questions that begin broadly and funnel into questions such as, “If there were a God …” or “What do you think Christians believe about that?” or “Why do you think religions have such different perspectives?” The Beatys’ goal in these conversations is to work toward deeper worldview questions within 45 minutes to an hour. Most of the people who attend their Meetup group are from Madrid, but they also have conversations with people from other countries. During one Meetup, Caleb and Carina shared how creation was perfect, but sin led to a world separated from the Father. God offers salvation through the death and resurrection of Jesus, they explained. “There are times we’re able to get to a clear gospel presentation with a group of people, and sometimes we’re doing pre-evangelism.” Caleb said. Some repeat attendees who have been attending for more than a year quickly jump to the heart of the discussion. “All right, Caleb, what’s the Bible say about suffering?” they’ll ask. Caleb and Carina then have the opportunity to share the Christian perspective. IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty and their children pose for a photo in a park in Madrid, Spain.  IMB Photo Spain has secularized rapidly since the 1990s, Caleb said. While many may think of it as a Catholic nation, many people do not know the basic tenets of Christianity. “We’ve got all the churches, we’ve got the cathedrals, and they do processions, but the average person on the street does not know anything about the gospel and does not know anything about Jesus,” Caleb said. Younger Spaniards are drawn to their group and are receptive to the gospel because they don’t have a spiritual foundation or know anyone who does. “There’s just this curiosity because, for a lot of them, they’ve never met someone who actually believes that God exists, and that changes your life,” Carina said. “I’ve had people completely shocked that we believe in God. ‘You really believe that God exists?’ They can’t wrap their mind around that.” During one Meetup, a man contrasted Protestant and Catholic beliefs by saying Protestants focus on Jesus’ suffering and Catholics on Mary’s grief. Caleb responded that evangelicals focus on the resurrection. When Caleb said Jesus rose from the dead, the man replied that he needed to look into that. Caleb said encounters like that reveal how little many Spaniards know about the gospel. Caleb noted the irony of the man’s sharing the Catholic perspective without truly understanding it. He is not the only person the Beatys have met who has missed the heart of the gospel. A friend of the Beatys told them she’d heard Jesus died, but she hadn’t heard he rose from the dead. A man reads a passage of Scripture during a Bible study hosted by IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty at their family’s apartment in Madrid, Spain. Five atheists began attending their Bible study after attending the couple’s Meetup group. IMB Photo The Beatys also host seasonal outreach events through the Meetup. Members from their church in Madrid have started attending the Meetup to learn how the Beatys lead discussions. Their group has become so popular, a waitlist has formed. Caleb and Carina host a small-group Bible study in their home. Five atheists who joined their Meetup now attend the Bible study.

summary_zh: 纳什维莱 — — 随着书籍在上个财政年度收尾,两个美南浸信会国家年度传教团的收据凸显出美南浸信会教堂对用福音传入世界的价值。 Lottie Moon Christmas Offering(LMCO)共提供2.125亿美元支持国际传教委员会(IMB)的传教士,Annie Armstrong Easter Offer Offering(AAEO)则提供7 360万美元支持北美传教委员会(NAMB)的教堂种植,同情心.
title_zh: AAEO、LMCO总计发出南方浸信会支持的信号，关注大使命
content: IMB Graphic NASHVILLE – As the books closed on the latest fiscal year, receipts for the two Southern Baptist national annual missions offerings underscored the value Southern Baptist churches place on reaching the world with the gospel. The Lottie Moon Christmas Offering® (LMCO) totaled $212.5 million to support International Mission Board (IMB) missionaries, and the Annie Armstrong Easter Offering® (AAEO) reached $73.6 million to support the North American Mission Board’s (NAMB) church planting, compassion ministry and other evangelistic efforts to reach North America. IMB President Paul Chitwood said he celebrates what God did in the 2025-26 season and what He is doing now to lead Southern Baptists toward historic generosity. “I thank God for Southern Baptists! With giving through the Lottie Moon offering at an all-time high, churches and individual givers continue to display a heart for the gospel to be proclaimed to every nation, all tribes, peoples and languages,” Chitwood said. The Annie total marked the second highest in NAMB’s history. The record Lottie Moon offering total surpassed last year’s total by more than $5 million and is the best offering in IMB history. “God is giving our generation unprecedented opportunity to send missionaries to the most unreached peoples and places,” Chitwood continued. “Though the challenges faced by our missionaries are enormous, the generosity of Southern Baptists ensures they have what they need to face those challenges and continue in the work while we hold the ropes with our support.” IMB missionary Landon Williams (center) walks with a Chilean pastor and a U.S. pastor on a remote island in Chile. Cooperation and generosity among Southern Baptists fuels the work to reach the uttermost parts of the world with the gospel. IMB Photo National goals for both offerings are set in partnership with Woman’s Missionary Union (WMU) each year. In response to the offering totals, Sandy Wisdom-Martin, executive director-treasurer of WMU, said: “As Southern Baptists, we are all in for His mission. When we give sacrificially, we prioritize the mission of God. Together our fervent prayers, our faithful generosity and our wholehearted obedience become channels for the gospel to reach our neighbors as well as the nations.” For the last 10 years, Southern Baptists have increasingly supported the Annie offering, setting records in seven of the last 10 years. title_zh: 俄克拉荷马州浸信会加入派遣教会实验室，以加强传教士支持
content: Staff members at First Baptist Church in Wagoner, Oklahoma, evaluate their church’s involvement with missions and missionary support. IMB Photo The chapel at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City turned into a science lab on Oct. 5-6. Microscopes, beakers and test tubes weren’t in the room, but this Sending Church Lab drew nearly 40 people representing 12 Oklahoma Baptist churches committed to send and care for international missionaries well. The Sending Church Lab, facilitated by the International Mission Board, brought pastors, church leaders and missionaries together for two days of discussion, self-assessment and planning centered on one question: What does it mean for a church to truly be a sending church? For Mike Wall, a global missions ministry partner of Oklahoma Baptists, the answer begins with churches reclaiming responsibility for the Great Commission. Wall first attended a Sending Church Lab last year in Tulsa with few expectations. He left convinced more churches needed the training. “When I went there, I thought, ‘You’ve got to do this in Oklahoma City,’” Wall said, “because of the content and how much our churches need something just like this.” After observing churches work through the exercises in the lab, Wall said he was encouraged by an emphasis on local church ownership in missions. “We can’t just send our people and say, ‘OK, now this is your job, IMB,’” he said. “We have to do our job in sending, preparing and training the best ‘sent ones’ so that when they get to the field, they can already hit the ground running.” Bryan Wooten, IMB senior church engagement specialist, leads a Sending Church Lab at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City. He is emphasizing the importance of sending churches assessing and equipping future IMB missionaries. IMB Photo Leading the lab was Bryan Wooten, IMB senior church engagement strategist, who developed the concept after seeing the need for stronger relationships between missionaries and local churches. “A Sending Church Lab is our attempt to raise up a host of IMB sending churches,” Wooten said, crediting the North American Mission Board for doing similar events and having successful results. The lab helps churches understand what Wooten calls the church engagement pathway: praying, cooperating, partnering and sending. While many churches faithfully pray, give and go, he said sending requires something more intentional. “Sending includes taking responsibility for an IMB missionary by providing ongoing encouragement, accountability and soul care throughout their term of service,” he explained. During the two-day event, participants gathered around whiteboards to evaluate their church’s missions practices, identify strengths and weaknesses and develop plans for improvement. “We don’t just need to deliver content,” Wooten said. “We need to invite churches to do some work on their own.” Rather than simply listening to presentations, attendees worked through practical questions about prayer, giving, short-term missions, missionary assessment and long-term care. Wooten said churches consistently tell him the greatest benefit is clarity. “They are thankful for clarity on what an IMB sending church is and what our roles and responsibilities are,” he said. For IMB missionaries Peter and Katie Weeks, that clarity is especially valuable. They participated in the lab alongside church leaders. Their real names have been changed to protect their work in Southeast Asia. “There’s no other place I’d rather be during these few days than here,” Peter said. Katie appreciated the interactive nature of the training. “I really appreciate the way they’re actually requiring information from the different churches and encouraging dialogue about how they can go through the steps,” she said. From a missionary perspective, she believes the lab addresses a common challenge. “It’s hard to know sometimes as churches how to be a good sending church and how to support missionaries,” she sa
content_zh: 俄克拉何马州瓦戈纳第一浸信会的工作人员评价了教会参与传教和传教活动的情况。 IMB 相片 俄克拉荷马城Constitute Road Baptist Church的小教堂于10月5-6日变成科学实验室. 但这个送信教会实验室吸引了近40人, 代表12个俄克拉何马浸会教会, 传教士实验室在国际传教委员会的协助下,召集牧师、教会领袖和传教士进行两天的讨论、自我评估和规划,其中心是一个问题: 教会真正成为送教之所意味着什么? 对于俄克拉何马浸信会的全球使命部合作伙伴迈克·沃尔来说,答案始于教会重新为大委员会负责。 去年沃尔在图尔萨参加了一个送教实验室, 他离开后确信更多的教会需要训练. “当我去那里时,我想,`你必须在俄克拉荷马城做这件事,'墙说,`因为内容和我们的教会需要这样的东西。 在观察了教堂通过实验室的演练工作后,沃尔说,他在任务中强调当地教会的所有权使他受到鼓舞. “我们不能只是派我们的人来说,“好吧,这是你的工作,IMB。” “我们必须在派遣、准备和训练最优秀的`派遣 ' 人员方面完成我们的工作,这样,当他们到达实地时,他们就已经可以奔跑地了。” Bryan Wooten,IMB高级教会订婚专家,在俄克拉荷马城的Constitution Road Baptist教堂领导一个送教实验室. 他强调派遣教会评估和装备未来的IMB传教士的重要性. IMB Photo Leading the lab是IMB高级教会接触策略师布莱恩·伍滕(Bryan Wooten),他在看到传教士与本地教会之间需要更牢固的关系后发展出这个概念. 伍腾说,“一个派遣教会实验室是我们努力培养许多派遣教会的IMB。 ”他赞扬北美传教委员会开展了类似的活动并取得了成功。 实验室帮助教会理解伍腾所谓的教会参与途径:祈祷,合作,合作和发送. 虽然许多教堂忠实地祈祷,奉献和去,但他说送去需要更有意图的东西. 他解释说,“最后包括负责一个IMB传教士,在整个任职期间提供持续的鼓励、问责和精神关怀。” 在为期两天的活动期间,与会者聚集在白板周围,评价其教会的任务做法,查明优缺点并制订改进计划。 」伍腾说: “我们需要邀请教会自己做一些工作。” 与会者不是简单地听取演讲,而是通过祷告、赠送、短期访问、传教士评估和长期照料等实际问题开展工作。 Wooten说,教会总是告诉他最大的好处是清晰. 他说,“他们感谢对派遣教会的咨监委的澄清,以及我们的作用和责任。” 对于IMB的传教士彼得和凯蒂·威克斯来说,这种清晰度特别有价值. 他们与教会领袖一起参加了实验室. 他们的真名被更改以保护自己在东南亚的工作. 彼得说,“在这几天里,我宁愿呆在这里。” 凯蒂对培训的互动性表示赞赏. 我非常欣赏他们要求不同教会提供信息的方式, 从传教士的角度来看,她认为实验室解决了共同的挑战. title_zh: 数字化之门为东南亚岛民打开福音之门
content: Just as young people today have become more comfortable with talking online than in person, the same is true for people in Southeast Asia. IMB missionaries are creating and publishing Jesus-focused ads, videos and other digital content to connect with the lost through the internet. IMB Photo Recently, an International Mission Board team in Southeast Asia asked a young woman if she had heard the story of Jesus. She replied that, yes, she had heard about Him through a video online! “Back in the day,” shared Amanda Clarkston, an IMB missionary who has served in Southeast Asia for 33 years, “when I first came on the field, you’d go somewhere and gather all the people together in the village to watch the JESUS film.” Now, face-to-face conversations about Christ on the Southeast Asian islands are harder to accomplish. While teams travel to these remote islands often, living in a sparsely populated, animistic background culture as a foreigner creates suspicion and make long-term ministry difficult. Furthermore, young people today have become more comfortable with talking online than they are in person, Clarkston said, which is true of the islanders as well. Attempting to have a spiritual conversation face-to-face has become “too much” for locals, Clarkston shared. So, how do you share the gospel with multiple people groups who are constantly online and less comfortable with in-person interactions? For these Southeast Asia teams, digital engagement — the use of social media platforms to share a message — has become a plausible and effective entry point. The social media agency We Are Social confirmed this, revealing that 82.4% of Southeast Asia’s population uses the internet. “No matter where they go, how far they go, how remote it is, people have phones,” Clarkston and her team realized, “And though sometimes they do have to climb up the highest peak to get reception, people do it.” Clarkston’s team has begun creating and publishing Jesus-focused ads, videos and other digital content in hopes of building bridges to the islanders through the internet. Viewers can click on the ad to message back and forth with a responder, a local believer or missionary who is available to pray, build relationships and answer spiritual questions. “It seems like locals are more open to watching those things in the privacy of their own cell phones,” Clarkston said. Clarkston intends to use digital engagement as a means for initial contact with people with animistic backgrounds, evangelism and, eventually, discipleship. She said that this new ministry has the potential to open doors with individuals across these islands who would normally never reach out on their own or respond to the gospel in person. “Maybe they’ll respond this way,” Clarkston said, “I know without a shadow of a doubt that God is calling people to Himself.” Now, more than ever, technology has a grip on society. Many spend hours each day mindlessly scrolling, searching for meaning, for happiness. And now, more than ever, there is an incredible opportunity to plant seeds across Southeast Asian islands through digital engagement. The IMB Southeast Asia team gives praise to the Lord that He has provided a creative way to reach the lost and plant seeds. Pray the people among the Southeast Asian islands would see these ads and engage with responders boldly, even though they may face persecution or harm because of it. Names were changed for security. Mikah Young is serving overseas with the IMB. The work of the IMB is sustained through faithful giving to the Cooperative Program and the Lottie Moon Christmas Offering ® . title_zh: IMB传教士在服务之旅中分享首尔的愿景
content: Ask most people what comes to mind when they think of South Korea, and they’ll likely mention K-pop, skincare, cutting-edge technology, or bustling city streets filled with young professionals. Hun and Eunjoo Sol see those things too. But after more than a decade serving as International Mission Board missionaries in Seoul, they also see something many visitors never notice. “Many people think that Korea is exciting and successful,” Hun said. “They think about the K-pop, the K-culture, K-technology, K-cosmetics. Yes, good things… But many Korean people are struggling right now.” The Sols, who were featured in the 2025 Week of Prayer for International Missions , continue to rely on the prayers of faithful Southern Baptists. Prayers sustain them and help to push back the darkness they confront in their home culture. Hun often describes that hidden struggle with a Korean word: han. There is no simple English translation. It speaks to a deep sorrow shaped by generations of war, division, loss, and the quiet resolve to endure. Hun sees it in the young adults he meets every week—people navigating loneliness and relentless expectations, quietly asking what their lives are for beneath a veneer of success. Han is heavy. For many young adults, that weight can feel unbearable. Suicide is one of the leading causes of death among teenagers and young adults in South Korean. Hun and Eunjoo see the effects of that reality every day, and it’s one reason they believe they have no time to waste. That understanding shaped the week of Serve Tour Seoul this summer. There were no construction sites, no paintbrushes, no tools or work gloves. Instead, the team stepped into ministries local churches had been faithfully building long before the volunteers arrived. In May, 27 volunteers from seven churches across the United States came alongside local churches already serving their communities in Seoul, Paju, and Gwangju. They taught English classes, ran children’s camps, walked neighborhoods in prayer, distributed food, and sat down with college students, one conversation at a time. For Nick Holst of Sandals Church in Riverside, California, the goal was simple enough to say in a sentence: “We came to meet people,” Holst said. “We want to hear their stories, and that leads to some very meaningful connections as you get past the surface into something deeper.” That’s where the week actually lived: past the surface and past the small talk, where the quiet weight of han is often carried without words. On college campuses, volunteers played games, asked questions and mostly just listened. Some conversations lasted a few minutes and ended there. Others kept going long past the point where either person expected them to. One morning, after asking his church back home to pray, Holst sat down with a university student named Intec. They talked about culture first, the way strangers do, and then the conversation turned somewhere neither of them planned. “I got to ask him, ‘What do Koreans believe?’” Holst recalled. Intec said he didn’t believe in God. Then he recited John 3:16 from memory, word for word, a verse he’d heard somewhere along the way and never forgotten. Before they parted, Holst asked if he could pray that God would keep drawing Intec toward Himself. “He said yes.” In a city where many conversations never move beyond the surface, the exchange was a reminder of why the team had come. Not to win an argument, but to listen, to ask questions, and to trust God with what happens next. The same pattern unfolded elsewhere, beginning in classrooms and ending on city streets. Jeremy Doyle, missions pastor at Valley Baptist Church in Bakersfield, California, watched an English conversation club grow from two students on its first night to eight by the second. Nobody advertised it as anything more than a place to practice English, but the room kept filling, and so did the conversations. The team’s work with students didn’t stop there. title_zh: IMB的Barger因任务创新而获得2026 Excelerate奖
content: Don Barger, left, IMB director of innovation and artificial intelligence, receives the Excelerate Award at the Missio Nexus Mission Leaders Conference in Orlando, Florida. The award recognizes individuals who demonstrate exceptional leadership and creativity in advancing missions through innovation. Photo provided Don Barger, director of innovation and artificial intelligence for the International Mission Board, received the 2026 Excelerate Award from Missio Nexus during the Mission Leaders Conference, Sept. 24 in Orlando, Florida. According to Missio Nexus, a network of mission-focused organizations and churches, the Excelerate Award recognizes individuals who demonstrate exceptional leadership and creativity in advancing missions through innovation. Barger has earned a reputation for identifying emerging technologies and applying them to ministry challenges, helping pioneer the use of artificial intelligence in global missions while promoting a biblically grounded approach to innovation. Barger said receiving the award was both surprising and encouraging. “I realized it was an affirmation not only of my work, but of the work our entire team has been doing,” he said. “It’s encouraging to see the IMB recognized as an organization willing to invest in innovation, think creatively and explore new ways to reach the nations.” Barger has served with the IMB for 29 years in a variety of roles. He was involved in church planting and led indigenous work in Mexico and Central America. Most of his work as a missionary focused on oral learners and Bible storying. Long before artificial intelligence became mainstream, Barger and his team began examining its potential for missions. IMB team members developed a framework to guide appropriate and inappropriate uses of AI in ministry settings. One principle that continues to shape that framework is Barger’s conviction that “souls should care for souls.” “We do not use AI for counseling or to replace human spiritual care,” Barger said. “Instead, we use AI to handle tasks that free people to spend more time ministering directly to people.” While much of his work centers on technology, Barger emphasizes that innovation extends far beyond technical advances. He defines innovation as a willingness to ask new questions and explore new approaches while remaining faithful to biblical truth. “Too often the response is, ‘That’s not how we’ve always done it,'” Barger said. “Innovation that advances the Great Commission begins by asking new questions and exploring new possibilities.” Barger noted that Christians have a long history of embracing new tools to support gospel ministry, from the printing press to broadcasting and healthcare advances. As artificial intelligence continues to generate discussion among ministry leaders, Barger encourages both optimism and discernment. He points to AI’s potential to improve communication, accelerate training and remove barriers that can hinder ministry efforts. At the same time, he cautions leaders to recognize the limitations of AI and ensure people remain responsible for ministry decisions and engagement. “Every tool throughout history has been capable of both good and evil,” Barger said. “The opportunity is to use AI for redemptive purposes.” Barger’s work includes developing faithbot.tools , a collection of AI tools designed for evangelical Christians. Throughout his career, he has advocated using technology not as an end in itself, but as a means of strengthening ministry and supporting relationships. Looking ahead, Barger hopes his greatest contribution will be encouraging future mission leaders to think creatively while remaining committed to God’s mission. “I hope mission leaders develop a mindset of curiosity,” he said. “Instead of simply accepting, ‘This is how we’ve always done it,’ I want them to ask, ‘How might we do this better?'” For Barger, innovation is ultimately about stewarding available tools in ways that help advance the Great Commission. summary: In a time of global challenge and opportunity, the Wycliffe Global Alliance is searching for its next Executive Director.

content: God’s Word transforms lives, strengthens churches and brings hope across generations. Bible translation is part of that story, as communities around the world encounter God’s Word in their own languages. Its future calls for leaders who listen deeply, build trust across cultures and empower others. Within this context, the Wycliffe Global Alliance is searching for its next Executive Director. Could this be your next calling? The Wycliffe Global Alliance is seeking its next Executive Director to serve a worldwide community of more than 100 organisations united in God’s mission through Bible translation. Th e opportunity : Bring our global community together around a shared vision, strengthen local leadership and help a diverse global movement respond to new opportunities with faith and wisdom. The challenge : Lead through change. Articulate a compelling shared vision, strengthen the support the Alliance offers its organisations, and engage support organisations and financial partners in advancing the work. This calls for leadership that honours local autonomy while strengthening global unity, trust, mutual accountability and financial sustainability. We are looking for a leader who brings: A deep commitment to Jesus Christ and a humble, prayerful approach to leadership. At least five years of senior leadership experience and a relevant master’s degree. Proven ability to lead across cultures, develop leaders and empower local churches. Strategic vision, significant fundraising experience and the ability to turn plans into meaningful outcomes. Emotional maturity, integrity and resilience through change. Feel called—or know someone who might be? Expressions of interest, or candidate recommendations, are welcomed confidentially by 30 November 2026 . More info: full profile and how to respond

summary: This project seeks to equip trainers who can contextualise and deliver OBT training within Latin America

title_zh: 威克里夫全球联盟传播研讨会–非洲地区
content: Communication staff at 18 Bible translation organizations across Africa need professional training to tell God’s stories well. In November 2026, a one-week workshop in Ruiru, Kenya will teach practical skills like writing, photography, design and video. Then, six months of follow-up support will continue to strengthen networks and create a collaborative culture of sharing God’s stories widely and effectively. Project Name: Africa Area Communication Capacity Building Workshop Implementing Organization: Wycliffe Global Alliance – Africa Area Contact: Phil Prior Director for Communication Wycliffe Global Alliance phil_prior@wycliffe.net Matthew Bore Project Funding Manager Wycliffe Global Alliance matthew_bore@wycliffe.net Start date: September 2026 End date: March 2027 Summary Across Africa, God is moving. Communities are receiving the Bible in their own language for the first time. Lives are being transformed. But too often, these stories never become known beyond the place where they happen. Why? Because not enough people are trained to recognise and report these stories to a wider audience. Among 18 Bible translation organisations across Africa, communication staff are doing their best—but without formal training in news writing, interviewing, photography, video and social media. Many also work in relative isolation without the chance to exchange ideas and collaborate on stories. The result: Amazing stories remain untold, and the people who could be praying, giving or getting involved never learn about the opportunities. This project changes that. For one week (2-6 November 2026) in Ruiru, Kenya, communication staff from those 18 Wycliffe Global Alliance organisations will come together — not just to sit in a classroom, but to actually create. Using smartphones and free tools, they will learn to capture the moments that matter: local communities and churches collaborating; a translation team’s challenges and creative solutions, groups engaging with Scripture, lives being transformed. Attendees also will build plans for how their organisations will keep telling these types of stories long after the workshop ends. Then, over the ensuing six months, this same group will keep coaching, encouraging, and learning from each other — turning 18 separate voices into one strong, unified story of what God is doing across Africa.
